questions.exp: 文中结尾说干净的表面不会写成文章，但能止住许多小泄漏，往往使学习更短也更有效。

junior.title: 👀 Reading the Instructions Twice Before You Start
junior.content:
Many mistakes in homework do not begin with a hard idea. They begin with a hurried first look at the instructions. A student sees the word “explain” and writes only a short answer, or sees “choose two” and answers all five, or skips a back page that holds half the marks. The habit of reading the instructions twice is a small brake that can save a long repair. The first reading is to see the whole task. The second is to notice the details that the hurry of starting often hides.

The second reading has a method. Underline the verbs: explain, compare, calculate, list, give an example. Circle the numbers: how many reasons, how many lines, how much time. Check whether there is a second part, a diagram, or a reminder about units. If the work is an exam paper, look at the mark next to each question so that you do not spend twenty minutes on a two-mark item. This is not wasted time. It is a map of the work you are about to do.

Teachers see this habit in the tidiness of answers. Students who read twice are less likely to miss a page or answer the wrong question number. At home, the same habit helps with project instructions and online forms. If a sentence is confusing, write a question in the margin before you guess. A wrong start can build a whole page of work that later has to be crossed out.

You can practise the habit for a week with every new exercise. Put a tiny mark at the top of the page after the second reading, so that your hand does not run ahead of your eyes. The mark is a promise: I know what is being asked. Study is not only knowing facts. It is also knowing the task, clearly, before you spend your best energy on it.
junior.translation:
作业里的许多错误，并不是从某个很难的想法开始的。它们开始于对说明的匆忙第一眼。学生看见“解释”却只写了很短的答案，或看见“选择两项”却答了全部五题，或跳过了占一半分数的背面。把说明读两遍的习惯，是一个可以省去长时间修补的小刹车。第一遍是为了看见整项任务。第二遍是为了注意到匆忙开始时常常被藏起来的细节。

第二遍阅读有一种方法。在动词下面画线：解释、比较、计算、列举、举一个例子。圈出数字：几个理由，几行，多少时间。检查是否有第二部分、一张图，或关于单位的提醒。如果是试卷，就看每道题旁边的分数，免得在一道两分的题上花二十分钟。这不是浪费时间。它是你即将要做的工作的一张地图。

老师会在答案的整齐里看见这种习惯。读两遍的学生不太会漏掉一页，或答错题号。在家里，同样的习惯也有助于项目说明和网上表格。如果一句话让人困惑，就在猜测之前在空白处写下问题。一个错误的开始，可能建成一整页后来又得划掉的工作。

你可以在一周里对每一道新练习练习这个习惯。在第二遍阅读之后，在页顶做一个小小的记号，好让你的手不跑到眼睛前面。这个记号是一个承诺：我知道正在被问的是什么。学习不仅仅是知道事实。它也是在把最好的精力花上去之前，先清楚地知道任务。

questions.q: 1. Where do many homework mistakes begin, according to the passage?
options: With a hurried first look at the instructions
With a hard idea that no one can learn
With reading the instructions twice
With a mark at the top of the page
questions.exp: 文中开篇指出许多错误开始于对说明的匆忙第一眼。

questions.q: 2. What is the second reading meant to catch?
options: Only the title of the textbook
A reason to skip the back page
A way to spend twenty minutes on every two-mark item
The details that the hurry of starting often hides, such as verbs, numbers and extra parts
questions.exp: 文中说第二遍是为了注意匆忙开始时被藏起的细节，并举例动词、数字、第二部分等。

questions.q: 3. Why should you look at the marks next to exam questions?
options: Because marks are only decoration
So that you can answer the wrong question number
So that you do not spend too long on a question that is worth very little
Because teachers dislike tidy answers
questions.exp: 文中建议看每道题旁边的分数，免得在两分的题上花二十分钟。

questions.q: 4. What does the tiny mark after the second reading mean?
options: That your hand should run ahead of your eyes
A promise that you know what is being asked before you spend your best energy
That the task is too confusing to begin
That facts matter and the task does not
questions.exp: 文中说页顶的小记号是一个承诺：我知道正在被问的是什么。

junior.title: 🕸️ Making a Simple Mind Map After a Lesson
junior.content:
A lesson can feel clear in the classroom and foggy an hour later. One useful method is to make a simple mind map while the ideas are still close. Write the topic in the centre of a page, then draw a few branches for the main parts: causes, examples, steps, or new words. On each branch, add only short phrases, not long sentences. The map is a picture of how the ideas connect, and making it forces you to decide what is important.

The method works because it is active. Copying the board word for word can keep the hand busy and the mind sleepy. Choosing a branch, however, is already a kind of thinking. If you cannot find a place for a fact, you may not yet understand it, and that is useful information. You can then check the book or ask a question the next day. A messy first map is fine. You can redraw a cleaner one later, which is also a review.

Mind maps are not only for science. A history lesson can branch into people, places and results. A language lesson can branch into grammar, examples and exceptions. A story can branch into characters, problems and endings. Use colours if they help you see the groups, but do not let decoration steal the time. Five to ten minutes after class is often enough for a first version.

Students can keep these maps in one folder and look at them before a test, covering a branch and trying to recall it. The page will remind you of the shape of the topic, not only of a single sentence. A simple mind map will not replace practice questions, but it can make that practice faster, because you already know where each idea lives.
Keep the first maps, even the messy ones. They show how your thinking has changed from week to week, and that record can encourage you when a later lesson feels heavy.
junior.translation:
一堂课可能在教室里显得清楚，一小时后却变得模糊。一个有用的方法，是趁想法还近的时候做一个简单的思维导图。把主题写在一页的中心，然后画出几条分支，表示主要部分：原因、例子、步骤，或新词。在每条分支上只加短语，不要加长句子。这张图是想法如何连接的一幅图画，而做它会迫使你决定什么是重要的。

这种方法之所以有效，是因为它是主动的。逐字抄黑板可能让手很忙，心却昏昏欲睡。然而，选择一条分支已经是一种思考。如果你不能给一个事实找到位置，你也许还没有理解它，而这是有用的信息。然后你可以查书，或在第二天问一个问题。第一张凌乱的图没有关系。你可以稍后重画一张更干净的，那也是一种复习。

思维导图不仅仅用于科学。一堂历史课可以分成人物、地点和结果。一堂语言课可以分成语法、例子和例外。一个故事可以分成人物、问题和结局。如果颜色能帮助你看见分组，就使用颜色，但不要让装饰偷走时间。课后五到十分钟，常常就足够做出第一版。

学生可以把这些图放在一个文件夹里，并在考试前看着它们，盖住一条分支并试着回忆。这一页会提醒你主题的形状，而不仅仅是单独一句话。简单的思维导图不会代替练习题，但它可以使练习更快，因为你已经知道每个想法住在哪里。
即使是凌乱的第一批图也请留下。它们会显示你的思考如何一周周变化，而当后面的课显得沉重时，这份记录可以鼓励你。

questions.q: 1. What is the first step of a simple mind map, according to the passage?
options: Write long sentences on every line at once
Write the topic in the centre and draw branches for the main parts with short phrases
Copy the board word for word without choosing
Let decoration use all of the ten minutes
questions.exp: 文中说明把主题写在中心，再为主要部分画出分支，并只加短语。

questions.q: 2. Why is making the map an active method?
options: Because choosing a branch forces you to decide what is important, and a fact with no place may be something you do not yet understand
Because the hand stays busy and the mind can sleep
Because messy maps are never useful
Because it replaces all practice questions
questions.exp: 文中对比抄写与选择分支：选择已经是思考，找不到位置可能说明还没理解。

questions.q: 3. How can mind maps be used in subjects other than science?
options: They are only for science and never for stories
They must always avoid people, places and examples
They cannot be redrawn as a review
History, language and stories can all be divided into clear branches
questions.exp: 文中举例历史分成人物地点结果，语言分成语法例子例外，故事分成人物问题和结局。

questions.q: 4. How can students use the maps before a test?
options: Throw the folder away and reread only one sentence
Decorate the page instead of recalling
Look at the maps, cover a branch and try to recall it, so the shape of the topic stays clear
Avoid practice questions forever
questions.exp: 文中建议考前看这些图，盖住分支试着回忆，以记住主题的形状。

junior.title: 🗣️ Teaching a Topic to a Family Member to Check Your Understanding
junior.content:
One of the most honest tests of understanding is this: can you teach the topic to someone who did not sit in the class? After a lesson, try to explain the main idea to a parent, a sibling, or even a stuffed animal that you pretend is listening. Use ordinary words first, then add the new terms. If you get stuck, you have found the exact edge of what you know. That edge is more useful than a page of notes you can only recognise, but cannot say aloud.

The method is simple, and it can be short. Choose five minutes, stand up, and speak as if you were helping a younger student. Begin with the question the lesson tried to answer. Then give one example, and one warning about a common mistake. Invite a real listener to ask a question. If they ask something you cannot answer, write it down and look it up later. Teaching is not a performance of being perfect. It is a way of making the gaps visible.

Some students feel shy at home. You can close the door and teach the wall, or record a voice note and listen once. The point is to retrieve the idea without looking at the book for the first minute. Then open the book and correct what you missed. This two-step pattern — speak, then check — turns the evening into a small classroom you can carry anywhere.

Families who make room for this habit give a great gift, even if they do not know the subject. A patient audience is enough. Students who practise teaching often remember more in exams, because they have already walked through the idea in their own sentences. To teach is to learn twice: once in class, and once in the voice you use at home.
junior.translation:
检验理解最诚实的测试之一是这个：你能否把这个主题教给一个没有坐在教室里的人？课后，试着把主要意思解释给父母、兄弟姐妹，甚至一个你假装在听的毛绒玩具。先用平常的词，再加上那些新术语。如果你卡住了，你就找到了自己所知的精确边缘。那条边缘，比一页你只能认出、却不能说出来的笔记更有用。

这种方法很简单，也可以很短。选择五分钟，站起来，像在帮助一个更小的学生那样说话。从这堂课试图回答的问题开始。然后给一个例子，以及关于一个常见错误的一句提醒。请一位真正的听者问一个问题。如果他们问了你不能回答的事，就写下来，稍后再去查。教不是一场关于完美的表演。它是一种让缺口变得可见的方式。

有些学生在家里会害羞。你可以关上门教墙壁，或录一段语音再听一遍。重点是在第一分钟不看书的情况下提取那个想法。然后打开书，纠正你错过的部分。这种两步的模式——先说，再检查——会把夜晚变成一间你可以带到任何地方的小小教室。

为这种习惯留出空间的家庭，即使并不懂这个科目，也给出了一份很大的礼物。一位有耐心的听众就足够了。练习教的学生常常在考试里记得更多，因为他们已经用自己的句子走过这个想法。教就是学习两次：一次在课堂上，一次在你在家里使用的声音里。

options: Because notes you can only recognise are always enough
Because a stuffed animal can mark the exam
Because a stuck moment shows the exact edge of what you know
Because you must never use ordinary words
questions.exp: 文中说如果卡住了，就找到了自己所知的精确边缘，这比只能认出的笔记更有用。

questions.q: 2. What can a short five-minute explanation include?
options: Only a performance of being perfect
The question the lesson tried to answer, one example, and a warning about a common mistake
A promise never to write down a listener’s question
A rule that families must know the subject already
questions.exp: 文中建议从课题问题开始，给一个例子和一句关于常见错误的提醒。

questions.q: 3. What should you do in the first minute of this method?
options: Retrieve the idea without looking at the book, then check and correct
Keep the book open and read it aloud only
Avoid speaking if you feel shy, and stop the habit
Skip the voice note and never listen back

questions.q: 4. Why do students who practise teaching often remember more in exams?
options: Because a patient audience takes the exam for them

Because they never look anything up later
Because they have already walked through the idea in their own sentences
questions.exp: 文中说他们常常记得更多，因为已经用自己的句子走过这个想法；教就是学习两次。

junior.title: 🪜 Breaking a Big Assignment Into Small, Clear Steps
junior.content:
A big assignment can look like a wall: a long report, a poster, a presentation, or a set of exercises that fills the weekend. If you stare at the whole wall, you may feel tired before you begin, and then you may delay until the last night. A better method is to break the work into small, clear steps that you can finish one at a time. The wall becomes a staircase. Each step is ordinary; together they climb.

Start by listing the parts on paper. For a report, the parts might be: choose a question, find two sources, write a plan, draft one section, check the facts, and make a neat copy. Put a realistic time next to each part, and put the first step on today’s list, not the whole report. When a step is finished, tick it. The tick is not childish. It is a signal to your mind that movement is happening, which makes the next step easier to start.

If a step still feels too large, break it again. “Find two sources” can become “search for twenty minutes” and “write the titles down.” A presentation can be divided into a script, a visual, and a rehearsal of the first minute only. The method is kind to tired days, because there is almost always a step small enough to do. It is also honest: you see early if the plan will not fit the time, and you can ask for help before the last night.

Students who use this habit often argue less with themselves. The question is no longer “How can I ever finish this?” It becomes “What is the next small step?” Teachers like work that arrives in time and in order, and you will like the calmer weekend. A big assignment is rarely one heroic evening. It is a series of ordinary steps, begun soon enough.
junior.translation:
一份大作业可能看起来像一堵墙：一篇长报告，一张海报，一次展示，或一套占满周末的练习。如果你盯着整堵墙，也许还没开始就觉得累，然后就会拖延到最后一晚。一个更好的方法，是把工作拆成你可以一次完成一个的、小而清楚的步骤。墙变成了楼梯。每一步都平常；合在一起，它们会向上爬。

先在纸上列出各个部分。对一篇报告来说，这些部分可能是：选择一个问题，找到两个来源，写一个计划，起草一节，核对事实，再抄写工整。在每个部分旁边写上现实的时间，并把第一步放进今天的清单，而不是整篇报告。当一步完成时，就打勾。这个勾不是幼稚。它是给头脑的一个信号：正在发生移动，而这会使下一步更容易开始。

如果某一步仍然显得太大，就再拆一次。“找到两个来源”可以变成“搜索二十分钟”和“把标题写下来。”一次展示可以分成讲稿、视觉材料，以及只排练第一分钟。这种方法对疲惫的日子很温和，因为几乎总有一步小到可以完成。它也很诚实：你会及早看见计划是否挤不进时间，并可以在最后一晚之前请求帮助。

使用这种习惯的学生常常少和自己争论。问题不再是“我怎么可能做完这个？”它变成“下一步小小的步骤是什么？”老师喜欢按时、按顺序到来的工作，你也会喜欢更平静的周末。一份大作业很少是一个英雄式的夜晚。它是一系列够早开始的平常步骤。

questions.q: 1. Why can a big assignment feel like a wall?
options: Because small steps are always impossible
Because teachers dislike work that arrives in order
Because a tick is childish and must be avoided
Because staring at the whole piece may make you tired and lead you to delay
questions.exp: 文中说盯着整堵墙可能还没开始就累，然后拖延到最后一晚。

questions.q: 2. What should you put on today’s list, according to the passage?
options: The entire report and nothing else
Only the neat copy, with no plan
The first small step, not the whole assignment
A heroic evening with no breaks
questions.exp: 文中建议把第一步放进今天的清单，而不是整篇报告。

questions.q: 3. What should you do if a step still feels too large?
options: Give up until the last night
Break it again into even smaller actions, such as a twenty-minute search
Hide the problem so that no one can help
Delete the realistic times from the plan
questions.exp: 文中举例把“找到两个来源”再拆成搜索二十分钟和写下标题。

questions.q: 4. How does this method change the question you ask yourself?
options: From ‘How can I ever finish this?’ to ‘What is the next small step?’
From a staircase back into a wall
From asking for help early to waiting until it is too late
From ordinary steps to one night of panic only
questions.exp: 文中说问题不再是如何做完整件，而变成下一步小小的步骤是什么。

junior.title: 🌱 Trying Something You Are Not Good at Yet
junior.content:
It is comfortable to stay with skills that already make you look able. A new sport, a new instrument, or a subject that feels clumsy at first can threaten that picture. Many students step back, not because they cannot learn, but because they do not like the feeling of being a beginner. Growth often begins exactly there: in the decision to try something you are not good at yet, and to stay long enough for the first awkward week to pass.

Being a beginner is not a verdict. It is a temporary address. Everyone who is now fluent in a language, or steady on a bicycle, once looked unsteady. The difference is not a secret talent that arrives complete. The difference is a period of practice that was allowed to be ugly. If you can laugh, a little, at a messy first attempt, you will have more courage for the second.

Choose a small, safe start. Ask for a beginner’s group, a short lesson, or a friend who remembers being new. Set a modest goal for two weeks: attend, try, and write down one thing that improved, even if it is tiny. Do not compare your first day with someone else’s third year. Compare it with your own yesterday. That comparison is fair, and it keeps the fire from going out.

People who inspire us are often described as naturally gifted, but their stories usually include a long chapter of not-yet. Students who dare to enter that chapter discover a wider self: not only the person who already scores well, but the person who can learn again. The prize is not immediate excellence. The prize is a character that is willing to begin.
If the first week feels long, remember that discomfort is a sign you have left the old, comfortable skill for a while. Stay kindly, practise a little each day, and let the new skill have time to arrive.
junior.translation:
停留在那些已经让你看起来能干的技能上，是舒服的。一项新的运动，一种新的乐器，或一门起初显得笨拙的功课，都可能威胁那幅图画。许多学生会退回去，不是因为他们不能学，而是因为他们不喜欢作为一个初学者的感觉。成长常常恰好从那里开始：从决定去尝试一件你还不好的事情，并停留得足够久，好让别扭的第一周过去。

作为初学者并不是一份判决。它是一个暂时的地址。每一个现在能流利说一种语言、或在自行车上站得稳的人，都曾经看起来不稳。差别不是一种完整到来的秘密天赋。差别是一段被允许难看的练习时期。如果你能对一次凌乱的第一次尝试微笑一点点，你就会有更多勇气去进行第二次。

选择一个小而安全的开始。请求一个初学者小组，一节短课，或一位记得自己也曾是新手的朋友。为两周设定一个谦逊的目标：参加，尝试，并写下一件哪怕很小的进步。不要把你的第一天和别人的第三年比较。把它和你自己的昨天比较。那种比较是公平的，它也能让火不熄灭。

激励我们的人常常被说成天生有天赋，但他们的故事里通常有很长一章叫做“还没有”。敢于走进那一章的学生，会发现一个更宽的自己：不仅仅是已经考得好的那个人，还有那个能够再一次学习的人。奖品不是立刻的卓越。奖品是一种愿意开始的品格。
如果第一周显得很长，请记得那种不适是一个信号：你暂时离开了旧的、舒服的技能。温柔地留下来，每天稍加练习，让新的技能有时间到来。

options: Because they do not like the feeling of being a beginner
Because they cannot learn anything new
Because being a beginner is a final verdict
Because practice is never allowed to be ugly
questions.exp: 文中说许多人退回，不是因为不能学，而是不喜欢作为初学者的感觉。

questions.q: 2. How does the writer describe being a beginner?
options: As a secret talent that arrives complete
As a reason to compare your first day with someone’s third year
As a fire that must go out
As a temporary address, not a verdict
questions.exp: 文中说作为初学者不是判决，而是一个暂时的地址。

questions.q: 3. What modest goal is suggested for the first two weeks?
options: Become excellent immediately and never write anything down
Join only if you already look able
Attend, try, and note one tiny improvement, comparing only with your own yesterday
Avoid beginner’s groups and short lessons
questions.exp: 文中建议两周的目标是参加、尝试，并写下一点点进步，只和自己的昨天比较。

questions.q: 4. What prize does the passage name at the end?
options: Immediate excellence in every subject
A character that is willing to begin, and a wider self that can learn again
A story with no chapter of not-yet
A comfortable decision to stay only with old skills

junior.title: 🙋 Asking for Help Is a Kind of Bravery
junior.content:
Some students think that asking for help is a confession of weakness. They sit with a problem they do not understand, hoping it will melt, or they copy a finished page in order to look able. In fact, a clear request for help is often a kind of bravery. It means you have noticed the gap, you still care about learning, and you are willing to be seen as unfinished. That courage is part of growing up, not a step away from it.

A good request is specific. “I do not understand this whole chapter” is a start, but “I can do the first two steps, and I get lost when the fraction appears” gives the helper a place to stand. Choose a suitable person: a teacher in office time, a classmate who is patient, a family member who can listen. Ask at a time when they can actually answer, not in the last ten seconds of a break. Then try the next example yourself, so that the help becomes a skill you own.

It also takes bravery to accept the answer you hoped not to hear: “You need more practice,” or “Let us start from an earlier page.” Growth is rarely a straight, proud line. People you admire have asked questions too, often more questions than students who are busy hiding. If someone laughs at a sincere question, the laugh says more about them than about you. Keep asking, and look for rooms where questions are welcome.

Students who build this habit waste less time in silent confusion. They also become kinder helpers later, because they remember the feeling of being stuck. Bravery is not only standing on a stage. Sometimes it is raising a hand in a quiet classroom, and trusting that a better understanding is worth a moment of discomfort.
junior.translation:
有些学生认为请求帮助是在承认软弱。他们坐在一道自己并不理解的题前，希望它会自行融化，或者抄写一页完成的作业来让自己看起来能干。事实上，一次清楚的求助常常是一种勇敢。它意味着你已经注意到缺口，你仍然在乎学习，并且愿意被看见自己尚未完成。那种勇气是长大的一部分，而不是远离长大的一步。

一个好的请求是具体的。“我整章都不懂”是一个开始，但“前两步我会，分数出现时我就迷路了”能给帮助者一个站立的位置。选择合适的人：办公时间里的老师，一位有耐心的同学，一位能够倾听的家人。在他们真正能够回答的时候问，而不是在课间最后十秒。然后再自己试下一道例题，好让帮助变成你自己拥有的技能。

接受你不希望听到的回答，也需要勇气：“你需要更多练习，”或“让我们从更前面的一页开始。”成长很少是一条笔直而骄傲的线。你钦佩的人也问过问题，常常比忙于隐藏的学生问得更多。如果有人嘲笑一个真诚的问题，那笑声关于他们自己，多于关于你。继续问，并寻找欢迎问题的房间。

养成这种习惯的学生，会在沉默的困惑里少浪费时间。他们后来也会成为更善意的帮助者，因为他们记得卡住的感觉。勇敢不仅仅是站在舞台上。有时它是在一间安静的教室里举起一只手，并相信更好的理解值得片刻的不适。

questions.q: 2. What makes a good request more useful?
options: Making it specific, such as naming the step where you get lost
Keeping it vague so that no one can stand anywhere
