questions.q: 2. How can families make the habit fair?
options: By agreeing on a place for devices and on exceptions such as a family call, an oven timer, or an emergency
By giving children a rule that adults do not follow
By hating every kind of technology
By keeping every phone on the table in loud mode
questions.exp: 文中建议用篮子或架子放置设备，并商定例外；若只有孩子被要求而大人滑动屏幕，会显得不公平。

questions.q: 3. What practical gains does a meal without a screen bring?
options: Guests must compete with a glowing rectangle
One-word answers become the only kind of talk
Study and work should continue on the phone at the table
Food may taste more distinct, conversation can grow, people may chew more slowly, and eyes can rest
questions.exp: 文中列举味道更分明、对话更展开、嚼得更慢，以及眼睛得到休息，客人也更受欢迎。

questions.q: 4. What should a student do if a lunchtime message is urgent?
options: Watch a short video instead of talking with a classmate
Keep the phone out for the whole lunch even when it is not needed
Step aside, answer, and return, rather than leaving the phone on the table all through the meal
Give technology no time and no place in daily life
questions.exp: 文中建议紧急消息可以走到一边回答再回来，技能在于给科技一个时间和地点。

junior.title: ▦ How a Small Code Helps a Ticket or a Package Find Its Way
junior.content:
On a ticket, a bottle, or a delivery box you will often see a square pattern or a set of black lines. It looks like decoration, but it is a language for machines. A scanner reads the code in a second and learns a price, a seat number, a website, or a place in a huge warehouse. This quiet invention has changed daily life in shops, stations and post offices. Work that once needed a long typed list can now happen with a beep, and fewer mistakes are made when tired eyes have to copy a long number.

The idea is simple even if the maths behind it is not. The pattern stores information in a form that a camera or a laser can see clearly, including extra marks that help the machine notice an error. That is why a slightly wrinkled ticket can still be read, and why a shop can update a price in the computer without sticking a new label on every shelf at the same moment. For a student, the same kind of code may open a worksheet, mark attendance, or link a library book to your name.

Useful tools still need care. A code on a poster in a strange street should not be scanned without thinking, because it may lead to an unhelpful or unsafe page. A payment code should be checked with a trusted adult if you are unsure. Personal tickets are not pictures to share with the whole class, because they may hold a seat or a journey that belongs only to you. Technology is handy, but it is not a substitute for a careful pause.

Next time you hear the beep at a checkout or at a gate, you can picture a tiny message travelling from the pattern to a computer, and then to a person who needs the fact. Daily life is full of these invisible helpers. Understanding them a little makes the city less magical and more readable — a useful feeling when you travel, shop, or send a package of your own.
junior.translation:
在一张票、一个瓶子或一个快递盒上，你常常会看见一个方形图案，或一组黑线。它看起来像装饰，其实是给机器的语言。扫描器在一秒钟里读出这个码，并得知一个价格、一个座位号、一个网页，或一个巨大仓库里的位置。这项安静的发明已经改变了商店、车站和邮局里的日常生活。曾经需要一份长长的打字清单的工作，现在一声蜂鸣就可以完成，而当疲倦的眼睛必须抄写一长串数字时，错误也会更少。

这个想法是简单的，即使它背后的数学并不简单。图案把信息储存在相机或激光能够清楚看见的形式里，也包括帮助机器发现错误的额外标记。这就是为什么一张稍微皱了的票仍然可以被读出，以及为什么商店可以在电脑里更新价格，而不必在同一时刻给每一个架子贴上新标签。对学生来说，同一种码可以打开一份练习、记录出勤，或把一本图书馆的书连接到你的名字。

有用的工具仍然需要小心。奇怪街道上海报里的码，不应当不经思考就扫描，因为它可能通向一个无益或不安全的页面。如果你不确定，支付码应当和一位可信的成年人一起核对。个人的票不是可以分享给全班看的图片，因为它们可能带着只属于你的座位或旅程。科技很方便，但它不能代替一次小心的停顿。

下一次你在收银台或门口听见那一声蜂鸣时，你可以想象一条小小的消息从图案走到电脑，再走到一个需要这个事实的人那里。日常生活充满了这些看不见的帮手。稍微理解它们，会让城市少一些神奇、多一些可读——当你旅行、购物，或寄出属于你自己的包裹时，这是一种有用的感觉。

questions.q: 1. What can a scanner learn from the small code on a ticket or a box?
options: Only a decoration with no meaning
A long typed list that must be copied by tired eyes
A price, a seat number, a website, or a place in a warehouse, in a second
A rule that shops can never update a price
questions.exp: 文中说扫描器可在一秒内得知价格、座位号、网页或仓库位置。

questions.q: 2. Why can a slightly wrinkled ticket still be read?
options: Because cameras and lasers can never see the pattern clearly
Because the pattern includes extra marks that help a machine notice an error
Because information cannot be stored in a visible form
Because library books cannot be linked to a name
questions.exp: 文中说明图案以机器可看清的形式储存信息，并有帮助发现错误的额外标记。

questions.q: 3. When should you be careful about scanning a code?
options: A code on a strange poster may be unsafe, a payment code may need a trusted adult, and a personal ticket should not be shared with the whole class
Every poster in a strange street is always safe
Technology can replace every careful pause
Personal tickets should be posted for everyone to copy
questions.exp: 文中提醒陌生海报上的码可能不安全，支付码应与可信成年人核对，个人票不宜分享。

questions.q: 4. What does the writer want you to picture when you hear the beep?
options: A city that must remain magical and unreadable
A package that can never find its way
A checkout with no invisible helpers at all
A tiny message travelling from the pattern to a computer, and then to a person who needs the fact
questions.exp: 文中建议想象一条小消息从图案到电脑再到需要这个事实的人，从而让城市更可读。

junior.title: 🎧 Using Headphones Kindly in a Shared Space
junior.content:
Headphones are one of the most common tools of modern life. They let you listen to a lesson, a song, or a story without filling the whole room. Used well, they are a kind invention: a student can review English on a bus, and a family member can rest in the same room. Used without care, they become a wall. A volume that leaks into the quiet carriage, a person who cannot hear a warning, or a conversation that has to be shouted across a table can turn a helpful tool into a problem for everyone nearby.

Kind use begins with volume and awareness. If a person beside you can sing your song, the sound is too loud, for their ears and for yours. Look up when you move, so that you notice a request, a bicycle, or a door. In class, take the headphones off when a teacher or a classmate speaks to you; leaving them on, even with the sound down, can look like a closed door. At night, over-ear cushions may be gentler for a brother or sister who is trying to sleep than a leaky pair of buds.

There is also a social question. Hours spent inside a private soundtrack can make a shared lunch feel distant. It is polite, sometimes, to take the headphones off and join the room, especially with guests or with a friend who has been waiting to talk. Technology should not become a permanent hiding place. Parents and students can agree on places where ears stay open: the dinner table, a crossing, and the first minutes after someone comes home.

You can keep a light bag or hook for the headphones so that they are not left on a chair for someone to sit on, and you can keep the volume at a level you could live with for a long walk. Daily life with technology is full of these small courtesies. A pair of headphones can protect a quiet space or disturb it. The difference is rarely the machine. It is the habit of remembering that other people are still in the room.
junior.translation:
耳机是现代生活里最常见的工具之一。它们让你可以听一课、一首歌或一个故事，而不必把整个房间填满。用得好，它们是一种善意的发明：学生可以在公共汽车上复习英语，一位家人可以在同一间房里休息。用得不小心，它们就会变成一堵墙。漏进安静车厢的音量，一个听不见警告的人，或一次必须隔着桌子喊过去的对话，都能把一件有用的工具变成附近所有人的问题。

善意的使用从音量和觉察开始。如果旁边的人能够唱出你的歌，声音就太响了，对他们的耳朵是如此，对你的也是如此。走动时抬起头，好让你注意到请求、一辆自行车或一扇门。在课堂上，当老师或同学对你说话时，把耳机取下；即使音量已经调低，仍戴着它，看起来也会像一扇关着的门。夜里，对于一个正在设法睡觉的兄弟姐妹来说，包耳的垫子可能比一副漏音的耳塞更温和。

这里也有一个社交问题。许多小时留在一条私人的配乐里，会让一顿共享的午餐显得遥远。有时，取下耳机并加入这个房间，是礼貌的，尤其是有客人时，或有一位一直等着说话的朋友时。科技不应当变成一个永久的躲藏处。父母和学生可以商定一些耳朵保持敞开的地方：餐桌，路口，以及有人回家后的最初几分钟。

你可以把耳机放在一个轻便的袋子或钩子上，免得它们被留在椅子上让人坐下，也可以把音量保持在你能够带着它走很长一段路的水平上。和科技一起的日常生活，充满了这些小小的礼貌。一副耳机可以保护一个安静的空间，也可以打扰它。差别很少在机器上。它在于记得其他人仍然在这个房间里的习惯。

questions.q: 1. When can headphones turn from a kind invention into a problem?
options: When a student reviews English on a bus without filling the room
When a family member can rest in the same room
When the tool never becomes a wall
When the volume leaks, a person cannot hear a warning, or a conversation has to be shouted across a table
questions.exp: 文中说漏音、听不见警告、或必须隔桌喊话时，有用的工具会变成附近所有人的问题。

questions.q: 2. What is a sign that the volume is too loud?
options: The sound never reaches anyone else
Over-ear cushions are always worse at night than leaky buds
A person beside you can sing your song
You always look up when you move
questions.exp: 文中说如果旁边的人能唱出你的歌，声音就太响了，对双方的耳朵都是如此。

questions.q: 3. Why should headphones come off when a teacher or classmate speaks to you?
options: Because class is a place where ears should never be open
Because leaving them on can look like a closed door, even if the sound is down
Because technology should be a permanent hiding place
Because guests prefer a distant lunch with a private soundtrack
questions.exp: 文中指出即使音量已调低，仍戴着耳机看起来也像一扇关着的门。

questions.q: 4. What places does the passage suggest for keeping ears open?
options: The dinner table, a crossing, and the first minutes after someone comes home
Only a private party on a chair
Any place where other people are forgotten
A long walk with the highest possible volume
questions.exp: 文中建议约定餐桌、路口，以及有人回家后的最初几分钟里耳朵保持敞开。

junior.title: 🏞️ Protecting a Small River or Pond Near Home
junior.content:
People often picture nature protection as a faraway forest. Many students, however, live near a small river, a canal, or a pond in a park. That water is a home for fish, insects, birds and plants, and it is also part of the town’s health. If rubbish is thrown in, if oil is poured down a drain, or if the banks are trampled bare, the water can turn cloudy and the living things can leave. Protecting a nearby pond is a local kind of nature care, small enough to see, and important enough to matter.

Care begins with what we do not put in the water. Plastic bags, bottles and food waste do not disappear; they float, sink, or break into pieces that animals may swallow. Soap and paint should not be tipped into a storm drain that may lead to the stream. If a class visits, they can stay on the path so that the mud of the bank, which holds roots and nests, is not destroyed in one excited afternoon. Looking is a form of protection when looking is gentle.

A community can do more together. Volunteers can pick up litter on a weekend, plant reeds where the bank is weak, and report a leak of oil or a strange colour in the water to an adult who can call for help. Schools can adopt a stretch of stream and keep a simple diary of birds and plants through the year. Children who know the name of a duck or a reed are more likely to defend it. Knowledge and care grow side by side.

You do not need to be a scientist to start. Walk the edge with a bag for rubbish, keep dogs from chasing birds if there is a sign, and tell a younger child why a stone should stay on the path, not in the water for fun. A small river that is loved stays alive in the middle of a busy town. Nature protection is not only a poster about a distant jungle. Sometimes it is the pond at the end of your own street.
junior.translation:
人们常常把自然保护想象成一片遥远的森林。然而，许多学生住在一条小河、一条运河，或公园里的一个池塘附近。那片水是鱼、昆虫、鸟和植物的家，也是城镇健康的一部分。如果垃圾被扔进去，如果油被倒进下水道，或者如果岸边被踩得光秃，水就会变浑，生命就会离开。保护附近的池塘，是一种本地的自然照料，小到可以看见，也重要到有关系。

照料从我们不把什么放进水里开始。塑料袋、瓶子和食物残渣并不会消失；它们会漂浮、下沉，或碎成动物可能吞下的碎片。肥皂和油漆不应当被倒进可能通向溪流的雨水口。如果一个班级去参观，他们可以留在小路上，好让握着根和巢的岸边泥土，不在一个兴奋的下午被毁掉。当观看是温和的时候，观看也是一种保护。

一个共同体可以一起做更多。志愿者可以在周末捡起垃圾，在岸边软弱的地方种植芦苇，并把漏油或水里奇怪的颜色报告给一位能够求助的成年人。学校可以认领一段溪流，并在一年里为鸟和植物保留一本简单的日记。知道一只鸭子或一棵芦苇名字的孩子，更可能去保护它。知识与照料并排生长。

你不必成为科学家才能开始。带着一个装垃圾的袋子在水边走，如果有标牌就不要让狗去追鸟，并告诉更小的孩子为什么一块石头应当留在路上，而不是为了好玩被扔进水里。一条被爱着的小河，会在一座忙碌城镇的中间保持活着。自然保护不仅仅是一张关于遥远丛林的海报。有时它就是你自己那条街尽头的池塘。

questions.q: 1. Why does a small river or pond near home matter?
options: It is a home for living things and part of the town’s health, and rubbish or oil can drive those lives away
Because nature protection is only about a faraway forest
Because cloudy water is always a good sign
Because banks should be trampled bare on purpose
questions.exp: 文中说附近的水是鱼虫鸟植物的家，也是城镇健康的一部分，垃圾、油或踩踏会让生命离开。

questions.q: 2. What should we not put into the water or a storm drain?
options: Only stones that always help nests
Roots and reeds that hold the bank
A gentle look from the path
Plastic, food waste, soap and paint, which may not disappear and may harm animals
questions.exp: 文中明确不要把塑料、食物残渣、肥皂和油漆倒进可能通向溪流的地方。

questions.q: 3. How can a school or community help together?
options: Destroy the mud of the bank in one excited afternoon
Refuse to learn the name of any duck or reed
Pick up litter, plant reeds, report a strange colour or oil, and keep a diary of birds and plants
Leave a leak of oil unreported
questions.exp: 文中建议周末捡垃圾、种芦苇、报告异常，以及学校认领一段溪并做观察日记。

questions.q: 4. What simple start does the writer offer if you are not a scientist?
options: Throw stones in the water for fun
Walk the edge with a bag for rubbish, and tell a younger child why a stone should stay on the path
Let dogs chase birds even when a sign asks you not to
Treat the pond at the end of the street as less important than a distant jungle
questions.exp: 文中说不必成为科学家：带着垃圾袋走，遵标牌，并告诉小孩子不要为好玩把石头扔进水里。

junior.title: 🌸 Leaving a Wild Corner in a Garden for Small Lives
junior.content:
A tidy garden can look perfect to human eyes: short grass, no fallen leaves, and every flower in a straight line. To a bee, a beetle or a small bird, that perfect garden can be a desert with nowhere to hide and little to eat. Nature protection can begin in a very small place by leaving a wild corner — a patch of longer grass, a pile of safe branches, a few native flowers, or a shallow dish of water. The corner is not laziness. It is a decision to share the land with lives that were there before the fence.

The corner works because variety matters. Different heights of plants give different animals a home. Fallen leaves slowly become food for the soil. A log can shelter beetles. Flowers that bloom at different times of year offer nectar when it is needed, not only in one showy week. If you use fewer strong chemicals on the lawn, more of those small lives can remain. A garden that is a little less perfect can be a great deal more alive, even in a city balcony if the pots are chosen with care.

There are simple safety rules. Do not pile branches where they block a path or sit against a wooden wall in a risky way. Change the water in a dish so that it does not become stale. Learn which plants are native and which may spread too fast. Children should look, draw and count, not take every insect home in a jar. The aim is a living corner, not a collection that dies on a shelf.

Families can pick a small square, mark it, and visit it through the seasons. A notebook of visitors — a butterfly in May, a bird in winter — turns the corner into a classroom. Neighbours may ask why the grass is longer there, and that question is a chance to explain. Protecting nature is not always a grand trip. Sometimes it is the courage to let one patch of earth stay a little wild, so that the smallest neighbours still have a place.
junior.translation:
一座整洁的花园在人的眼睛里可能看起来完美：短草，没有落叶，每一朵花都在一条直线上。对一只蜂、一只甲虫或一只小鸟来说，那座完美的花园可能是一片无处躲藏、也几乎没有东西可吃的沙漠。自然保护可以从一个很小的地方开始：留出一个野生的角落——一块更长的草，一堆安全的树枝，几朵本地的花，或一盘浅浅的水。这个角落不是懒惰。它是一个决定：与那些在篱笆之前就在这里的生命分享土地。

这个角落之所以有效，是因为多样性重要。不同高度的植物给不同的动物一个家。落叶会慢慢变成土壤的食物。一根圆木可以庇护甲虫。在一年不同时间开放的花，会在被需要时提供花蜜，而不仅仅在一个炫耀的星期里。如果你在草坪上少用强烈的化学品，这些小生命就会有更多能够留下。一座稍不那么完美的花园，可以鲜活得多，即使在城市的阳台上，只要花盆被小心地选择。

也有简单的安全规则。不要把树枝堆在挡住路的地方，或以危险的方式靠着木墙。给盘子换水，免得它变得不新鲜。了解哪些植物是本地的，哪些可能传播得太快。孩子应当观看、绘画和计数，而不是把每一只昆虫都带回家装进罐子。目的是一个活着的角落，而不是一套在架子上死去的收藏。

家庭可以挑选一小块方地，做上记号，并在各个季节里拜访它。一本关于来访者的笔记本——五月的一只蝴蝶，冬天的一只鸟——会把这个角落变成一间教室。邻居也许会问为什么那里的草更长，而那个问题正是一个解释的机会。保护自然并不总是一次盛大的旅行。有时它是让一小块土地保持一点野性的勇气，好让最小的邻居仍然有一个地方。

questions.q: 1. Why can a perfectly tidy garden be a desert for small lives?
options: Because a wild corner is only laziness
Because short grass and no fallen leaves may leave nowhere to hide and little to eat
Because bees and beetles prefer a straight line of flowers and nothing else
Because fences always protect every animal automatically
questions.exp: 文中说对人完美的短草无落叶花园，对蜂、甲虫或小鸟可能无处躲藏、缺少食物。

questions.q: 2. What can a wild corner include, and why does variety matter?
options: Longer grass, safe branches, native flowers or a shallow dish, because different heights and seasons give more animals a home and food
Only one showy week of flowers and many strong chemicals
A risky pile of branches against a wooden wall and a blocked path
A jar on a shelf for every insect
questions.exp: 文中列举长草、安全树枝、本地花或浅水盘，并说明不同高度与花期能提供更多家园和花蜜。

questions.q: 3. What should children do in the corner, according to the passage?
options: Change nothing about stale water in a dish
Ignore which plants are native
Build a collection that dies on a shelf
Look, draw and count, rather than take every insect home in a jar
questions.exp: 文中明确孩子应当观看、绘画和计数，而不是把每只昆虫带回家。

questions.q: 4. How can a family turn the corner into a classroom?
options: Refuse to explain why the grass is longer if a neighbour asks
Treat nature protection as only a grand trip
Mark a small square, visit it through the seasons, and keep a notebook of visitors such as a butterfly or a winter bird
Leave the smallest neighbours with no place at all
questions.exp: 文中建议标记一小块地，按季节拜访，并用笔记本记录来访者，邻居的提问也是解释的机会。

junior.title: 🦌 Why Wild Animals Should Stay in the Wild
junior.content:
A baby bird on a path, a tortoise at a market, or a beautiful feather on a forest floor can tempt a kind hand. Many people want to help, or to keep a piece of nature at home. Yet taking a wild animal away, or buying one that was taken from a forest, often harms the creature and the place it came from. Nature protection includes a hard, loving rule: wild animals should stay in the wild, unless a trained person says they truly need rescue.

A wild animal is not a toy and not a farm pet. It may have a parent nearby, waiting for you to leave. It may need a special diet or a large territory that a bedroom cannot give. Stress, the wrong food, or a closed box can kill a creature that looked only “a little tired.” In the wild, even a single animal may be part of a pair or a group that helps plants, spreads seeds, or feeds other lives. Removing it is not a small souvenir. It is a hole in a living system.

There is a better way to show care. If an animal is clearly injured, keep a safe distance, and ask an adult to call a wildlife centre or a park ranger. Do not feed bread or snacks to ducks and monkeys, which can make them ill and too bold around people. In a reserve, stay on the path, keep quiet, and take photographs instead of taking the animal. Money should go to places that protect habitats, not to sellers who empty those habitats for a cage.

Students can practise this rule on trips and in daily talk. Admire a nest without touching it. Refuse a “cute” wild pet if you do not know where it came from. Share the reason with a friend who means well but has not heard it yet. Love of nature is strongest when it leaves the wild world intact. The best home for a fox, a parrot or a tiny frog is usually the one it already has.
junior.translation:
小路上的一只幼鸟，市场上的一只乌龟，或森林地面上一根美丽的羽毛，都可能诱惑一只善意的手。许多人想要帮忙，或想把自然的一片留在家里。然而，把一只野生动物带走，或买下一只从森林里被拿走的动物，常常会伤害这个生命和它来自的地方。自然保护包括一条艰难而慈爱的规则：野生动物应当留在野外，除非受过训练的人说它们真正需要救助。

野生动物不是玩具，也不是农场里的宠物。它也许有一位父母就在附近，等着你离开。它也许需要特殊的食物，或一间卧室无法提供的广阔领地。压力、错误的食物，或一个封闭的盒子，可能杀死一只看起来只是“有点累”的生命。在野外，即使单独一只动物，也可能是一对或一群中的一部分，它们帮助植物、传播种子，或喂养其他生命。把它拿走不是一件小小的纪念品。它是活着的系统里的一个洞。

有一种更好的方式来表达关心。如果一只动物明显受了伤，保持安全距离，并请成年人给野生动物中心或公园管理员打电话。不要用面包或零食喂鸭子和猴子，那会使它们生病，并在人周围变得太大胆。在保护区里，留在小路上，保持安静，并拍照，而不是把动物带走。钱应当流向保护栖息地的地方，而不是流向为了一只笼子而掏空那些栖息地的卖家。

学生可以在旅行里和日常谈话里练习这条规则。欣赏一个巢，却不触摸它。如果你不知道一只“可爱”的野生宠物从哪里来，就拒绝它。把这个理由分享给一位出于好意、却还没有听过它的朋友。当它让野生世界保持完整时，对自然的爱才是最强的。狐狸、鹦鹉或一只小青蛙最好的家，通常就是它已经拥有的那个。

questions.q: 1. What ‘hard, loving rule’ does the passage give?
options: A baby bird on a path should always be taken home
Buying an animal taken from a forest is a kind way to help
Wild animals should stay in the wild, unless a trained person says they truly need rescue
A wild animal is a good bedroom toy
questions.exp: 文中给出规则：野生动物应留在野外，除非受过训练的人确认它们真正需要救助。

questions.q: 2. Why can taking a wild animal away cause harm even if you mean to help?
options: Stress and the wrong food never hurt a tired creature
A parent may be nearby, the diet or territory may be wrong, and removing one animal can leave a hole in a living system
A closed box is always a safe souvenir
Wild animals do not help plants or spread seeds
questions.exp: 文中说明父母可能在附近等待，错误食物或封闭盒子可能致命，移走一只动物会在系统里留下一个洞。

questions.q: 3. What should you do if an animal is clearly injured?
options: Keep a safe distance and ask an adult to call a wildlife centre or a park ranger
Feed it bread and snacks so that it becomes bold around people
Take it from the path and hide it in a jar
Pay a seller who empties habitats for a cage
questions.exp: 文中建议保持安全距离，请成年人联系野生动物中心或公园管理员。

questions.q: 4. How can students practise this kind of love of nature?
options: Touch every nest and take a fox home
Leave the wild world less intact
Ignore where a pet came from if it looks cute
Admire a nest without touching it, refuse a ‘cute’ wild pet of unknown origin, and share the reason with a well-meaning friend
questions.exp: 文中建议欣赏而不触摸巢，拒绝来源不明的野生宠物，并把理由分享给出于好意的朋友。

junior.title: 🎶 How a School Choir Learns to Listen to One Another
junior.content:
A school choir looks, from the seats, like one voice. Up close, it is a team. Sopranos, altos and those who sing the lower line must come in at the right moment, at a volume that does not bury the others, and with words that match. The art is musical, but the work is cooperation. A choir that only tries to be loud will sound messy. A choir that learns to listen, to wait, and to blend will sound stronger than any single proud voice.

Rehearsal is where the cooperation is built. The conductor gives a sign, and the group must watch as well as sing. If one row is late, the others do not shout; they stop, smile, and try the phrase again. Students learn to accept a note about pitch or diction without taking it as a personal attack. They also learn to help a neighbour find the starting note, and to share a score when a copy is missing. These small acts are the hidden music of the group.

A concert makes the lesson public. Someone may feel nervous, and a friend can stand a little closer, or breathe with them in the pause. If a word goes wrong, the choir continues together rather than staring at the person who slipped. After the applause, the credit belongs to every section, including those who sang a quieter line that the audience hardly named. Art that is made together teaches a generous kind of pride: I did my part, and we made something none of us could have made alone.

Students who are not in a choir can still use the idea in a band, a dance, or a class reading. Listen for the others, do not rush to be first, and leave space so that a smaller part can be heard. Cooperation in art is not a soft extra. It is the method that turns many people into one piece of work, and it is a skill that still matters when the song is over.
junior.translation:
从座位上看，学校合唱团像一个声音。靠近看，它是一个团队。女高音、女低音和唱较低声部的人，必须在恰当的时刻进入，以一种不淹没别人的音量，并配上一致的词。这门艺术是音乐的，但这项工作是合作。一个只想大声的合唱团会听起来混乱。一个学会倾听、等待和融合的合唱团，会比任何单独一个骄傲的声音更强。

排练是合作被建立的地方。指挥给出一个手势，团体必须一边唱一边看。如果一排晚了，其他人并不喊叫；他们停下，微笑，再试一次那个乐句。学生学会接受关于音高或咬字的提醒，而不把它当作人身攻击。他们也学会帮助旁边的人找到起始音，并在缺了复印谱时共享一份。这些小行动是这个团体隐藏的音乐。

一场音乐会让这一课变得公开。有人也许会紧张，一位朋友可以站得近一点，或在停顿里和他们一起呼吸。如果一个词错了，合唱继续在一起，而不是盯着那个滑了一下的人。掌声之后，功劳属于每一个声部，包括那些唱了观众几乎叫不出名字的、更安静的声部的人。一起做成的艺术，教出一种慷慨的骄傲：我做了我的部分，而我们做成了谁也不能独自做成的东西。

不在合唱团里的学生，仍然可以把这个想法用在乐队、舞蹈或课堂朗读里。倾听别人，不要抢着当第一，并留出空间，好让更小的声部被听见。艺术里的合作不是一种柔软的附加。它是把许多人变成一件作品的方法，也是一首歌结束之后仍然重要的技能。

questions.q: 1. Why will a choir that only tries to be loud sound messy?
options: Because cooperation is not part of the work
Because the conductor should never be watched
Because words do not need to match
Because the group must listen, wait and blend, and no single proud voice should bury the others
questions.exp: 文中说只想大声会混乱，学会倾听、等待和融合才会比单独骄傲的声音更强。

questions.q: 2. What hidden music of cooperation appears in rehearsal?
options: Shouting at a row that is late
Refusing to help a neighbour find the starting note
Stopping and trying a phrase again, accepting a note about pitch without taking it as an attack, and sharing a score
Watching the conductor never, and singing only
questions.exp: 文中举例停下再试、不把音高提醒当作人身攻击、帮邻居找音并共享乐谱。

questions.q: 3. How should a choir treat a mistake in a concert?
options: Stop and point so that the audience can name the quieter line
Continue together rather than staring at the person who slipped, and share the credit with every section after the applause
Give pride only to the loudest voice
Leave a nervous friend to breathe alone
questions.exp: 文中说词错了也要一起继续，不要盯着滑了一下的人，功劳属于每个声部。

questions.q: 4. How can students use the same idea outside a choir?
options: Listen for the others, do not rush to be first, and leave space so that a smaller part can be heard in a band, a dance or a class reading
Treat cooperation as a soft extra that never matters after the song
Always rush to be first so that no smaller part is heard
Work only alone, because art cannot be made together
questions.exp: 文中建议在乐队、舞蹈或课堂朗读里同样倾听、不抢先，并给更小的部分留出空间。

junior.title: 🎨 Painting a Wall Mural as a Group
junior.content:
A mural on a school wall begins as a blank, slightly frightening space. No one person can usually fill it well in a day, and no one person should decide every colour if the wall belongs to everyone. Painting a mural is therefore a lesson in art and in cooperation. The group must agree on a theme, sketch the big shapes together, and then share the work so that a tree, a window of the school, or a row of faces is made by many hands that still look like one picture.

The first meetings matter as much as the brushes. Students bring ideas, and some ideas must be left out without leaving the person out. A simple vote, or a mix of two sketches, can keep the peace. Then the wall is measured, the drawing is copied lightly, and tasks are given: large backgrounds, careful outlines, a border, and the cleaning at the end. Taller students may take the high parts, and those who like detail may take the smaller figures. Cooperation is practical here. It is also kind: a mistake can be painted over, and a tired painter can be replaced for a while.

As the picture grows, the group must keep looking at the whole, not only at their own patch. A colour that is too bright in one corner can unbalance the wall. Someone needs to step back, say so honestly, and help to adjust it. Shared rules about dropping paint on the ground, wearing old clothes, and washing brushes protect the space and the friendship. A mural that is finished in anger will not feel like a gift to the school.

When the last line is dry, sign it as a team, and tell the story of how the choices were made. Visitors will see a picture; the painters will remember the hour when they disagreed and then found a third way. Art made on a wall is public, so the cooperation stays visible long after the brushes are cleaned. That is why a group mural is worth the mess: it teaches that a shared place can be made more beautiful when many people decide, and paint, together.
junior.translation:
学校墙上的一幅壁画，开始时是一片空白而略微让人害怕的空间。通常没有一个人能在一天里把它填好，如果这面墙属于每一个人，也不应当由一个人决定每一种颜色。因此，画一幅壁画是一堂关于艺术和合作的课。团体必须商定一个主题，一起勾出大的形状，然后分担工作，好让一棵树、学校的一扇窗，或一排面孔，由许多仍然看起来像一幅画的手来完成。

最初的几次会议和画笔同样重要。学生们带来想法，有些想法必须被放下，却不把那个人排除在外。一次简单的投票，或把两张草图混合，可以维持和平。然后墙被测量，图画被轻轻地拷上去，任务被分配：大的背景，仔细的轮廓，一条边框，以及最后的清理。个子高的学生可以负责高处，喜欢细节的人可以负责较小的形象。合作在这里是实际的。它也是善意的：一个错误可以再被涂上，一位疲倦的画家可以暂时被替换。

当图画生长时，团体必须继续看整体，而不仅仅看自己的那一块。一角过亮的颜色可能让整面墙失去平衡。需要有人退后一步，诚实地说出来，并帮助调整它。关于不要把颜料掉在地上、穿旧衣服、以及清洗画笔的共享规则，保护着这片空间和这段友谊。一幅在愤怒中完成的壁画，不会感觉像给学校的礼物。

当最后一条线干了，以一个团队的名义署名，并讲述那些选择是如何做出的。来访者会看见一幅画；画家们会记得他们意见不合、然后找到第三条路的那个小时。墙上做成的艺术是公共的，所以在画笔被清洗很久之后，合作仍然看得见。这就是为什么一幅集体壁画值得那场忙乱：它教人明白，当许多人一起决定、一起画时，一个共享的地方可以变得更美。

questions.q: 1. Why is painting a mural a lesson in cooperation as well as art?
options: Because the wall belongs to everyone, so the group must agree on a theme and share the work so that many hands still look like one picture
Because one person should decide every colour in a single day
Because ideas must leave the person out of the group
Because a blank wall should stay frightening and empty
questions.exp: 文中说墙属于每个人，必须商定主题并分担工作，使许多手仍然像一幅画。

questions.q: 2. How can the group keep peace when some ideas must be left out?
options: By giving every task only to taller students
By refusing to measure the wall or copy the drawing
By never painting over a mistake or replacing a tired painter
By a simple vote or a mix of two sketches, without leaving the person out
questions.exp: 文中建议用简单投票或混合两张草图来维持和平，放下想法而不排除那个人。

questions.q: 3. What must the group do as the picture grows?
options: Look only at their own patch and ignore the corner
Drop paint on the ground to finish faster
Keep looking at the whole, step back, and honestly adjust a colour that unbalances the wall
Finish the mural in anger so that it feels like a gift
questions.exp: 文中说必须看整体，有人退后诚实指出过亮的颜色并帮助调整。

questions.q: 4. What will the painters remember after they sign the wall as a team?
options: Only the mess, and never the shared place
The hour when they disagreed and then found a third way, which stays visible as public art
A story that must not be told to visitors
That many people should never decide or paint together
questions.exp: 文中说画家会记得意见不合后找到第三条路的那个小时，公共墙上的合作在清洗之后仍可见。

junior.title: 📰 Making a Class Newspaper Together
junior.content:
A class newspaper is a small work of art made by many roles. Someone gathers news from a sports day or a science fair. Someone draws a comic or a heading. Someone checks the spelling, and someone arranges the pages so that a short poem and a long report can both breathe. If one student tried to do all of this the night before it was due, the paper would be thin and late. Cooperation turns the work into a weekly or monthly craft that the class can be proud of, and that other classes can read.

The team needs a plan and a kind editor. At a short meeting, jobs are chosen, and deadlines are written where everyone can see them. The editor’s task is not to shout, but to ask for a clearer sentence, to make sure two articles are not about the same event, and to thank people who finish on time. Writers must accept cuts that help the page, and artists must leave space for the words. A newspaper is a conversation between parts. When the parts respect one another, the whole looks professional even if it is printed on ordinary paper.

Truth and fairness are part of the art. A report should check a fact before it is published, and a joke should not hurt a classmate. If a mistake appears, the next issue can correct it, which is also a lesson in responsibility. Cooperation includes the quiet jobs: numbering pages, saving a copy, and delivering the paper to the library or the hallway wall. Those jobs are easy to forget and essential to the finished object.

Students who have made a paper together often work better on later group projects, because they have already practised the mix of talent and patience. You can start with one page, four hands, and a single story. The art will grow as more people join, each bringing a skill the others lack. A class newspaper is not only writing. It is a picture of a community thinking together, and then sharing that thinking in a form that anyone can pick up and enjoy.
junior.translation:
一份班级报纸，是由许多角色做成的一件小小的艺术品。有人从运动会或科学展览搜集新闻。有人画一幅漫画或一个标题。有人检查拼写，有人安排版面，好让一首短诗和一篇长报道都能呼吸。如果一个学生想在截止前的那个晚上做完所有这一切，报纸就会又薄又晚。合作把这项工作变成一种班级可以为之骄傲、其他班级也可以阅读的每周或每月的手艺。

这个团队需要一个计划和一位善意的编辑。在一次短会上，工作被选定，截止日期被写在人人都能看见的地方。编辑的任务不是喊叫，而是请求一句更清楚的句子，确保两篇文章不是在写同一件事，并感谢按时完成的人。写的人必须接受有助于版面的删减，画的人必须给文字留出空间。一份报纸是各个部分之间的对话。当这些部分彼此尊重时，即使印在普通的纸上，整体也会看起来专业。

真实和公平是这门艺术的一部分。一篇报道在发表前应当核对一个事实，一个笑话不应当伤害同学。如果出现错误，下一期可以改正它，而这也是一课关于责任的课。合作也包括那些安静的工作：给页面编号，保存一份拷贝，并把报纸送到图书馆或走廊的墙上。那些工作容易被忘记，对最终的成品却是必要的。

一起做过报纸的学生，在后来的小组项目里常常合作得更好，因为他们已经练习过才能与耐心的混合。你可以从一页纸、四只手和单独一个故事开始。随着更多人加入，每人带来别人缺少的一种技能，这门艺术就会生长。班级报纸不仅仅是写作。它是一个共同体一起思考、然后以一种任何人都可以拿起来欣赏的形式分享那种思考的图画。

questions.q: 1. Why would one student doing all the work the night before make a thin, late paper?
options: Because art and comics should never appear beside a report
Because a newspaper needs many roles — news, drawings, spelling checks and page design — and cooperation turns it into a regular craft
Because other classes must not be allowed to read it
Because a short poem cannot share a page with a long report
questions.exp: 文中说明报纸需要搜集新闻、漫画标题、校对和排版等多种角色，一人赶工只会又薄又晚。

questions.q: 2. What is the editor’s job, according to the passage?
options: To ask for clearer sentences, avoid two articles on the same event, thank people who finish on time, and keep a kind plan
To shout at the team
To refuse all cuts that would help the page
To fill every space so that artists have no room for words
questions.exp: 文中说编辑不是喊叫，而是让句子更清楚、避免重复选题、感谢按时完成的人。

questions.q: 3. How are truth and fairness part of this art?
options: Mistakes must never be corrected
Quiet jobs such as numbering pages do not matter
The paper should be hidden from the library and the hallway
A report should check a fact, a joke should not hurt a classmate, and a later issue can correct a mistake
questions.exp: 文中强调发表前核对事实，笑话不伤害同学，下一期可改正错误，这也是责任。

questions.q: 4. What can students start with if the paper is new?
options: A finished professional magazine on the first night
A project with no patience and no talent
One page, four hands, and a single story, then grow as more people bring skills the others lack
A community that never shares its thinking
questions.exp: 文中建议从一页纸、四只手和单一故事开始，随更多人加入各自技能而生长。

junior.title: 🎨 Why Mixed Colours Do Not Always Behave as We Expect
junior.content:
Art and science meet on the palette. A student who mixes blue and yellow may hope for a clean green, and sometimes the result is dull, brownish, or surprisingly dark. This is not simply bad luck. Colour mixing follows rules that science can explain, and artists who learn those rules waste less paint and get closer to the colour in their mind. The brush is a tool of feeling, but it also stirs real materials with real limits.

Paints are made of tiny particles of pigment in a medium. When you mix two paints, you are stacking filters: each pigment swallows some of the light and reflects the rest. Blue paint keeps some blue light; yellow paint keeps some yellow-green light; together they may leave only a modest green, or almost no bright light at all if both are strong and dark. This is why mixing many colours often leads to mud. Light on a screen works differently. Red, green and blue light added together can make white, which is the opposite of the muddy mix on a plate. The two systems are easy to confuse, and a science lesson can keep them apart.

Artists use the science without losing the play. They test a small patch first, clean the brush between colours, and add a little white or a little earth colour on purpose, not by accident. They notice how a colour changes when it sits beside a different neighbour, because the eye compares. A grey next to a bright orange can look bluish. That fact is both an experiment and a trick that painters have used for centuries.

Students can keep a mixing page in a sketchbook: two colours, the result, and a short note. They can also shine a torch through coloured films and compare that mix with a mix of paints. The double experiment makes the idea stick. Art becomes less mysterious, and science becomes something you can see. When a green finally appears as you hoped, you will know it was not only a gift. It was a question you asked of light and of matter, and a careful answer from both.
junior.translation:
艺术和科学在调色板上相遇。一个把蓝色和黄色混合的学生，也许希望得到干净的绿色，而结果有时是沉闷的、发棕的，或出奇地暗。这并不只是运气不好。颜色混合遵循科学能够解释的规则，学会那些规则的艺术家会少浪费颜料，并更接近他们心里的颜色。画笔是感觉的工具，但它也搅拌着真实的材料，以及真实的限度。

颜料由介质里细小的色素颗粒做成。当你混合两种颜料时，你是在叠放滤镜：每一种色素吞下一些光，并反射其余的光。蓝颜料留住一些蓝光；黄颜料留住一些黄绿光；它们在一起也许只留下温和的绿色，或者，如果两者都又浓又暗，就几乎不留下明亮的光。这就是为什么混合许多颜色常常得到泥浆。屏幕上的光则不同。红、绿、蓝光加在一起可以变成白色，这与盘子上泥浆般的混合相反。两套系统很容易被弄混，而一堂科学课可以把它们分开。

艺术家使用科学，却不失去玩耍。他们先试一小块，在颜色之间清洗画笔，并有意地加入一点白或一点大地色，而不是偶然如此。他们注意到，一种颜色坐在不同的邻居旁边时会改变，因为眼睛会比较。一块灰色挨着明亮的橙色，可能看起来发蓝。那个事实既是一个实验，也是画家使用了几个世纪的技巧。

学生可以在素描本里保留一页混合记录：两种颜色，结果，和一句短注。他们也可以用手电筒照过彩色薄膜，并把那种混合与颜料的混合比较。这个双重实验会让想法留住。艺术变得不那么神秘，科学变成你能够看见的东西。当一种绿色终于如你希望的那样出现时，你会知道它不仅仅是一份礼物。它是你向光和向物质提出的一个问题，也是两者给出的一个小心的回答。

questions.q: 1. Why may blue and yellow paint not make a clean green?
options: Because colour mixing has no rules that science can explain
Because a brush never stirs real materials
Because each pigment swallows some light, and together they may leave only a modest or dull green, especially if both are dark
Because luck is the only cause of a brownish result
questions.exp: 文中解释颜料像滤镜一样吞下部分光，两种又浓又暗的颜料可能只留下温和甚至几乎不亮的绿。

questions.q: 2. How is mixing light on a screen different from mixing paints?
options: Light and paint follow exactly the same system
Red, green and blue light added together can make white, which is the opposite of the muddy mix on a plate
Adding paints together always makes white
A science lesson cannot keep the two systems apart
questions.exp: 文中对比屏幕上红绿蓝光相加可得白色，与盘子上越混越浊相反。

questions.q: 3. What scientific fact about the eye do painters use?
options: A colour can change when it sits beside a different neighbour, because the eye compares, so a grey next to orange may look bluish
A colour never changes beside a neighbour
Tests and clean brushes are useless
White or earth colours should be added only by accident
questions.exp: 文中说眼睛会比较，灰色挨着亮橙可能发蓝，这既是实验也是古老技巧。

questions.q: 4. What double experiment can help students remember the idea?
options: Mix as many colours as possible until only mud remains
Avoid all notes in a sketchbook
Ask no questions of light or of matter
Keep a mixing page of paints, and also shine a torch through coloured films and compare the two kinds of mix
questions.exp: 文中建议在素描本记录颜料混合，并用手电筒透过彩色薄膜比较两种混合。

junior.title: △ How Perspective Makes a Flat Picture Feel Deep
junior.content:
A sheet of paper is flat, yet a careful drawing can feel like a road that runs away under your feet. That feeling is called perspective, and it is a meeting of art and science. Artists noticed, and then mathematicians described, that parallel lines appear to come together as they go farther from the eye, and that objects look smaller with distance. When a drawing follows these rules, the brain accepts the trick and reads depth on a flat page.

You can test the idea in a hallway. Stand at one end and hold up a pencil: the far door looks small enough to cover with a thumb, though you know it is as tall as the door beside you. Rails of a track, edges of a table, and the tops of a row of windows all point toward a vanishing point on the horizon of your view. Renaissance painters used this geometry to build streets and rooms that still surprise us. A science of light and lines became a language of art.

The rules can be played with, too. A slightly high or low vanishing point can make the viewer feel tall or small. Two vanishing points can show the corner of a building. If the rules are broken on purpose, the picture may feel strange, like a dream, which some modern artists want. If they are broken by accident, the chair may look as if it is sliding off the floor. Knowing the science gives the artist a choice, not only a habit.

Students can practise with a ruler, a horizon line, and a simple box that becomes a house, a street, or a classroom. They can also photograph a corridor and trace the lines. The exercise trains the eye to see that the world is already full of geometry. Art is not the opposite of measurement. Sometimes it is measurement, used with feeling, so that a flat page can hold a deep space, and a viewer can take a walk without leaving the chair.
junior.translation:
一张纸是平的，然而一幅仔细的画可以感觉像一条从你脚下远去的路。那种感觉叫做透视，它是艺术与科学的相遇。艺术家先注意到，随后数学家描述道：平行线在离开眼睛越来越远时，看起来会聚到一起，而物体随着距离会显得更小。当一幅画遵循这些规则时，大脑就会接受这个把戏，并在一张平纸上读出深度。

你可以在走廊里测试这个想法。站在一端，举起一支铅笔：远处的门看起来小到可以用拇指盖住，虽然你知道它和你身边的门一样高。铁轨、桌子的边，以及一排窗户的顶，都会指向你视野地平线上的一个消失点。文艺复兴的画家用这种几何去建造至今仍让我们吃惊的街道和房间。一门关于光和线条的科学，变成了艺术的一种语言。

这些规则也可以被拿来玩。一个稍高或稍低的消失点，可以让观者感觉自己很高或很小。两个消失点可以显示一座建筑的转角。如果规则被有意地打破，图画也许会感觉奇怪，像一场梦，而这正是一些现代艺术家想要的。如果它们是偶然被打破的，椅子也许会看起来像要从地板上滑走。了解科学，给艺术家的是一种选择，而不仅仅是一种习惯。

学生可以用一把尺子、一条地平线和一个变成房子、街道或教室的简单方盒子来练习。他们也可以给一条走廊拍照，并描出那些线。这个练习训练眼睛去看见：世界已经充满了几何。艺术不是测量的反面。有时它就是带着感觉被使用的测量，好让一张平纸能够装下一个深深的空间，而观者可以不必离开椅子就去走一段路。

questions.q: 1. What scientific idea helps a flat drawing feel deep?
options: A sheet of paper is already deep without any trick
The brain never accepts depth on a flat page
Objects look larger as they move farther from the eye
Parallel lines appear to meet as they go farther away, and objects look smaller with distance
questions.exp: 文中说明平行线在远处看起来会聚，物体随距离变小，大脑便在平纸上读出深度。

questions.q: 2. What hallway test does the writer suggest?
options: Rails and window tops never point toward a vanishing point
Renaissance painters refused all geometry
Hold up a pencil: the far door may be covered by a thumb, though it is as tall as the door beside you
A far door always looks larger than the near one
questions.exp: 文中建议在走廊一端用铅笔比较：远处的门小到可用拇指盖住，尽管实际一样高。

questions.q: 3. Why does knowing the rules give an artist a choice?
options: Rules must never be played with
A high or low vanishing point, or two points, can change the feeling, and rules broken on purpose can look like a dream, while accidents can make a chair slide
A strange, dreamlike picture is only a mistake
Science can never become a language of art
questions.exp: 文中说高低消失点会改变观者感觉，有意打破规则可像梦，偶然打破却可能让椅子像要滑走。

questions.q: 4. How can students practise perspective?
options: With a ruler, a horizon line and a simple box, or by photographing a corridor and tracing the lines
By avoiding all measurement, because art is the opposite of geometry
By never looking at a hallway or a street
By leaving the page flat and refusing any feeling of deep space
questions.exp: 文中建议用尺子、地平线和方盒子练习，或给走廊拍照并描线，看见世界已充满几何。

junior.title: 🏺 How Heat Turns Soft Clay Into Lasting Pottery
junior.content:
A pot begins as soft clay that can be squeezed, rolled and collapsed with a wet thumb. After it is shaped and dried, it goes into a kiln, a special oven that becomes far hotter than a kitchen. Heat changes the material in a way that art depends on and science can explain. Water is driven out, and the tiny particles of clay begin to bond. The pot that comes out is no longer mud. It is a hard object that can hold soup, flowers, or a story in its surface design.

The temperature and the time must be right. Too little heat, and the pot may stay weak and crumble. Too much heat, or a sudden change, and it may crack or slump. Potters learn these limits by testing, by listening to teachers, and by reading the colour of the kiln. A glaze — a glassy coat — melts in the fire and then hardens into a smooth skin that can be waterproof and brightly coloured. Chemistry and patience share the same shelf in a pottery room.

Artists use the science as a partner. They choose a clay that fits the purpose, leave the walls even so that heat can travel fairly, and dry the work slowly to avoid hidden pockets of steam. A handle must be joined with care, or the fire will find the weak line. Decorations may be painted before or after certain firings, depending on the materials. Each choice is both a design decision and an experiment that can fail, which is why a first successful cup can feel like a small miracle.

Students who try even a pinch pot, later fired at school or at a studio, can feel this meeting of hands and heat. They learn that art is not only an idea on paper. It is matter changing state, and a craftsman walking beside that change with respect. The next time you hold a mug, you can remember that it once was soft earth, and that fire, guided by knowledge, gave it a lasting shape. Art and science drink from the same cup.
junior.translation:
一只陶罐开始时是柔软的黏土，可以用湿拇指挤压、搓滚，也可以把它弄塌。在成形和干燥之后，它进入窑，一种比厨房热得多的特制炉子。热以一种艺术所依赖、科学能够解释的方式改变这种材料。水被赶出来，细小的黏土颗粒开始结合。出来的罐子不再是泥。它是一件可以盛汤、插花，或在表面图案里盛一个故事的硬物。

温度和时间必须恰当。热太少，罐子也许仍然脆弱并碎开。热太多，或一次突然的变化，它也许会裂或塌。陶工通过试验、倾听老师，以及阅读窑的颜色来学习这些限度。一层釉——一层玻璃般的涂层——在火里融化，然后硬成一层可以防水、也可以色彩明亮的光滑外皮。化学和耐心在陶艺室里共享同一层架子。

艺术家把科学当作伙伴来使用。他们选择适合用途的黏土，让壁厚均匀好让热能够公平地旅行，并慢慢干燥作品，以避免隐藏的蒸汽囊。把手必须被小心地接上，否则火会找到那条软弱的线。装饰可能在某几次烧制之前或之后被画上，这取决于材料。每一个选择既是一个设计决定，也是一个可能失败的实验，这就是为什么第一只成功的杯子会感觉像一个小奇迹。

即使只做过一个用手指捏成的小盆、稍后在学校或工作室被烧制的学生，也能感觉到这双手与热的相遇。他们会学到，艺术不仅仅是纸上的一个想法。它是物质在改变状态，以及一位匠人带着尊敬走在那种改变旁边。下一次你握着一只杯子时，你可以记得它曾经是柔软的泥土，而被知识引导的火给了它一个持久的形状。艺术和科学，从同一只杯子里饮水。

questions.q: 1. What does heat do to soft clay in a kiln?
options: It drives out water and bonds the tiny particles, so the pot becomes a hard object that can hold soup or flowers
It turns the pot back into wet mud
It always leaves the pot weak, with no change of material
It works only in a kitchen oven, never in a special kiln
questions.exp: 文中说热把水赶出，使黏土颗粒结合，出来的罐子不再是泥，而是可盛汤或插花的硬物。

questions.q: 2. Why must temperature and time be right?
options: A glaze never melts or hardens in the fire
Potters should ignore the colour of the kiln
Chemistry has no place in a pottery room
Too little heat can leave the pot weak; too much heat or a sudden change can make it crack or slump
questions.exp: 文中说明热太少会脆弱粉碎，太多或突然变化会裂或塌，陶工需试验并观察窑的颜色。

questions.q: 3. How do artists use the science as a partner?
options: They hide pockets of steam and join handles carelessly
They avoid all experiments, because a cup can never fail
They choose a fitting clay, keep walls even, dry the work slowly, and join a handle with care so the fire does not find a weak line
They paint decorations with no thought of when the firings happen
questions.exp: 文中列举选择合适黏土、壁厚均匀、慢慢干燥、小心接把手，以免火找到软弱的线。

questions.q: 4. What does the writer want you to remember when you hold a mug?
options: That art is only an idea on paper and never a change of matter
That it was once soft earth, and that fire guided by knowledge gave it a lasting shape
That a craftsman should not walk beside the change with respect
That science and art can never share the same cup
questions.exp: 文中说握着杯子时可记得它曾是软泥，被知识引导的火给了它持久的形状。

junior.title: 🧊 How the Refrigerator Changed What Families Could Eat
junior.content:
For most of history, keeping food fresh was a race against time and weather. Families used cool cellars, salt, smoke, or winter ice cut from lakes and stored under straw. These methods helped, but they were limited. Milk could sour in a day of heat, and meat had to be eaten or preserved quickly. The refrigerator, invented and then improved over many decades, changed this daily problem. A closed box, cooled by a machine, gave ordinary homes a small, steady winter in every season.

The invention did not arrive all at once. Early machines were large, costly, and sometimes dangerous. Engineers worked on safer gases, better pumps, and quieter motors. Factories learned to build boxes that more families could buy. As the appliance spread, shops could keep fish and fruit for longer, and hospitals could store medicine that needed the cold. History often looks like a single “aha.” In this case it was a long chain of designs, each one making the last more useful and more common.

The change in the kitchen was huge. Families could shop less often, waste less food, and eat a wider variety in summer and winter. Leftovers became a normal lunch, not a risk. Fresh milk and vegetables could travel farther from the farm. There were new habits, too: people had to learn to close the door, not to pack the box so full that air could not move, and not to leave cooked food out for hours before cooling it. An invention changes behaviour as well as machines.

Today a fridge feels ordinary, almost invisible. That is a sign of how completely it entered daily history. When you open the door, you can remember the cellars and the blocks of ice, and the long work that brought the cold inside. The best inventions do not only surprise us once. They quietly rewrite what a family can eat, when they can eat it, and how far a town can sit from the fields that feed it.
junior.translation:
在历史的大部分时间里，保存食物新鲜是一场与时间和天气的赛跑。家庭使用凉爽的地窖、盐、烟，或从湖里切下、在稻草下储存的冬冰。这些方法有帮助，但它们是有限度的。牛奶在一天的炎热里就会变酸，肉必须被很快吃掉或腌制。冰箱在许多十年里被发明、又被改进，改变了这个日常问题。一个由机器冷却的封闭盒子，给了普通家庭一个在每个季节里都稳定的小小冬天。

这项发明并不是一次全部到来的。早期的机器又大又贵，有时还危险。工程师研究更安全的气体、更好的泵，以及更安静的马达。工厂学会制造更多家庭买得起的箱子。随着这种器具的普及，商店可以把鱼和水果保存得更久，医院也可以储存需要寒冷的药品。历史看起来常常像一声单独的“啊哈”。在这件事里，它是一长串设计，每一个都让上一个更有用、也更常见。

厨房里的变化是巨大的。家庭可以少去几次商店，少浪费食物，并在夏天和冬天吃到更丰富的种类。剩菜变成一顿平常的午饭，而不是一种风险。新鲜的牛奶和蔬菜可以从农场走得更远。也有了新的习惯：人们必须学会关上门，不要把箱子塞到空气无法流动，也不要让做熟的食物在冷却前在外面放上几小时。一项发明既改变机器，也改变行为。

今天一台冰箱感觉很平常，几乎看不见。那是一个标志，说明它多么彻底地走进了日常历史。当你打开门时，你可以记起那些地窖和冰块，以及把寒冷带进屋里的漫长工作。最好的发明不只让我们吃惊一次。它们会安静地改写一个家庭能够吃什么，何时能吃，以及一座城镇可以离养活它的田地多远。

questions.q: 1. How did families try to keep food fresh before the refrigerator?
options: By leaving milk out in a day of heat on purpose
With cool cellars, salt, smoke, or winter ice stored under straw
By inventing a quiet motor in every kitchen at once
By never eating meat or fruit
questions.exp: 文中列举地窖、盐、烟，以及在稻草下储存的冬冰。

questions.q: 2. Why does the passage say the invention did not arrive all at once?
options: Early machines were large, costly and sometimes dangerous, and many later designs made them safer and more common
Engineers refused to work on safer gases or better pumps
Shops and hospitals never stored fish, fruit or medicine in the cold
History in this case was a single ‘aha’ with no chain of designs
questions.exp: 文中说明早期机器大、贵、有时危险，后来的气体、泵和马达改进使它更普及。

questions.q: 3. What new kitchen habits did families have to learn?
options: To pack the box so full that air could not move
To shop more often and waste more food
To keep leftovers as a risk, never as a lunch
To close the door, leave space for air to move, and cool cooked food instead of leaving it out for hours
questions.exp: 文中提到要关门、不要塞太满以致空气无法流动，以及不要让熟食在冷却前久放。

questions.q: 4. What does a fridge quietly rewrite, according to the ending?
options: Only a single surprise, with no change to daily history
The need to forget cellars and blocks of ice
What a family can eat, when they can eat it, and how far a town can sit from the fields
A rule that farms must always sit next to every house
questions.exp: 文中说最好的发明会改写家庭能吃什么、何时能吃，以及城镇可以离田地多远。

junior.title: 🖨️ How the Printing Press Spread Words Faster Than a Hand Could Copy
junior.content:
Before the printing press, a book was usually copied by hand. A scribe sat for weeks or months, letter by letter, and a single mistake could travel into the next copy. Books were rare and costly, and many people never held one. Then a press was developed that could ink a page of movable metal letters and stamp it again and again. One skilled shop could produce many identical pages in a day. This invention belongs to history because it changed not only workshops, but who could read, learn and share an idea.

Movable type was the heart of the idea. Letters could be set in a tray, used, then taken apart and set again for a new page. Oil-based ink and a firm press helped the marks stay sharp. The work was still physical and skilled: someone had to arrange the letters backward, check a first sheet, and keep the paper even. Yet compared with a hand copy, the speed was astonishing. A pamphlet, a school book, or a public notice could reach a town before a messenger had finished one careful manuscript.

The effects spread in waves. More books meant more readers, and more readers created a demand for still more books, including cheaper ones. Scientific drawings and maps could be shared with fewer errors than a tired hand might introduce. News and arguments travelled farther, which was exciting and, for some rulers, uncomfortable. History shows that a tool for words is also a tool for power: it can educate, and it can also spread a false claim more quickly. People had to become more careful readers as well as faster ones.

Today a printer or a screen can copy a page in a second, and it is easy to forget the first leap. When you hold a printed textbook, you can picture the trays of metal letters and the workers who set them. The press did not invent writing, and it did not invent paper. It invented a way for writing to travel at the speed of a machine, and that change still shapes classrooms, newspapers and public life.
junior.translation:
在印刷机之前，一本书通常是用手抄写的。一位抄写员一封信一封信地坐上几周或几个月，而一个单独的错误就可能走进下一份抄本。书又少又贵，许多人从未拿过一本。后来出现了一种印刷机，它能够给一页活的金属字母上墨，并一次又一次地压印。一个熟练的作坊一天可以做出许多相同的页。这项发明属于历史，因为它改变的不仅是作坊，还有谁能够阅读、学习并分享一个想法。

活字是这个想法的核心。字母可以被排进一个托盘，使用，然后再拆开，为新的一页重新排。油性的墨和结实的压印帮助字迹保持清晰。这项工作仍然是费力而需要技能的：必须有人把字母反向排列，检查第一张纸，并让纸保持平整。然而与手抄相比，速度是惊人的。一本小册子、一本课本，或一张公告，可以在信使写完一份仔细的手稿之前就到达一座城镇。

影响一波一波地散开。更多的书意味着更多的读者，而更多的读者又创造出对更多书、包括更便宜的书的需求。科学图画和地图可以以比一只疲倦的手可能引入的更少的错误被分享。新闻和争论走得更远，这令人兴奋，而对一些统治者来说并不舒服。历史表明，一件用于文字的工具也是一件用于权力的工具：它可以教育，也可以更快地传播一个虚假的说法。人们必须成为更小心的读者，同时也是更快的读者。

今天一台打印机或一块屏幕可以在一秒内复制一页，人们很容易忘记那第一次跳跃。当你拿着一本印刷的课本时，你可以想象那些金属字母的托盘，以及排字的工人。印刷机并没有发明书写，也没有发明纸。它发明了一种让书写以机器的速度旅行的方法，而那种改变至今仍在塑造教室、报纸和公共生活。

questions.q: 1. What problem did hand-copied books have before the press?
options: Every family already held many identical books
A single shop could already stamp a page again and again
A scribe needed weeks or months, mistakes could travel into the next copy, and books were rare and costly
Writing and paper did not yet exist
questions.exp: 文中说手抄需要数周或数月，错误可能进入下一份，书又少又贵。

questions.q: 2. What was the heart of the printing invention?
options: A machine that invented writing and paper at the same time
Movable type that could be set, used, taken apart and set again, with ink and a firm press
A method that needed no skill and no checking of a first sheet
A rule that letters must never be arranged backward
questions.exp: 文中指出活字是核心：字母可排进托盘、使用后再拆开重排。

questions.q: 3. What waves of change followed cheaper, faster books?
options: More readers, fewer errors in drawings and maps, and news that travelled farther — which also meant false claims could spread more quickly
A demand for fewer books and fewer readers
Rulers who were always comfortable with every argument
A world that no longer needed careful readers
questions.exp: 文中说明更多书带来更多读者，图画错误更少，新闻走得更远，虚假说法也可能传得更快。

questions.q: 4. What did the press invent, according to the ending?
options: The first kind of writing and the first kind of paper
A textbook that cannot be printed
A world with no workers setting type
A way for writing to travel at the speed of a machine, which still shapes classrooms, newspapers and public life
questions.exp: 文中说印刷机没有发明书写或纸，而是发明了让书写以机器速度旅行的方法。

junior.title: 🗣️ Telling Family Stories at the Dinner Table
junior.content:
A family’s culture is not only in festivals and photographs. It also lives in the stories told at the table when the plates are still on the cloth. A grandparent may describe a first job, a long journey, or a funny mistake in the kitchen. A parent may tell how the street looked before the new buildings. Children may add a story from school. These ordinary tellings are a kind of living book. They cost nothing, and they can hold a family’s humour, values and memory more warmly than a silent meal.

The table is a good stage because people are already together and the time is limited, so stories stay short and vivid. Listeners can ask a question, which makes the tale richer than a recording that never pauses. Over years, the same story may be told again, with a new detail, and a younger child who was once only listening begins to tell it too. That is how a private history is passed on. Culture is not only what a museum keeps. It is also what a family chooses to remember out loud.

There is a gentle skill in this habit. Leave room for quieter people. Do not turn a story into a test or a lecture. If a memory is sad, it can be told with care, or saved for another time. Phones can wait, not because technology is bad, but because a face and a voice are the true medium of this art. A guest at the table is a gift: they may carry a story from another place, and your family story may travel home with them.

Students can start this culture with one question: “What happened at work or at school today?” or “How did you learn to cook this?” A notebook of favourite family tales, written later, can become a treasure, but the first job is to listen. Cultural life is happening in ordinary rooms, on ordinary evenings. If the stories stop, a family may still eat together, yet something shared and irreplaceable will have gone quiet.
junior.translation:
一个家庭的文化不仅仅在节日和照片里。它也活在盘子还在桌布上时、在餐桌上被讲述的那些故事里。一位祖父母也许会描述第一份工作、一次长途旅行，或厨房里一个好笑的错误。一位父母也许会讲新楼出现以前这条街的样子。孩子们也许会补上一个学校里的故事。这些平常的讲述是一种活着的书。它们不花钱，却可以比一顿沉默的饭，更温暖地装下一个家庭的幽默、价值和记忆。

桌子是一个好舞台，因为人们已经在一起，而时间是有限的，所以故事会保持短而生动。听的人可以问一个问题，这会让故事比一段从不暂停的录音更丰富。许多年里，同一个故事也许会被再讲一遍，带上一个新的细节，而一个曾经只是在听的更小的孩子，也开始讲它。家庭的私人历史就是这样被传下去的。文化不仅仅是博物馆所保存的东西。它也是一个家庭选择大声记住的东西。

这个习惯里有一种温和的技能。给更安静的人留出空间。不要把故事变成一次测验或一堂训话。如果一段记忆是悲伤的，它可以小心地被讲述，或留到另一个时候。手机可以等待，不是因为科技不好，而是因为一张脸和一个声音才是这门艺术真正的媒介。餐桌上的一位客人是一份礼物：他们也许带着另一个地方的故事，而你们的家庭故事也许会和他们一起回家。

学生可以用一个问题开始这种文化：“今天工作里或学校里发生了什么？”或“你是怎么学会做这道菜的？”一本稍后写下的、关于最喜爱的家庭故事的笔记本，可以成为一件珍宝，但第一项工作是倾听。文化生活正在平常的房间里、在平常的晚上发生。如果故事停了，一个家庭也许仍然一起吃饭，然而某种被共享、又不可替代的东西，就会已经安静下去。

questions.q: 1. Why does the passage call family stories at the table a living book?
options: Because they must be kept only in a museum
Because they are expensive to tell
Because children should never add a story from school
Because they can hold a family’s humour, values and memory more warmly than a silent meal
questions.exp: 文中说这些平常的讲述是活着的书，能比沉默的饭更温暖地装下幽默、价值和记忆。

questions.q: 2. Why is the table a good stage for these stories?
options: A recording that never pauses is always richer
A story must never be told again with a new detail
People are already together, time is limited so tales stay short, and listeners can ask questions
Younger children should only listen and never begin to tell
questions.exp: 文中说人们已在一起、时间有限所以故事短而生动，听者还可以提问。

questions.q: 3. What gentle skills belong to this habit?
options: Use the tale as a lecture every night
Leave room for quieter people, avoid turning a story into a test, tell sad memories with care, and let phones wait
Make technology the true medium instead of a face and a voice
Refuse any guest a chance to carry a story home
questions.exp: 文中建议给安静的人留空间，不把故事变成测验或训话，悲伤记忆要小心处理，手机可以等待。

questions.q: 4. What first job does the writer give students who want this culture?
options: Ask one kind question and listen, even if a notebook of tales is written later
Stop all stories so that something irreplaceable goes quiet
Eat together but never speak
Avoid ordinary evenings and ordinary rooms
questions.exp: 文中建议从一个问题开始，第一项工作是倾听，笔记本可稍后写。

junior.title: 🎫 Sitting in the Audience at a Live Performance
junior.content:
A recording can be paused, repeated and played in a bedroom. A live performance cannot. When you sit in an audience — at a school concert, a play, a dance, or a street show — the music or the scene happens only once, in the same air you are breathing. That shared risk is part of cultural life. A singer may hold a note a little longer, a dancer may nearly slip and then recover, and the room will feel it together. You are not only a consumer of art. You are part of the event.

Good audience habits protect that event. Arrive on time, or wait for a pause if you are late. Silence a phone and keep it dark. Do not talk through a quiet solo, and do not film the whole show in a way that blocks the person behind you. Applause has its moments; between them, attention is the gift you give. These manners are not cold rules. They are a way of saying to the performers, and to the strangers beside you, that the work matters.

Live art also teaches you to notice live people. The players have practised for weeks, and some may be as young as you. A kind face in the front rows can steady a nervous hand. After the final bow, a specific word — “the duet was beautiful,” “I loved the lighting” — is warmer than a rushed exit. If you can, thank a teacher or a volunteer who kept the door and the tickets. Culture is made by many roles, including the ones that never stand in the spotlight.

Students who go to performances, even small ones, build a richer inner library than a feed of short videos can offer. Try a kind of show you have not seen, and give it a fair twenty minutes before you decide. Then talk about it on the way home. Cultural life grows when more people are willing to sit still, listen hard, and be present for an hour that will not come again in exactly the same way.
junior.translation:
一段录音可以被暂停、重复，并在卧室里播放。一场现场演出不能。当你坐在观众席里——在学校音乐会、一出戏、一场舞蹈或一次街头表演上——音乐或场景只发生一次，就在你正在呼吸的同一片空气里。那种共享的风险是文化生活的一部分。一位歌手也许会把一个音多延长一点，一位舞者也许几乎滑倒然后又稳住，而整个房间会一起感觉到它。你不仅仅是艺术的消费者。你是这个事件的一部分。

好的观众习惯保护着这个事件。准时到达，如果迟到就等到一个停顿再进去。让手机关静音并保持屏幕黑暗。不要在安静的独奏里谈话，也不要以挡住后面的人的方式把整场都拍下来。掌声有它的时刻；在那些时刻之间，注意力是你给出的礼物。这些礼貌不是冰冷的规则。它们是一种对表演者、也对你身边的陌生人说“这项工作很重要”的方式。

现场艺术也教你去注意活着的人。演员已经练习了几周，有些也许和你一样年轻。前排一张善意的脸，可以稳住一只紧张的手。在最后的鞠躬之后，一句具体的话——“那段二重唱很美”，“我喜欢那些灯光”——比匆忙离开更温暖。如果可以，感谢一位守门和管票的老师或志愿者。文化是由许多角色做成的，包括那些从不站在聚光灯下的角色。

去看演出、即使是小小的演出的学生，会建立起一座比一串短视频更丰富的内心图书馆。试一种你还没有看过的演出，并在决定之前先给它公平的二十分钟。然后在回家的路上谈论它。当更多人愿意坐定、认真听，并出现在一个不会以完全相同的方式再来的小时里时，文化生活就会生长。

questions.q: 1. How is a live performance different from a recording?
options: It happens only once in the same air, with a shared risk, and the audience is part of the event
It can be paused and repeated in a bedroom like a file
The room never feels a longer note or a recovered slip together
You are only a consumer and never part of what happens
questions.exp: 文中说现场演出只发生一次，共享风险，观众是事件的一部分，而不能像录音那样暂停重复。

questions.q: 2. Which audience habits does the passage ask for?
options: Talk through every quiet moment and keep the screen bright
Film the whole show from a seat that blocks the person behind you
Give applause only, and never give attention
Arrive on time, silence the phone, do not talk through a quiet solo, and do not block others with filming
questions.exp: 文中要求准时或等到停顿再进，手机静音且屏幕暗，安静独奏时不交谈，拍摄不挡别人。

questions.q: 3. What kind word is warmer than a rushed exit after the bow?
options: No word at all, and no notice of nervous players
A remark only about the spotlight, never about a volunteer
A specific comment, such as ‘the duet was beautiful,’ and thanks to people who kept the door and the tickets
A face in the front rows that never looks kind
questions.exp: 文中说一句具体的话更温暖，并建议感谢守门和管票的老师或志愿者。

questions.q: 4. How can students grow a richer cultural life?
options: Replace every performance with a feed of short videos
Go to even small shows, try a new kind and give it a fair twenty minutes, then talk about it on the way home
Leave early and refuse to sit still or listen hard
Wait for an hour that will come again in exactly the same way
questions.exp: 文中建议即使是小演出也去，给没看过的类型公平的二十分钟，并在回家路上谈论。

junior.title: 👕 Why Wet Clothes Dry on a Line
junior.content:
Wet clothes on a line become dry without a machine that you can see, and that everyday fact is a small science lesson hanging in the air. The water does not vanish into nothing. It changes into vapour, a gas, and mixes with the air. This process is called evaporation. Wind, heat and dry air speed it up; cold, still and humid air slow it down. That is why a shirt dries faster on a breezy, sunny balcony than in a closed, damp bathroom, even if both places feel like “home.”

You can notice the variables in daily life. Spreading the clothes so that they do not overlap gives each surface more air. A thick towel takes longer than a thin scarf because there is more water to leave. If the air is already full of moisture, evaporation has less room to happen, which is why a rainy day is a poor drying day. The sun helps in two ways: it warms the cloth, and it can make the surrounding air hold more vapour. Science is not only in a lab beaker. It is on the washing line.

People use the same idea in other corners of the house. A wet mop dries when it is stood open, not left in a tight bucket. A spilled drop on a table disappears faster near a window. Hair dries more quickly when air moves across it. In some climates, families still prefer the line to a dryer because it uses the weather instead of extra electricity, and the cloth often smells of outdoor air. The choice is practical, and it is also a quiet experiment you repeat every week.

Students can test the idea with two identical cloths, one in a breeze and one in a cupboard, and feel them at the same time later. They can write which one dried first and why. Once you see evaporation at work, many ordinary puzzles become clearer, from a cooling cup of tea to a shrinking puddle after rain. Science lives in the clothes we wear, and in the air that slowly steals the water away.
junior.translation:
晾衣绳上的湿衣服会在没有一台你能看见的机器的情况下变干，这个日常事实，是挂在空气里的一堂小小的科学课。水并不是消失成了虚无。它变成水蒸气，一种气体，并和空气混合。这个过程叫做蒸发。风、热和干燥的空气会加快它；寒冷、静止和潮湿的空气会减慢它。这就是为什么一件衬衫在有风、晴朗的阳台上，比在一间封闭潮湿的浴室里干得更快，即使两个地方摸起来都像“家”。

你可以在日常生活里注意到这些变量。把衣服展开、不让它们重叠，会给每一面更多的空气。一条厚毛巾比一条薄围巾更久，因为要离开的水更多。如果空气里已经充满了湿气，蒸发就更少有空间发生，这就是为什么雨天是糟糕的晾晒日。太阳以两种方式帮忙：它温暖布料，也能让周围的空气容纳更多蒸气。科学不仅仅在实验室的烧杯里。它就在晾衣绳上。

人们在房子的其他角落里也使用同一个想法。一把湿拖把在被撑开立着时会干，而不是留在一只紧的桶里。桌上洒出的一滴，在靠近窗户时消失得更快。当空气从头发上吹过时，头发会干得更快。在一些气候里，家庭仍然更喜欢晾衣绳而不是烘干机，因为它使用天气而不是额外的电，布也常常带有户外空气的气味。这个选择是实际的，它也是你每周重复的一个安静实验。

学生可以用两块相同的布来测试这个想法，一块在风里，一块在橱柜里，稍后在同一时间摸摸它们。他们可以写下哪一块先干，以及为什么。一旦你看见蒸发在工作，许多平常的谜题就会变得更清楚，从一杯正在变凉的茶，到雨后一块缩小的水洼。科学活在我们穿的衣服里，也活在慢慢把水偷走的空气里。

questions.q: 1. What happens to the water when wet clothes dry on a line?
options: It vanishes into nothing and leaves no science behind
It changes into vapour and mixes with the air, in a process called evaporation
It only dries in a closed, damp bathroom, never on a breezy balcony
It needs a machine you can always see
questions.exp: 文中说水变成蒸气并与空气混合，这个过程叫做蒸发。

questions.q: 2. Which conditions speed drying, and which slow it?
options: Wind, heat and dry air speed it; cold, still and humid air slow it
Rainy air full of moisture always dries a shirt fastest
A thick towel always dries faster than a thin scarf
Overlapping clothes always give each surface more air
questions.exp: 文中明确风、热和干燥空气会加快，寒冷、静止和潮湿会减慢。

questions.q: 3. How does the sun help in two ways?
options: It only works inside a lab beaker
It stops families from using a line in any climate
It makes a wet mop dry faster inside a tight bucket
It warms the cloth, and it can make the surrounding air hold more vapour
questions.exp: 文中说太阳温暖布料，也能让周围空气容纳更多蒸气。

questions.q: 4. What simple test can students try?
options: Leave both cloths in the same closed space and invent no reason
Ignore puddles, tea and other everyday examples of evaporation
Compare two identical cloths, one in a breeze and one in a cupboard, and feel which dries first
Never write down which cloth dried first
questions.exp: 文中建议用两块相同的布，一块在风里一块在橱柜里，稍后同时触摸并写下结果。

junior.title: 🫖 How a Thermos Keeps a Drink Hot or Cold
junior.content:
A thermos can keep tea hot on a winter trip, or keep water cold on a summer walk, for hours. The trick looks like magic until you look at the science of heat. Heat always tends to move from a warmer place to a cooler one. If you want a drink to stay hot, you must slow that journey down. If you want it to stay cold, you must slow the arrival of heat from the outside. A good flask is a carefully built delay, not a machine that creates temperature from nothing.

Most thermos flasks use a double wall with a very thin space between the layers, often with the air pumped out. Heat travels in three ways: through a material, through moving air or liquid, and as radiation you can feel from a fire or a hot bulb. A vacuum, which is almost empty of air, blocks the first two paths very well. A silver inner surface reflects radiation and helps even more. A tight lid reduces the steam and air that would otherwise carry heat in or out at the top, which is often the weakest point.

Daily use follows from the design. Pre-warming or pre-cooling the bottle with a little hot or cold water can help. Do not leave the lid loose, and do not drop the flask, because a broken inner wall may quietly stop working. A thermos is not meant to sit on a fire or in a freezer as a shortcut. It keeps what you gave it; it does not cook or freeze. Understanding this saves disappointment and keeps the tool useful for years.

Students can compare a thermos with an ordinary cup, and measure which drink is still warm after half an hour. They can also feel how a metal mug loses heat faster than a thick ceramic one. Science in daily life is often the art of slowing a natural process just enough. The next time you open a flask and the tea is still steaming, you can thank a vacuum, a lid, and a long line of careful design.
junior.translation:
一只保温瓶可以在冬天的旅途里让茶保持热，或在夏天的步行里让水保持冷，长达几小时。这个把戏看起来像魔法，直到你看见关于热的科学。热总是倾向于从更暖的地方走向更凉的地方。如果你想让一杯饮料保持热，你就必须把那段路程减慢。如果你想让它保持冷，你就必须减慢从外面到来的热。一只好的瓶子是一个被小心建成的延迟，而不是一台从虚无中制造温度的机器。

大多数保温瓶使用双层壁，两层之间有非常薄的空间，常常把空气抽掉。热以三种方式旅行：通过一种材料，通过流动的空气或液体，以及作为你从火或热灯泡上能感觉到的辐射。几乎没有空气的真空，能很好地挡住前两条路。一层银色的内表面反射辐射，并提供更多帮助。一个严实的盖子减少本会在顶部把热带进或带出的蒸气和空气，而顶部常常是最弱的一点。

日常使用来自这种设计。用一点热水或冷水预先暖瓶或凉瓶，会有帮助。不要让盖子松着，也不要摔瓶子，因为破碎的内壁也许会悄悄地停止工作。保温瓶不是用来放在火上或放进冰柜当捷径的。它保持你给它的东西；它并不烹饪或冷冻。理解这一点可以减少失望，并让这件工具好用许多年。

学生可以把保温瓶和一只普通杯子比较，并测量半小时后哪一杯仍然暖。他们也可以感觉一只金属杯比一只厚陶瓷杯更快地失去热。日常生活里的科学，常常是刚好把一个自然过程减慢到足够的程度的艺术。下一次你打开瓶子、茶仍然冒着热气时，你可以感谢一道真空、一个盖子，以及一长串小心的设计。

questions.q: 1. What scientific tendency must a thermos slow down?
options: Heat never moves, so a drink stays hot by magic
A flask must always sit on a fire to stay useful
Heat tends to move from a warmer place to a cooler one, so the flask is a delay, not a machine that creates temperature from nothing
Cold drinks stay cold because heat cannot arrive from outside in any way
questions.exp: 文中说热总是从更暖处走向更凉处，保温瓶是精心建造的延迟，并不从虚无制造温度。

questions.q: 2. How does the double wall and vacuum help?
options: Heat travels in only one way, through a tight lid
A space with almost no air blocks heat travelling through material or moving air, and a silver surface reflects radiation
A vacuum fills the flask with moving air on purpose
The top is always the strongest point, so the lid does not matter
questions.exp: 文中说明热有三种传播方式，真空能挡住前两种，银色内表面反射辐射，严实盖子保护最弱的顶部。

questions.q: 3. What daily habits keep a thermos working?
options: Pre-warm or pre-cool it, keep the lid tight, and do not drop it or use it on a fire or in a freezer as a shortcut
Leave the lid loose and pack the flask on a fire
Ignore a broken inner wall
Expect the bottle to cook or freeze the drink by itself
questions.exp: 文中建议预热或预冷、盖严、不要摔，也不能把它当炉子或冰柜的捷径。

questions.q: 4. What comparison can students make at home?
options: Assume every cup keeps tea equally warm
Never measure which drink is still warm
Thank only magic, never a vacuum or a lid
Compare a thermos with an ordinary cup after half an hour, and feel how a metal mug loses heat faster than a thick ceramic one
questions.exp: 文中建议把保温瓶和普通杯比较半小时后的温度，并感受金属杯比厚陶瓷杯更快失热。

junior.title: 🛰️ How Satellites Help Us Watch the Weather
junior.content:
A weather forecast on a phone looks simple: a sun, a cloud, or a drop of rain. Behind that picture is a kind of exploration that never stops. Satellites circle the Earth and look down with cameras and sensors. They watch clouds grow, storms turn, ice melt, and temperature patterns change across whole oceans. From the ground we see only the sky above our town. From space, scientists can see the weather as a moving system, and that wider view has changed how we prepare for a day and for a danger.

A weather satellite does not feel the wind with a hand. It measures light, heat and microwave signals that bounce off clouds, rain and the surface below. Computers then turn those numbers into maps that forecasters can read. Some satellites stay over the same region, which is useful for watching a typhoon hour by hour. Others sweep around the planet in a lower path and build a global picture. This is exploration with patience: the same path, again and again, so that a change can be noticed.

The work helps ordinary life and urgent life. Farmers, pilots, ship crews and students checking an umbrella all use the result. Warnings of a heavy storm or a sudden flood can save lives if people trust them and move in time. The pictures also help scientists study a changing climate over years, which is a slower kind of exploration than a single voyage, but just as important. Tools this powerful still need careful humans, because a model can be wrong, and a warning must be clear.

Students can look at a satellite image of their region and compare it with the sky they see. They can learn the difference between a photo of clouds and a forecast, which is a prediction. Technology has not ended surprise in the weather, but it has made the atmosphere less of a mystery and more of a map. To explore is not only to travel outward. Sometimes it is to watch our own planet more closely, from a machine we sent to hang above it.
junior.translation:
手机上的天气预报看起来很简单：一个太阳，一朵云，或一滴雨。在那幅图画后面，是一种从不停止的探索。卫星环绕地球，并用相机和传感器向下看。它们观察云的生长、风暴的旋转、冰的融化，以及温度模式在整片海洋上的变化。从地面，我们只看见自己城镇上方的天空。从太空，科学家可以把天气看作一个移动的系统，而那种更宽的视野，已经改变了我们如何为一天、也为一种危险做准备。

一颗气象卫星并不用手去感觉风。它测量从云、雨和下面的表面弹回的光、热和微波信号。电脑随后把那些数字变成预报员能够阅读的地图。有些卫星停留在同一区域上空，这对一小时一小时地观察台风很有用。另一些在更低的轨道上扫过行星，并建立起一幅全球的图画。这是带着耐心的探索：同一条路径，一次又一次，好让一种变化能够被注意到。

这项工作帮助平常的生活，也帮助紧急的生活。农人、飞行员、船员，以及查看雨伞的学生，都在使用这个结果。如果人们信任并及时行动，关于一场大风暴或一次突然洪水的警告可以拯救生命。这些图像也帮助科学家研究多年来正在变化的气候，那是一种比单次航行更慢、却同样重要的探索。如此强大的工具仍然需要小心的人类，因为一个模型可能出错，而警告必须清楚。

学生可以看一张自己所在地区的卫星图像，并把它和他们看见的天空比较。他们可以学习云的照片和预报之间的差别，而预报是一种预测。科技并没有结束天气里的意外，但它已经让大气少了一些神秘，多了一张地图。探索不仅仅是向外旅行。有时它是更近地观察我们自己的行星，从一架我们送上去、挂在它上方的机器里。

questions.q: 1. What can weather satellites see that a person in a town cannot?
options: Only the sky above one town, with no wider view
The wind, by feeling it with a hand in space
A forecast that never uses cameras or sensors
Clouds, storms, ice and temperature patterns across whole oceans, as a moving system
questions.exp: 文中对比地面只见本镇天空，而卫星能看到整片海洋上的云、风暴、冰和温度模式。

questions.q: 2. How does a weather satellite gather its information?
options: It stays on the ground and guesses the typhoon
It never repeats a path, so change cannot be noticed
It measures light, heat and microwave signals that bounce off clouds, rain and the surface, and computers turn the numbers into maps
It refuses both a fixed region and a global sweep
questions.exp: 文中说明卫星测量弹回的光、热和微波信号，再由电脑变成地图。

questions.q: 3. Who can the work help in ordinary and urgent life?
options: Only scientists, never a person with an umbrella
Farmers, pilots, ship crews and students, and storm or flood warnings can save lives if people trust them
Nobody, because a model is never wrong
Only a single voyage, never a study of climate over years
questions.exp: 文中列举农人、飞行员、船员和学生，并指出可信而及时的警告能救命，也对气候的长期研究有帮助。

questions.q: 4. What difference should students learn when they look at a satellite image?
options: The difference between a photo of clouds and a forecast, which is a prediction
That technology has ended every surprise in the weather
That the atmosphere must remain only a mystery, never a map
That exploring can never mean watching our own planet more closely
questions.exp: 文中建议比较卫星图与眼前天空，并分清云的照片和作为预测的预报。

junior.title: 🔭 Looking Farther With a Telescope
junior.content:
Human eyes are excellent for a forest path, but they are small windows on the night sky. A telescope is a tool for looking farther. It uses lenses or mirrors to collect more light than the pupil can, and to bring a distant object into a clearer, larger image. With this instrument, a blur becomes a planet with rings, or a cloud of stars that no one could name with the naked eye. Exploration does not always mean a ship. Sometimes it means a deeper look from the ground we already stand on.

The idea grew over centuries. Early telescopes were simple tubes that still surprised their first users: mountains on the Moon, moons around another planet, and countless stars in a strip of the Milky Way. Later designs used bigger mirrors, darker sites, and cameras that can gather light for a long time. Today some telescopes sit on high mountains, and some fly in space above the blur of the air. Each improvement is a new kind of voyage, even if the astronomer stays in a chair.

A telescope also teaches patience and care. The sky appears to move, so the tool must be aimed and sometimes gently followed. City lights can wash out faint objects, which is why dark nights and dark places still matter. Students with a small telescope, or even binoculars, can start with the Moon’s shadows, a bright planet, or a star cluster. The first look may be shaky. The second look, with a steadier hand and a little knowledge of where to point, often feels like a door opening.

You do not need to become a professional to join this exploration. A library book or a reliable app can show what is visible tonight. Look with a friend, write what you saw, and remember that every famous picture of the cosmos began with someone deciding to look longer. Technology extends the eye, but wonder still begins in a person who is willing to stand still under a big sky and wait for the light to arrive.
junior.translation:
人的眼睛对于一条林间小路是出色的，但对于夜空，它们是小小的窗。望远镜是用来看得更远的工具。它用透镜或镜子收集比瞳孔更多的光，并把一个遥远的物体带进更清晰、更大的影像。有了这件仪器，一团模糊可以变成一颗带环的行星，或一团用肉眼谁也叫不出名字的星云。探索并不总是意味着一艘船。有时它意味着从我们已经站着的地面，看得更深。

这个想法在几个世纪里生长。早期的望远镜是简单的管子，却仍然让第一批使用者吃惊：月亮上的山，另一颗行星周围的卫星，以及银河一条带子里数不清的星。后来的设计使用更大的镜子、更暗的地点，以及可以长时间收集光的相机。今天有些望远镜坐在高山上，有些飞在空气的模糊之上的太空里。每一种改进都是一种新的航行，即使天文学家仍然坐在椅子上。

望远镜也教耐心和小心。天空看起来在移动，所以工具必须被瞄准，有时还要被轻轻跟随。城市的灯光可以洗掉微弱的物体，这就是为什么黑暗的夜和黑暗的地方仍然重要。拥有一架小望远镜、甚至一副双筒望远镜的学生，可以从月亮的阴影、一颗明亮的行星，或一个星团开始。第一次看也许会晃。第二次，手更稳一点，并稍微知道该指向哪里，常常感觉像一扇门正在打开。

你不必成为专业人士才能加入这种探索。一本图书馆的书或一个可靠的应用，可以显示今夜能看见什么。和一位朋友一起看，写下你看见的，并记住每一张关于宇宙的著名照片，都开始于某个人决定看得更久。科技延伸了眼睛，但惊奇仍然开始于一个愿意在一片大天空下站定、并等待光到来的人。

questions.q: 1. How does a telescope help us look farther?
options: It uses lenses or mirrors to collect more light than the pupil can, and to make a distant object clearer and larger
It shrinks a planet with rings into a blur the naked eye already sees
It always means leaving the ground on a ship
It collects less light than the human eye
questions.exp: 文中说望远镜用透镜或镜子收集比瞳孔更多的光，并把遥远物体带进更清晰更大的影像。

questions.q: 2. How has the tool improved over centuries?
options: By refusing cameras and staying only in bright cities
By ending all voyages, even for astronomers in chairs
By making the Milky Way show fewer stars than the first users saw
From simple tubes that showed mountains on the Moon, to bigger mirrors, darker sites, cameras, mountain observatories and telescopes in space
questions.exp: 文中回顾从简单管子看见月球山脉，到更大镜子、暗处、相机、高山与太空望远镜。

questions.q: 3. Why do dark nights and a steady aim still matter?
options: Binoculars can never show the Moon’s shadows or a star cluster
Patience and care are unnecessary once you have any tube
The sky appears to move, and city lights can wash out faint objects, so a first look may be shaky until you know where to point
A shaky first look means you should never try a second
questions.exp: 文中说明天空看起来在动，城市灯光会洗掉微弱物体，第二次更稳的观看才会像门打开。

questions.q: 4. How can a student join this exploration without becoming a professional?
options: Wait for wonder to begin only in a machine, never in a person
Use a book or a reliable app, look with a friend, write what you saw, and be willing to stand still and wait for the light
Avoid all library books and friends
Refuse to stand still under a big sky
questions.exp: 文中说不必成为专业人士，可用书或可靠应用，和朋友一起看并写下所见，惊奇始于愿意站定等待的人。

junior.title: ❄️ Why Ice Floats, and Why That Helps Living Things
junior.content:
Most solid things sink in their own liquid: a lump of iron falls through molten iron in a workshop thought-experiment, and a candle of wax sinks a little as it melts in a special test. Water is different, and that difference matters to nature. When water freezes, its molecules settle into a spacious crystal. The ice takes up more room than the same amount of liquid water, so it is less dense, and it floats. A pond therefore freezes from the top down, not from the bottom up.

This odd fact is a gift to living things. A floating lid of ice shelters the water below from the hardest cold and from the wind. Fish, insects and plants can survive in the liquid layer, sometimes all winter, instead of being locked in a solid block from the bed of the pond.
