In oceans, floating ice also changes how light and heat move, and it gives some animals a place to rest. If ice sank, the world’s waters would freeze in a very different, much harsher way, and many of the habitats we know would not exist.

You can see the science in a simple glass. Ice cubes rise. A full bottle of water left in a deep freeze may crack, because the ice needs more space. On a lake, the ice groans as it expands. Scientists measure density by comparing mass and volume; the numbers confirm what the eye already notices on a winter day. Nature and science meet in a property so ordinary that we forget to be surprised, until we imagine the opposite world.

Students can float an ice cube and then watch it melt, measuring the water line if they are careful. They can also ask why a frozen pipe is a problem in a house, which is the same expansion in a place we do not want it. Understanding ice is not only a winter curiosity. It is a way of seeing that a small fact about a molecule can shape a whole season of life under a white, quiet surface.
junior.translation:
大多数固体在它们自己的液体里会下沉：在一个思想实验里，一块铁会穿过熔化的铁落下，而一只蜡做的蜡烛在特殊试验里熔化时也会略微下沉。水是不同的，而那种不同对自然很重要。当水结冰时，它的分子会安顿进一种宽敞的晶体。这些冰比同量的液态水占据更多空间，所以密度更小，于是它浮着。因此一个池塘会从上往下结冰，而不是从底部往上。

这个奇怪的事实是给生命的一份礼物。一层浮着的冰盖保护下面的水，使它免受最硬的寒冷和风。鱼、昆虫和植物可以在那层液体里存活，有时是整整一个冬天，而不是从塘底起被锁进一整块固体里。在海洋里，浮冰也改变光和热的移动方式，并给一些动物一个休息的地方。如果冰会下沉，世界的水会以一种非常不同、也严酷得多的方式结冰，而我们所知道的许多栖息地就不会存在。

你可以在一只简单的杯子里看见这门科学。冰块会升起。一瓶装满的水在深度冷冻里可能会裂，因为冰需要更多空间。在湖上，冰在膨胀时会发出声响。科学家通过比较质量和体积来测量密度；这些数字证实了眼睛在冬日里已经注意到的事。自然和科学，在一种普通到我们忘了去吃惊的性质里相遇，直到我们想象相反的世界。

学生可以让一颗冰块浮着，然后看它融化，如果小心的话还可以测量水位。他们也可以问为什么房子里结冰的管道会成为问题，那是同一场我们并不想要它发生之处的膨胀。理解冰不仅仅是一种冬天的好奇。它是一种看见的方式：一个关于分子的小事实，可以塑造在一层洁白而安静的表面之下的整个季节的生命。

questions.q: 1. Why does ice float on water?
options: Ice is always denser than liquid water, so it should sink
Freezing water forms a spacious crystal that takes up more room, so the ice is less dense than liquid water
A pond freezes from the bottom up because ice is heavy
Molecules pack tighter in ice than in liquid water, with less room
questions.exp: 文中说结冰时分子形成宽敞晶体，占用更多空间，密度更小，所以会浮，池塘从上往下结冰。

questions.q: 2. How does floating ice help living things in a pond?
options: The lid of ice shelters the water below, so fish, insects and plants can survive in a liquid layer instead of a solid block
It locks every creature in ice from the bed of the pond upward
It has no effect on wind or the hardest cold
It only matters in a glass of cubes, never in nature
questions.exp: 文中说明浮着的冰盖庇护下面的水，生命可以在液体层里过冬，而不是被整块冻住。

questions.q: 3. What everyday signs of this science does the passage mention?
options: Density cannot be measured by mass and volume
A frozen pipe in a house is never related to expansion
The eye notices nothing on a winter day
Ice cubes rise, a full frozen bottle may crack, and lake ice groans as it expands
questions.exp: 文中举例冰块升起、装满的瓶子在冷冻中可能裂开，以及湖冰膨胀时发出声响。

questions.q: 4. What can students do to see the idea for themselves?
options: Ignore the water line and the molecule’s small fact
Treat ice as only a curiosity with no link to a season of life
Float an ice cube, watch it melt, and ask why a frozen pipe is a problem in a house
Imagine no opposite world, and ask no questions
questions.exp: 文中建议让冰块浮着再看它融化，并思考家中冻裂管道是同一场膨胀。

junior.title: 🌱 How a Quiet Seed Begins to Grow
junior.content:
A seed can look lifeless: small, dry, and still. Inside, however, is a plant in waiting, with a tiny root and leaf already formed, and a store of food packed around them. When the seed begins to grow, we call the first stage germination. It is one of the quiet wonders of nature and science, because the start depends on conditions, not on a wish. Water, a suitable temperature, and, for many seeds, a little air in the soil must all be present. Then the coat softens, the food store is used, and a root typically pushes down before a shoot finds the light.

Different seeds wait for different signals. Some need a cold period, as if winter must be proved. Some have a hard coat that must be worn or cracked. Some stay dormant in a dry packet for years and then wake in a single wet week. This variety is a survival design. If every seed in a dry land grew after one short rain, a second dry spell could kill them all. Nature staggers the risk. Science studies these signals so that farmers and gardeners can choose the right time and the right treatment.

You can watch the process in a jar with damp paper and a few beans. In days, a root appears, then a hook of stem, then pale leaves that green when they meet the light. The bean does not eat soil at this stage; it lives on its inner store until the leaves can begin to make food. That is why a seed planted too deep may run out of energy before it reaches the sun, and why a seed kept bone-dry will not start at all.

Students who grow one bean on a window and keep a diary of dates, water and height are already doing science. They can compare a warm windowsill with a colder one, or a dark cupboard with the light, and write what changed. A quiet seed is not empty. It is a plan, waiting for the world to say that it is time.
junior.translation:
一粒种子看起来可能没有生命：小小的，干的，静止的。然而在里面，是一株等待中的植物，已有细小的根和叶形成，周围还包着一份食物储备。当种子开始生长，我们把最初的阶段叫做萌发。它是自然和科学里安静的奇迹之一，因为开始取决于条件，而不是愿望。水、适宜的温度，以及对许多种子来说，土壤里的一点空气，必须同时存在。然后种皮变软，食物储备被使用，通常是根先向下推，然后芽才去寻找光。

不同的种子等待不同的信号。有些需要一段寒冷，仿佛冬天必须被证明。有些有必须被磨损或裂开的硬壳。有些在干燥的袋子里休眠许多年，然后在单独一个潮湿的星期里醒来。这种多样性是一种生存设计。如果干旱土地里的每一粒种子都在一场短雨之后生长，第二次干旱就可能把它们全部杀死。自然把风险错开。科学研究这些信号，好让农人和园丁可以选择恰当的时间和恰当的处理。

你可以在一个罐子里，用潮湿的纸和几粒豆子观看这个过程。几天里，根会出现，然后是一截钩状的茎，然后是苍白的叶子，它们在遇见光时变绿。豆子在这个阶段并不吃土壤；它靠里面的储备生活，直到叶子可以开始制造食物。这就是为什么种得太深的种子，也许在到达太阳之前就会耗尽能量，以及为什么一粒保持极干的种子根本不会开始。

在窗边种一粒豆子、并记下日期、水和高度的学生，已经在做科学了。他们可以比较温暖的窗台和更冷的窗台，或黑暗的橱柜和亮处，并写下什么改变了。一粒安静的种子并不是空的。它是一个计划，正等待世界宣布：时间到了。

questions.q: 1. What does a seed need before germination typically begins?
options: Only a wish, with no conditions
Light first, before any root or food store is used
Water, a suitable temperature, and, for many seeds, a little air in the soil
A bone-dry packet and no softening of the coat
questions.exp: 文中说开始取决于条件：水、适宜温度，以及许多种子还需要土壤中的一点空气。

questions.q: 2. Why do different seeds wait for different signals?
options: Every seed in a dry land should grow after one short rain
The variety is a survival design, so that one short rain does not cause every seed to grow and then die in a second dry spell
Farmers and gardeners should ignore the right time and treatment
A cold period or a hard coat is never useful
questions.exp: 文中说明多样性是生存设计，避免一场短雨后全部萌发又被第二次干旱杀死。

questions.q: 3. What can you see when beans germinate on damp paper?
options: A root, then a hook of stem, then pale leaves that green in the light, living on the inner store at this stage
The bean eating soil immediately, with no inner store
A seed planted very deep always reaching the sun with energy to spare
No root appearing before a shoot
questions.exp: 文中描述根先出现，再是钩状茎和遇光变绿的叶，此阶段靠内部储备生活。

questions.q: 4. How can students turn one bean into a science diary?
options: Write nothing about what changed
Treat the seed as empty, with no plan inside
Grow the bean with no observations at all
Record dates, water and height, and compare a warm windowsill with a colder one, or dark with light
questions.exp: 文中建议记录日期、水和高度，并比较温暖与寒冷窗台，或黑暗与亮处。

junior.title: 🪥 Why Brushing Your Teeth Is Worth Two Minutes
junior.content:
Two minutes with a toothbrush can seem long when you are sleepy or late. Yet this small habit protects more than a smile in a photograph. After meals, bits of food and a film of bacteria stay on the teeth. The bacteria can produce acids that slowly wear the hard surface, and the gums can become sore if the film is left for days. Brushing morning and night, and cleaning between the teeth when you can, is a health habit that prevents pain that is much longer than two minutes.

The method matters as much as the time. Use a soft brush and a small amount of toothpaste with fluoride, unless a dentist has told you otherwise. Angle the brush toward the gum and use short, gentle strokes, not a hard scrub that can harm the gums. Include the inside surfaces and the back teeth, which are easy to skip. Spit, and do not rinse with a lot of water at once if you want a little toothpaste to keep working. Replace the brush when the bristles spread. A worn brush is like a broom that no longer sweeps.

Sugar and sips of sweet drinks through the day give the bacteria more fuel, so the habit also includes choosing water between meals and not going to bed with juice on the teeth. A dentist’s visit is not a substitute for the daily work, but it can catch a small problem early. If brushing hurts, or if gums bleed often, tell an adult; the answer may be a gentler method, not a reason to stop.

Students can set a two-minute song or a timer so that the habit has a clear shape. They can keep the brush where it is hard to forget, and they can help a younger sibling learn the same routine without turning it into a fight. Healthy teeth help you eat, speak and sleep without pain. The two minutes are not a decoration in the day. They are a quiet investment in a body you will need for a long time.
junior.translation:
当你困倦或要迟到时，用牙刷的两分钟可能显得很长。然而这个小习惯保护的不只是照片里的一个微笑。饭后，食物残渣和一层细菌会留在牙齿上。细菌可以产生慢慢磨损坚硬表面的酸，如果这层膜被留下好几天，牙龈也可能变得疼痛。早晚刷牙，并在可以的时候清洁牙缝，是一种健康习惯，它能防止比两分钟长得多的疼痛。

方法和时间同样重要。使用软毛牙刷和少量含氟的牙膏，除非牙医另有告诉。把牙刷斜向牙龈，用短而轻的动作，而不是可能伤害牙龈的用力刷。包括内侧和后牙，那些地方很容易被跳过。把泡沫吐掉，如果你想让一点点牙膏继续起作用，就不要立刻用大量水漱口。当刷毛张开时更换牙刷。一把用旧的牙刷，像一把不再扫地的扫帚。

糖和一天里一口口的甜饮料给细菌更多燃料，所以这个习惯也包括在两餐之间选择水，以及不带着牙齿上的果汁去睡觉。看牙医不能代替每天的工作，但它可以及早发现一个小问题。如果刷牙疼痛，或牙龈常常出血，就告诉成年人；答案也许是一种更轻的方法，而不是停止的理由。

学生可以设定一首两分钟的歌或一个计时器，好让这个习惯有清楚的形状。他们可以把牙刷放在不容易忘记的地方，并可以帮助更小的兄弟姐妹学习同样的例行，而不把它变成一场争吵。健康的牙齿帮助你吃饭、说话和睡觉时不疼痛。这两分钟不是一天里的装饰。它们是对一具你将需要很久的身体的安静投资。

questions.q: 1. Why is the two-minute habit worth more than a smile in a photograph?
options: Because bits of food never stay on the teeth after meals
Because brushing once a month is enough to protect the gums
Because the habit only matters in pictures
Because bacteria can produce acids that wear the teeth, and gums can become sore if the film is left, so brushing prevents much longer pain
questions.exp: 文中说细菌产生的酸会磨损牙面，膜留下数天牙龈会痛，刷牙能防止比两分钟长得多的疼痛。

questions.q: 2. Which method details does the passage recommend?
options: A hard scrub that can harm the gums, and skipping the back teeth
Rinsing with a lot of water at once if you want the toothpaste to keep working
A soft brush, a little fluoride toothpaste, short gentle strokes toward the gum, including inside and back teeth
Keeping a brush after the bristles have spread
questions.exp: 文中建议软毛、少量含氟牙膏、斜向牙龈的短而轻的动作，并刷到内侧和后牙。

questions.q: 3. What other choice supports the brushing habit?
options: Sip sweet drinks through the day to fuel the bacteria
Choose water between meals, and do not go to bed with juice on the teeth
Treat a dentist’s visit as a full substitute for daily brushing
Stop brushing if gums bleed, without telling an adult
questions.exp: 文中建议两餐之间选择水，不要带着牙齿上的果汁睡觉；牙医不能代替每天的工作。

questions.q: 4. How can students give the habit a clear shape?
options: Use a two-minute song or timer, keep the brush where it is hard to forget, and help a younger sibling learn the routine kindly
Treat the two minutes as only a decoration in the day
Turn the routine into a fight at the sink
Forget that healthy teeth help you eat, speak and sleep
questions.exp: 文中建议用两分钟的歌或计时器，把牙刷放在不易忘记的地方，并善意地帮助弟弟妹妹。

junior.title: 👀 Giving Your Eyes a Rest From the Screen
junior.content:
Study, messages and videos can keep a student’s eyes on a screen for hours. The light is useful, and the work may be necessary, but the body was not designed to stare at a close, bright rectangle without a break. Eyes may feel dry, tired or sore, and a headache can follow. A healthy life includes a simple rest habit: look away, blink, and give the muscles that focus on near work a chance to relax. The goal is not to throw the device away. The goal is to use it in a way the eyes can stand day after day.

A popular pattern is to look at something farther away, about six metres, for twenty seconds after twenty minutes of close work, and to blink on purpose, because people blink less when they stare. The exact numbers can vary, but the idea is regular and short, not one long rest after the damage is done. The room should not be the only bright thing in a dark cave, and the screen should not face a harsh reflection. A slightly lower brightness and a larger font can also reduce the strain. If you wear glasses, keep the prescription up to date.

The rest is more effective when the whole body joins it. Stand up, stretch the neck and shoulders, and let the eyes look out of a window if you can. Outdoor light in the daytime is helpful for growing eyes, so a walk after class is not only for the legs. Sleep matters too: tired eyes on a late-night screen often feel worse the next morning. If pain continues, or if the board at school looks unclear, tell an adult and see an eye doctor. A habit cannot fix every problem, but it can prevent some of them.

Students can set a gentle reminder, or use the end of a chapter as a cue to look into the distance. Friends can remind one another without nagging. Healthy living is made of these small protections, repeated until they feel normal. Your eyes have to last. A few pauses in a long evening of study are a fair price for seeing the world clearly tomorrow.
junior.translation:
学习、消息和视频可以让学生的眼睛在屏幕上停留几个小时。光是有用的，工作也许是必要的，但身体并不是被设计来不间断地盯着一块近而亮的长方形的。眼睛可能感到干燥、疲倦或酸痛，随后还可能出现头痛。健康的生活包括一个简单的休息习惯：看向别处，眨眼，并给那些聚焦近处工作的肌肉一次放松的机会。目标不是把设备扔掉。目标是以眼睛能够日复一日承受的方式使用它。

一种流行的模式是，在二十分钟的近处工作之后，看向大约六米外的某物二十秒，并有意地眨眼，因为人们在盯着看时眨眼会更少。确切的数字可以不同，但想法是规律而短暂的，而不是在损害已经造成之后才一次长休息。房间不应当是黑暗洞穴里唯一明亮的东西，屏幕也不应当对着刺眼的反光。稍低的亮度和更大的字体也可以减轻负担。如果你戴眼镜，就让度数保持更新。

当整个身体也加入时，休息会更有效。站起来，伸展颈和肩，如果可以，就让眼睛望向窗外。白天的户外光对正在生长的眼睛有帮助，所以课后的一次步行不仅仅是为了腿。睡眠也重要：在深夜屏幕上疲倦的眼睛，第二天早晨常常感觉更糟。如果疼痛继续，或学校里的黑板看起来不清楚，就告诉成年人并去看眼科医生。一个习惯不能修好每一个问题，但它可以防止其中的一些。

学生可以设定一个温和的提醒，或把一章的结束当作看向远处的信号。朋友可以在不唠叨的情况下互相提醒。健康的生活，就是由这些被重复到感觉正常的小小保护组成的。你的眼睛必须持久。在一个漫长的学习夜晚里的几次停顿，是为了明天清楚地看见世界而付的公平价格。

questions.q: 1. Why do eyes need rest from a long time on a screen?
options: The body was not designed to stare at a close, bright rectangle without a break, and eyes may feel dry, tired or sore
The light is never useful and all work on a screen is unnecessary
The only solution is to throw the device away forever
Headaches never follow tired eyes
questions.exp: 文中说身体不是被设计来不间断盯着近而亮的长方形的，眼睛可能干燥酸痛并伴随头痛。

questions.q: 2. What popular rest pattern does the passage describe?
options: One long rest only after the damage is done, with no short breaks
Sit in a dark cave with the screen as the only bright thing, facing a harsh reflection
Use the smallest font and the highest brightness to reduce strain
After about twenty minutes of close work, look about six metres away for twenty seconds, and blink on purpose
questions.exp: 文中介绍约二十分钟近工作后看向约六米外二十秒，并有意眨眼，同时注意光线与反光。

questions.q: 3. How can the rest be more effective for the whole body?
options: Stay still and use a late-night screen until the morning feels worse
Ignore a board that looks unclear and never tell an adult
Stand, stretch, look out of a window if you can, get daytime outdoor light, and sleep well
Assume a habit can fix every eye problem without a doctor
questions.exp: 文中建议站起来伸展，望向窗外，白天户外光有益，并重视睡眠；持续疼痛要告诉成人。

questions.q: 4. How can students remember to pause?
options: Treat pauses in a long evening of study as a waste
Set a gentle reminder, or use the end of a chapter as a cue, and let friends remind one another without nagging
Refuse all small protections until they feel abnormal
Forget that eyes have to last until tomorrow
questions.exp: 文中建议设定温和提醒，或把一章结束当作看向远处的信号，朋友也可不唠叨地互提。

junior.title: 🌫️ Why You Can See Your Breath on a Cold Day
junior.content:
On a cold morning, a small cloud appears in front of your mouth when you breathe out, and then it fades. The cloud is not smoke, and it is not magic. It is a simple piece of science you can see in the street. The air you exhale is warm and holds a lot of water as an invisible vapour. When that warm, moist air meets cold air outside, it cools quickly. Cool air cannot hold as much vapour, so some of the water changes into tiny liquid droplets. The droplets scatter light, and you see a mist.

The same idea appears in other ordinary places. A bathroom mirror fogs after a hot shower because warm, wet air meets a cooler glass. A glass of ice water gathers beads on the outside as water from the room’s air condenses. In winter, a window may show a pattern of droplets or frost. Clouds in the sky form when moist air rises, cools, and cannot keep all of its vapour as a gas. Your visible breath is a tiny, private cloud, made at mouth height for a second or two.

Temperature and humidity change the show. On a dry, mild day you may see nothing, even though you are still breathing out water. On a very cold day the cloud is thick and lingers. If you wear a scarf, the mist may appear at the edge of the cloth. Science common sense is often the habit of asking “where did the water come from, and why did it become visible here?” once you know that cooling can turn vapour into droplets.

Students can compare breaths in a warm room and by an open winter window, or watch a cold bottle come out of a fridge. They should not confuse this mist with the grey air of pollution, which is a different problem and not a reason to fear their own breath. A cold-day cloud in front of your face is a reminder that the air is a mixture, that water can hide in it, and that a change of temperature can make the hidden suddenly seen.
junior.translation:
在一个寒冷的早晨，当你呼气时，嘴前会出现一小团云，然后它又散去。那团云不是烟，也不是魔法。它是你可以在街上看见的一份简单的科学。你呼出的空气是温暖的，并作为看不见的蒸气包含着许多水。当那些温暖、潮湿的空气遇到外面的冷空气时，它会迅速变凉。冷空气不能容纳同样多的蒸气，于是一些水变成细小的液滴。这些液滴散射光，于是你看见一层雾。

同一个想法也出现在其他平常的地方。热淋浴之后，浴室的镜子会起雾，因为温暖潮湿的空气遇到了更凉的玻璃。一杯冰水会在外侧聚集水珠，那是房间空气里的水在凝结。冬天，窗户上可能出现液滴或霜的图案。天上的云，是在潮湿空气上升、变凉、并且不能再把全部蒸气保持为气体时形成的。你看得见的呼吸，是一团小小的、私人的云，在嘴巴的高度被做成一两秒。

温度和湿度会改变这场表演。在干燥、温和的日子里，你也许什么也看不见，即使你仍然在呼出水。在非常冷的日子里，这团云又厚，也停留得更久。如果你围着围巾，雾也许会出现在布的边缘。科学常识常常是这样一种习惯：一旦你知道冷却可以把蒸气变成液滴，就问“水从哪里来，以及它为什么在这里变得可见？”

学生可以比较在温暖房间里和在打开的冬天窗户旁的呼吸，或看着一只冷瓶子从冰箱里拿出来。他们不应当把这层雾和污染的灰色空气搞混，那是一个不同的问题，也不是害怕自己呼吸的理由。你面前一团冷天的云，是一个提醒：空气是一种混合物，水可以藏在里面，而温度的一次变化，可以让隐藏的东西突然被看见。

questions.q: 1. What is the small cloud you see when you breathe out on a cold day?
options: Smoke from the lungs, or a kind of magic
Warm, moist air meets cold air, some vapour turns into tiny droplets, and the droplets scatter light
Dry air that holds no water at all
A cloud that never fades
questions.exp: 文中解释呼出的暖湿空气遇到冷空气后，部分蒸气变成散射光的细小液滴。

questions.q: 2. Which other ordinary examples follow the same idea?
options: A fogged bathroom mirror, beads on a cold glass, winter window droplets or frost, and clouds in the sky
A glass of ice water that never gathers beads
Clouds that form when air gets warmer and holds more vapour as a gas
A breath cloud that lasts for hours at mouth height
questions.exp: 文中列举浴室镜起雾、冰水杯外壁水珠、冬窗上的液滴或霜，以及空气上升变凉形成的云。

questions.q: 3. Why might you see no cloud on a dry, mild day?
options: You stop breathing out water on mild days
A scarf always hides every trace of mist
Science common sense says cooling never turns vapour into droplets
Temperature and humidity change the show; you are still breathing out water, but less of it becomes visible
questions.exp: 文中说温度和湿度会改变现象，干燥温和的日子里即使仍在呼出水也可能看不见。

questions.q: 4. What should students not confuse this mist with?
options: A cold bottle coming out of a fridge, which can never show condensation
The idea that water can hide in a mixture of air

A change of temperature that makes the hidden suddenly seen

junior.title: 🚿 Saving Water at Home, One Tap at a Time
junior.content:
Clean water from a tap feels endless when it is always there, but it is not. It has been collected, cleaned, pumped and sometimes carried a long way, and in many places it is already scarce. Saving water at home is a form of nature care that students can practise every day. It is not a grand speech about a distant river only. It is the shorter shower, the tap closed while you soap your hands or brush your teeth, and the full load of washing instead of two half-empty ones. Small actions, repeated, protect a resource that plants, animals and people all need.

Leaks are quiet thieves. A dripping tap can waste a surprising amount in a month, and a running toilet can waste even more. Reporting a leak to an adult, and not ignoring the sound, is part of the habit. In the kitchen, wash vegetables in a bowl and use the water for plants if it is clean enough. In the garden, water in the cooler evening so that less is lost to the air, and give the roots a deep drink rather than a daily sprinkle that never sinks. Care is a kind of attention: where is the water going, and is that journey necessary?

Schools can join in with the same eyes: taps that shut firmly, signs that remind, and a quick report when a fountain runs without pause. The point is not to make anyone afraid of washing. Health still needs clean hands and clean clothes. The point is to match the amount to the need, and to treat water as precious even when the bill is paid by someone else. Nature is not only a forest in a book. It is also the reservoir that feeds your street.

Students can do a simple home check for a week: notice how often a tap runs when no one is using the water, and change one habit on purpose. Share the idea without shaming the family, because change is easier when it feels like a team. Protecting nature includes protecting water, and protecting water can begin at the nearest tap, today.
junior.translation:
当水龙头里的干净水总是在那里时，它感觉像是无穷的，其实并不是。它已经被收集、清洁、泵送，有时还被输送了很长的路，而在许多地方，它已经稀缺。在家里节约用水，是学生每天都可以练习的一种自然照料。它不仅仅是关于一条遥远河流的盛大演说。它是更短的淋浴，是在打肥皂或刷牙时关上的龙头，是一次满载的洗涤，而不是两次半空的洗涤。被重复的小行动，保护着植物、动物和人都需要的一种资源。

漏水是安静的小偷。一个滴水的龙头可以在一个月里浪费惊人的量，而一个不停流水的马桶可能浪费得更多。向成年人报告漏水，并且不忽视那个声音，是这个习惯的一部分。在厨房里，在一只碗里洗蔬菜，如果水足够干净，就用它来浇植物。在园子里，在更凉的晚间浇水，好让更少的水消失在空气里，并给根一次深深的喝水，而不是一次从不下沉的每日浅洒。照料是一种注意：水正在去哪里，以及那段路程是否必要？

学校可以用同样的眼睛加入：关得紧的龙头，提醒的标牌，以及当一座饮泉不停流水时的迅速报告。重点不是让任何人害怕清洗。健康仍然需要干净的手和干净的衣服。重点是让用量匹配需要，并且即使账单由别人支付，也把水当作珍贵的。自然不仅仅是书里的一片森林。它也是供给你那条街的水库。

学生可以用一周做一次简单的家庭检查：注意龙头有多少次在没有人用水时还开着，并有意地改变一个习惯。在不让家里人羞愧的情况下分享这个想法，因为当它感觉像一个团队时，改变会更容易。保护自然包括保护水，而保护水可以从今天、从最近的那个龙头开始。

questions.q: 1. Why is tap water not endless, even when it always seems to be there?
options: It appears in the tap from nowhere, with no link to nature
Only a distant river needs care, never a shorter shower or a closed tap while you soap your hands
It has been collected, cleaned, pumped and sometimes carried a long way, and in many places it is already scarce
Small actions at home cannot protect a resource that living things need

questions.q: 2. Why are leaks called quiet thieves?
options: A leak should be ignored if the sound is small
A dripping tap or a running toilet can waste a large amount, so reporting the sound to an adult is part of the habit
Kitchen and garden habits cannot save any water
A daily sprinkle that never sinks is the best way to water roots
questions.exp: 文中说滴水的龙头和不停流水的马桶可能浪费惊人，向成人报告是习惯的一部分。

questions.q: 3. What is the point of saving water at school and at home?
options: To match the amount to the need, and to treat water as precious, without becoming afraid of washing for health

To let a fountain run without pause as a reminder
To care only when you personally pay the bill
questions.exp: 文中强调重点不是害怕清洗，而是让用量匹配需要，即使账单由别人付也把水当作珍贵。

senior.title: 🌊 The Ocean as Earth’s Climate Engine
senior.content:
The ocean covers more than 70 percent of our planet’s surface, yet many people still think of it mainly as a place for swimming or fishing. In reality, the ocean is one of the most powerful climate regulators on Earth. 🔬

Ocean currents, driven by wind, temperature differences and the Earth’s rotation, move huge amounts of heat around the globe. Warm water travels from the equator toward the poles, while cold water returns toward the tropics. This continuous circulation helps keep temperatures in many regions moderate and stable. Without it, some places would be much hotter and others much colder.

The ocean also absorbs a large share of the carbon dioxide that human activities release into the atmosphere. Phytoplankton — tiny plant-like organisms floating near the surface — take in carbon during photosynthesis. When they die, some of that carbon sinks to the deep ocean, where it can remain locked away for centuries. In this way, the ocean acts as a giant carbon sink that slows the pace of global warming.

However, this vital system is under growing pressure. Rising temperatures cause seawater to expand and ice sheets to melt, contributing to sea-level rise. Warmer water holds less oxygen and can harm coral reefs and other marine ecosystems. At the same time, the ocean’s ability to absorb extra carbon is not unlimited; as it takes in more CO₂, the water becomes more acidic, threatening shellfish and the food chains that depend on them.

Understanding these processes is essential if we want to mitigate climate change. Protecting marine ecosystems, reducing greenhouse-gas emissions and supporting sustainable fishing are all part of the solution. The ocean is not just a beautiful blue landscape — it is a dynamic engine that helps keep our planet livable. The more we learn about it, the clearer it becomes that caring for the ocean means caring for ourselves. 🌍

The same currents that help regulate regional temperatures are also a reminder that climate is not only an atmospheric phenomenon. A change in one basin can travel, over months or years, into weather far from the shore. Coastal cities, fishing communities and low-lying islands are especially vulnerable when the system is disturbed. Sea-level rise is not an abstract chart; it is a practical consequence for homes, ports and farmland.

Because the ocean’s work is mostly invisible, it is easy to delay action until the damage is obvious. That delay itself has a cost. If we want the climate engine to keep running in our favour, we have to treat marine protection as climate policy, not as a separate hobby. Reducing emissions, guarding wetlands that buffer storms, and restoring damaged reefs are ways of paying attention to a system that has been quietly supporting us for a very long time.

Students can begin with a map of a major current and a simple question: who depends on it? The more clearly we see the links, the harder it becomes to think of the sea as only a holiday view. Caring for this engine is part of caring for the climate we will live with.
senior.translation:
海洋覆盖了地球表面超过70%的面积，但许多人仍主要把它当作游泳或钓鱼的地方。实际上，海洋是地球上最强大的气候调节器之一。🔬

由风、温度差异和地球自转驱动的洋流，在全球范围内输送着大量热量。温暖的海水从赤道流向两极，而冷水则返回热带。这种持续的循环有助于使许多地区的温度保持温和稳定。如果没有它，有些地方会热得多，另一些地方则冷得多。

海洋还吸收了人类活动释放到大气中的大量二氧化碳。浮游植物——漂浮在表层的微小植物样生物——在光合作用过程中吸收碳。当它们死亡后，部分碳会沉入深海，并可能在那里封存数百年。这样，海洋就像一个巨大的碳汇，减缓了全球变暖的速度。

然而，这个至关重要的系统正承受着越来越大的压力。气温上升导致海水膨胀、冰盖融化，从而加剧海平面上升。温暖的海水含氧量更低，并可能伤害珊瑚礁和其他海洋生态系统。同时，海洋吸收额外碳的能力并非无限；随着它吸收更多二氧化碳，海水会变得更酸，威胁贝类以及依赖它们的食物链。

如果我们想缓解气候变化，理解这些过程至关重要。保护海洋生态系统、减少温室气体排放、支持可持续捕捞，都是解决方案的一部分。海洋不仅仅是美丽的蓝色风景——它是帮助维持我们星球宜居的动力引擎。我们对它了解得越多，就越清楚：关爱海洋就是关爱我们自己。🌍

同样帮助调节区域温度的洋流，也提醒我们：气候并不仅仅是一种大气现象。一个海盆中的变化，可能在数月或数年后传到远离海岸的天气里。当这个系统被扰乱时，沿海城市、渔业社区和低洼岛屿尤其脆弱。海平面上升不是一张抽象的图表；它对家园、港口和农田来说是切实的后果。

因为海洋的工作大多看不见，人们很容易把行动推迟到损害已经明显的时候。这种拖延本身就有代价。如果我们希望这部气候引擎继续对我们有利地运转，就必须把海洋保护当作气候政策，而不是一项单独的爱好。减少排放、守护能够缓冲风暴的湿地，以及修复受损的珊瑚礁，都是在关注一个已经默默支撑我们很久的系统。

学生可以从一张主要洋流的地图和一个简单的问题开始：谁依赖它？我们把这些联系看得越清楚，就越难再把海仅仅想成度假的风景。爱护这部引擎，就是爱护我们将要与之共处的气候的一部分。

senior.title: 🧠 How Habits Quietly Shape Our Future
senior.content:
We often think of success as the result of big decisions or sudden inspiration. In truth, much of who we become is shaped by the small, repeated actions we take every day — our habits. 🔄

A habit is a behaviour that has become automatic through repetition. When you first learn to ride a bicycle or type on a keyboard, every movement requires attention. With practice, the brain creates stronger neural pathways, and the action becomes almost effortless. The same process applies to studying, exercising, reading, or even negative patterns like procrastination.

Because habits run largely on autopilot, they can work for us or against us. A student who reviews notes for twenty minutes every evening is quietly building knowledge and confidence. Another student who checks social media first thing every morning may be reinforcing distraction. Over months and years, these tiny differences compound into very different results.

Changing a habit is possible, but it usually requires more than motivation alone. Motivation comes and goes; systems and environment matter more. Making the desired behaviour easier (for example, putting a book on your pillow) and the unwanted behaviour harder (leaving the phone in another room) increases the chance of success. Tracking progress and celebrating small wins also helps reinforce the new pattern.

Perhaps the deepest power of habits lies in identity. When you repeatedly act like a reader, a runner, or a careful thinker, you begin to see yourself that way. The behaviour and the self-image support each other. In this sense, habits do not just change what we do — they gradually transform who we believe we are.

Building good habits is therefore an act of long-term self-respect. It is not about perfection, but about consistent, intentional effort. The person you will be in five years is being shaped by the habits you practise today. Choose them wisely. 🌱

Discipline is what carries a habit through the days when motivation is quiet. It does not have to look severe. It can be as ordinary as sitting down at the same desk at the same hour, even when the work feels dull. Over time, that steadiness becomes a form of resilience: after a missed day, you return the next morning instead of declaring the whole plan a failure. The habit is allowed to be imperfect and still continue.

It also helps to choose a small number of keystone habits rather than trying to redesign an entire life in one week. Sleep, movement, and a short daily review often support many other goals. When these are consistent, studying and mood usually become easier to manage. When they collapse, even strong motivation has little to hold on to.

Friends and families shape habits too, sometimes more than we notice. A household that keeps phones off the dinner table makes conversation easier; a class that begins with two minutes of planning makes distraction harder. You can ask for this kind of support without waiting to become a different person first.

In five years you will have practised something, whether you choose it or not. The question is whether that practice will compound into the identity you respect. Intentional habits are a quiet way of answering yes.
senior.translation:
我们常常认为成功来自大的决定或突然的灵感。实际上，我们成为什么样的人，很大程度上是由每天重复的小行动——我们的习惯——塑造的。🔄

习惯是一种通过重复变得自动化的行为。当你第一次学骑自行车或打字时，每一个动作都需要注意力。通过练习，大脑会建立更强的神经通路，动作几乎变得不费力。同样的过程也适用于学习、锻炼、阅读，甚至像拖延这样的负面模式。

因为习惯很大程度上在“自动驾驶”状态下运行，它们既可以为我们服务，也可能与我们作对。一个每天晚上复习二十分钟笔记的学生，正在悄悄积累知识和自信。另一个每天早上第一件事就刷社交媒体的学生，可能在强化分心。几个月、几年后，这些微小的差异会累积成截然不同的结果。

改变习惯是可能的，但通常需要的不只是动机。动机来了又走；系统和环境更重要。让期望的行为更容易（比如把书放在枕头上），让不想要的行为更难（把手机放在另一个房间），会提高成功的几率。记录进度并庆祝小胜利也有助于强化新模式。

也许习惯最深层的力量在于身份认同。当你反复表现得像一个读者、跑步者或谨慎的思考者时，你开始以这种方式看待自己。行为与自我形象相互支持。从这个意义上说，习惯不仅改变我们做什么——它们逐渐转变我们认为自己是谁。

因此，培养好习惯是一种长期的自我尊重。它不关乎完美，而关乎持续、有意识的努力。五年后的你，正被你今天实践的习惯所塑造。请明智地选择它们。🌱

纪律，是在动机安静下来的那些日子里，把一个习惯扛过去的东西。它不必显得严厉。它可以普通到在同一时刻坐到同一张书桌前，即使工作让人觉得乏味。随着时间推移，这种稳定会成为一种韧性：错过一天之后，你第二天早晨再回来，而不是宣布整个计划失败。习惯被允许不完美，却仍然继续。

选择少数几个关键习惯，而不是试图在一周内重新设计整个人生，也会有帮助。睡眠、活动和每天短暂的回顾，常常能支撑许多其他目标。当这些保持一致时，学习和心情通常更容易管理。当它们崩溃时，即使强烈的动机也没有什么可以依靠。

朋友和家庭也会塑造习惯，有时比我们注意到的更多。一个在餐桌上收起手机的家庭让交谈更容易；一个以两分钟计划开始的课堂让分心更难。你可以请求这种支持，而不必先等待自己变成另一个人。

五年后你一定练习过某些东西，无论你是否有意选择。问题在于，那种练习是否会复利成你所尊重的身份。有意识的习惯，是一种安静地回答“是”的方式。

options: Because they are always positive

senior.title: 📱 The Double-Edged Sword of Social Media
senior.content:
Social media has become an inseparable part of modern life. Platforms like WeChat, Douyin, and Instagram allow people to share moments, stay connected with friends, and access information instantly. Yet this powerful tool is a double-edged sword. 📱

On the positive side, social media enables rapid communication across distances. Students can join study groups online, discuss problems, and share learning resources. During difficult times, people can receive emotional support from online communities. Businesses use these platforms to reach customers, and public organizations spread important messages quickly.

However, the negative effects are equally real. Many teenagers spend hours scrolling through short videos, which can reduce the time available for study, exercise, and face-to-face interaction. Constant comparison with others’ carefully edited lives often leads to anxiety and lower self-esteem. Addiction to likes and comments can make some people dependent on external approval rather than inner confidence.

Privacy is another serious concern. Personal information shared online may be collected and used without full awareness. Cyberbullying and the spread of false information also damage trust and mental well-being.

The key is not to abandon social media, but to use it with awareness and balance. Setting time limits, choosing high-quality content, and protecting personal information are practical steps. Offline activities—reading, sports, and real conversations—remain essential for healthy development.

Technology itself is neutral. Its value depends on how we choose to use it. By developing digital literacy and self-discipline, young people can enjoy the benefits of social media while avoiding its traps. 🌱

One hidden influence of social media is the way it trains attention. A platform is designed to offer the next item before you have finished thinking about the last. That design can be useful when you need a quick fact, and costly when you need a long, quiet hour. If you never notice the pull, the day is easily divided into fragments that feel busy but leave little memory behind.

A practical response is to decide, in advance, what a session is for. Ten minutes to message a friend, twenty minutes to watch a tutorial, or a short look at the news are different tasks. When the purpose is clear, it is easier to close the app and return to offline life. Some students also keep a simple log for a week: not to judge themselves, but to see how often a “quick check” becomes an hour.

Influence travels in the other direction as well. The comments we leave, the rumours we forward, and the photos we share all shape the atmosphere other people meet. Digital citizenship is not a formal title; it is the habit of asking whether a post is fair, private, or true before it leaves our hands.

Used with that kind of awareness, social media can remain a tool rather than a mood. The double edge does not disappear, but it becomes something we can hold more carefully.
senior.translation:
社交媒体已成为现代生活中不可分割的一部分。微信、抖音和Instagram等平台让人们分享瞬间、与朋友保持联系、即时获取信息。然而，这个强大的工具是一把双刃剑。📱

积极方面，社交媒体使跨距离的快速沟通成为可能。学生可以加入在线学习小组、讨论问题、分享学习资源。在困难时期，人们可以从在线社区获得情感支持。企业利用这些平台接触客户，公共机构快速传播重要信息。

然而，负面影响同样真实。许多青少年花数小时刷短视频，这会减少学习、锻炼和面对面交流的时间。不断与他人精心编辑的生活比较，往往导致焦虑和自尊心下降。对点赞和评论的沉迷会让一些人依赖外部认可，而非内在自信。

隐私是另一个严重问题。在线分享的个人信息可能在不完全知情的情况下被收集和使用。网络欺凌和虚假信息的传播也会损害信任和心理健康。

关键不是放弃社交媒体，而是带着意识和平衡去使用它。设定时间限制、选择高质量内容、保护个人信息都是切实可行的步骤。线下活动——阅读、运动和真实对话——对健康发展仍然至关重要。

技术本身是中性的。它的价值取决于我们如何选择使用它。通过培养数字素养和自律，年轻人可以享受社交媒体的好处，同时避免其陷阱。🌱

社交媒体一种隐蔽的影响，是它训练注意力的方式。一个平台被设计成在你还没想完上一条时，就送上下一条。当你需要一条快速事实时，这种设计可能有用；当你需要一段长而安静的时间时，它就可能代价很高。如果你从未注意到这股拉力，一天就很容易被切成许多碎片：感觉忙碌，却几乎留不下记忆。

一个实际的应对，是事先决定一次使用是为了什么。十分钟给朋友发消息，二十分钟看教程，或短暂看一下新闻，是不同的任务。当目的清楚时，就更容易关掉应用，回到线下生活。有些学生也会做一个星期的简单记录：不是为了评判自己，而是看看一次“快速查看”有多频繁地变成一个小时。

影响也会朝另一个方向传播。我们留下的评论、转发的传言，以及分享的照片，都会塑造别人遇到的气氛。数字公民身份不是一个正式头衔；它是在一条内容离开我们的手之前，先问一问它是否公平、是否涉及隐私、是否真实的习惯。

带着这样的觉察去使用，社交媒体可以仍然是工具，而不是一种情绪。双刃并不会消失，但会变成我们可以更小心地握住的东西。

senior.title: 🌍 Plastic Pollution: A Challenge We Must Face
senior.content:
Plastic is everywhere—in bottles, bags, packaging, and countless everyday products. It is cheap, light, and convenient. Yet the same qualities that make plastic useful also make it a serious environmental threat. 🌍

Most plastics do not decompose naturally for hundreds of years. When they enter rivers and oceans, they break into smaller pieces called microplastics. These tiny particles are eaten by fish and other marine animals, and eventually enter the human food chain. Birds and sea turtles often mistake plastic bags for food, which can cause injury or death.

The scale of the problem is enormous. Millions of tons of plastic waste enter the ocean every year. Beaches around the world are littered with bottles and packaging. Even remote areas far from cities are no longer free from plastic pollution.

Solving this challenge requires action at many levels. Individuals can reduce single-use plastics by carrying reusable bags and bottles. Governments can ban certain plastic products and improve recycling systems. Companies can redesign packaging and invest in alternative materials that are biodegradable or easier to recycle.

Education also plays a vital role. When people understand the long-term cost of plastic pollution, they are more likely to change their habits. Schools, media, and communities can all help raise awareness.

Plastic pollution is not someone else’s problem—it is a shared responsibility. Every choice we make, from refusing a plastic straw to supporting sustainable products, contributes to a cleaner planet. The future of our oceans and ecosystems depends on the actions we take today. 🌊

The problem is made worse by how casually we consume plastic and then forget it. A bottle used for ten minutes may remain in the environment for generations. Because the harm is delayed and often happens far from the shop, it is tempting to treat each item as too small to matter. Added together, however, those small items become a tide that no single beach clean-up can fully reverse.

Better design can help, but it cannot replace responsibility. An alternative material is only an improvement if it is collected and processed honestly. A label that says “recyclable” means little when local systems cannot handle the product, or when people are not sure which bin to use. Clear rules, honest information, and convenient collection have to travel together.

Young people already have more power than they sometimes think. A class audit of lunch packaging, a request that a canteen offer water refills, or a family decision to buy in bulk can change what is purchased next week. Sharing the reason, not only the rule, makes the habit more likely to last.

Plastic will not vanish from useful work such as medicine or safety equipment. The challenge is to stop treating it as a disposable background to ordinary life. If we consume less of what we do not need, and deal more carefully with what remains, ecosystems have a better chance to recover.
senior.translation:
塑料无处不在——瓶子、袋子、包装以及无数日常产品中。它便宜、轻便、方便。然而，让塑料有用的这些特性，也使它成为严重的环境威胁。🌍

大多数塑料在自然中数百年都不会分解。当它们进入河流和海洋时，会碎成叫做微塑料的小块。这些微小颗粒被鱼类和其他海洋动物吃掉，最终进入人类食物链。鸟类和海龟经常把塑料袋误认为食物，可能导致受伤或死亡。

问题的规模巨大。每年有数百万吨塑料废物进入海洋。世界各地的海滩上散落着瓶子和包装。即使远离城市的偏远地区也不再没有塑料污染。

解决这一挑战需要多层次的行动。个人可以通过携带可重复使用的袋子和瓶子来减少一次性塑料。政府可以禁止某些塑料产品并改善回收系统。公司可以重新设计包装，投资可生物降解或更容易回收的替代材料。

教育也起着至关重要的作用。当人们理解塑料污染的长期代价时，他们更有可能改变习惯。学校、媒体和社区都可以帮助提高意识。

塑料污染不是别人的问题——它是共同的责任。我们做出的每一个选择，从拒绝塑料吸管到支持可持续产品，都有助于更清洁的星球。我们海洋和生态系统的未来，取决于我们今天采取的行动。🌊

这个问题会因我们如此随意地消费塑料、然后又把它忘掉而变得更糟。一个使用十分钟的瓶子，可能在环境中停留好几代。因为伤害是延迟的，而且常常发生在远离商店的地方，人们很容易把每一件物品都当作小到无关紧要。然而把这些小物件加在一起，就会变成一股单靠一次海滩清理无法完全扭转的潮流。

更好的设计可以有帮助，但它不能代替责任。一种替代材料，只有在被诚实收集和处理时，才算改进。当本地系统无法处理这种产品，或人们不确定该投进哪个桶时，写着“可回收”的标签就没有多大意义。清楚的规则、诚实的信息和方便的收集必须一起到来。

年轻人已经拥有比他们有时以为的更大的力量。一次对午餐包装的班级盘点，一次请食堂提供加水服务的请求，或一个家庭批量购买的决定，都可以改变下周被买下的东西。分享理由，而不仅仅是规则，会让这个习惯更可能持续。

塑料不会从医疗或安全设备等有用的工作中消失。挑战在于停止把它当作日常生活可随意丢弃的背景。如果我们少消费并不需要的东西，并更小心地处理剩下的，生态系统就有更好的机会恢复。

senior.title: 🧠 Growth Mindset: How Beliefs Shape Success
senior.content:
Have you ever thought “I’m just not good at maths” or “I’ll never be able to speak English fluently”? These thoughts reflect what psychologists call a fixed mindset—the belief that abilities are fixed and cannot change much. In contrast, a growth mindset is the belief that abilities can be developed through effort, learning, and persistence. 🧠

Research shows that students with a growth mindset tend to achieve more. When they face a difficult problem, they see it as a challenge to learn from, not as proof that they are not smart enough. They are more willing to try different strategies, ask for help, and keep practising. Students with a fixed mindset, however, often avoid challenges because failure feels like a judgment of their intelligence.

How can we develop a growth mindset? First, notice your inner voice. When you catch yourself saying “I can’t do this,” add the word “yet”—“I can’t do this yet.” This small change opens the door to future improvement. Second, value effort and strategy more than natural talent. Praise yourself and others for hard work and smart methods, not only for high scores. Third, treat mistakes as information. Every error tells you what to practise next.

Teachers and parents can also help. When feedback focuses on process—“You used a good method” or “You improved because you practised”—students learn that growth is possible. When feedback only praises results—“You’re so smart”—students may fear challenges that could threaten that label.

A growth mindset does not mean that everyone will become a genius. It means that with deliberate practice and the right strategies, most people can improve significantly in areas they care about. The belief that you can grow is itself a powerful tool for learning and life. 🌱

A growth mindset is most tested when progress is slow. It is easy to praise effort after a quick win; it is harder to persist when a skill stays awkward for weeks. This is where potential can be misunderstood. Potential is not a hidden medal that you either have or lack. It is the room that practice, feedback and time can still open. If you leave as soon as the work feels clumsy, that room stays closed.

It also helps to separate identity from a single result. “I failed this test” is information; “I am a failure” is a story that makes the next attempt heavier. Students who persist tend to ask better questions after a setback: What method did I use? What should I try next? That curiosity keeps the belief flexible.

Teachers cannot install a mindset the way they hand out a worksheet, but they can make growth visible. Showing early drafts beside later ones, or talking about their own unfinished learning, tells a class that improvement is normal. Peers matter too. A group that laughs at struggle will shrink risk; a group that treats struggle as part of the method will make courage cheaper.

None of this erases the need for good teaching or fair chances. A growth mindset is not a command to try harder in a broken system. It is a way of staying in the work long enough for strategy and support to have an effect, so that more of your potential has a chance to be used.
senior.translation:
你有没有想过“我就是不擅长数学”或“我永远无法流利说英语”？这些想法反映了心理学家所说的固定型思维——相信能力是固定的，无法有太大改变。相反，成长型思维是相信能力可以通过努力、学习和坚持得到发展。🧠

研究表明，拥有成长型思维的学生往往取得更多成就。当他们面对难题时，他们把它看作学习的挑战，而不是证明自己不够聪明。他们更愿意尝试不同策略、寻求帮助并持续练习。而固定型思维的学生常常回避挑战，因为失败感觉像是对智力的评判。

我们如何培养成长型思维？首先，注意内心的声音。当你发现自己说“我做不到”时，加上“还”——“我还做不到”。这个小改变打开了未来进步的大门。其次，更看重努力和策略，而不是天赋。表扬自己和他人的努力与聪明方法，而不只是高分。第三，把错误当作信息。每个错误都告诉你下一步该练习什么。

老师和家长也可以帮助。当反馈关注过程——“你用了好方法”或“你进步是因为练习”——学生会学到成长是可能的。当反馈只表扬结果——“你真聪明”——学生可能害怕会威胁这个标签的挑战。

成长型思维并不意味着每个人都会成为天才。它意味着通过刻意练习和正确策略，大多数人可以在自己关心的领域显著提高。相信自己可以成长，本身就是学习和生活的强大工具。🌱

成长型思维在进步缓慢时最受考验。在一次快速胜利之后赞美努力很容易；当一项技能连续几周都显得笨拙时，仍要坚持就更难。潜能在这里容易被误解。潜能不是一枚你要么拥有、要么缺少的隐藏奖牌。它是练习、反馈和时间仍然可以打开的空间。如果你一感到笨拙就离开，那片空间就会一直关着。

把身份和一次单独的结果分开，也会有帮助。“我这次考试失败了”是信息；“我是一个失败者”则是让下一次尝试更沉重的故事。能够坚持的学生，往往会在挫折之后问出更好的问题：我用了什么方法？下一步该试什么？这种好奇让信念保持灵活。

老师不能像发练习纸那样把一种思维安装进学生心里，但他们可以让成长变得可见。把早期草稿放在后来的稿子旁边，或谈论他们自己尚未完成的学习，都在告诉全班：进步是正常的。同伴也很重要。一个嘲笑挣扎的小组会缩小冒险的空间；一个把挣扎当作方法一部分的小组，会让勇气变得更便宜。

这一切并不能取消对良好教学和公平机会的需要。成长型思维不是在一个破碎的系统里下令更加努力。它是一种让你在工作中停留得足够久的方式，好让策略和支持能够发挥作用，从而让你更多的潜能有机会被用上。

senior.title: 🤝 The Value of Volunteering
senior.content:
Volunteering means offering your time and energy to help others without expecting payment. It may seem like a small act, but its impact on both the helper and the community can be profound. 🤝

For the people who receive help, volunteers can make a real difference. A student tutoring a younger child in English may improve that child’s confidence and grades. A group cleaning a park makes the neighbourhood more pleasant for everyone. During natural disasters, volunteers often provide food, shelter, and emotional support when official help is limited.

For the volunteers themselves, the benefits are equally valuable. Volunteering builds skills such as communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. It also develops empathy—the ability to understand other people’s feelings. Many students discover new interests and even future career directions through volunteer work. In addition, helping others often brings a sense of purpose and happiness that is hard to get from other activities.

Schools and communities increasingly encourage youth participation in volunteering. Some schools include community service as part of the curriculum. Online platforms make it easier to find opportunities that match personal interests, whether teaching, environmental protection, or caring for the elderly.

Of course, volunteering should be meaningful and well organized. Short, one-time actions are good, but long-term commitment often creates deeper impact. Reflection after volunteering—thinking about what was learned and what could be improved—helps turn experience into personal growth.

In a society that sometimes focuses too much on competition and individual success, volunteering reminds us of our shared responsibility. When more people choose to give a little of their time, the whole community becomes stronger and warmer. 🌱

A lasting contribution often looks quieter than a camera might suggest. Returning every Saturday to read with the same child, or spending a term sorting donations, can matter more than a single dramatic day. The people you help learn that they can count on you, and you learn how a real organisation works — including the unglamorous parts. That kind of reliability is itself a gift to a community.

It is wise to match the work to a genuine interest and to a schedule you can keep. A project chosen only to decorate an application may feel empty, and the people being helped will sense it. Talk with organisers about what is actually needed. Sometimes the most useful task is not the one that looks best in a photograph.

Volunteering also teaches the limits of help. You will meet problems you cannot fix in an afternoon, and you will need humility as well as energy. That tension is not a reason to stop; it is a reason to listen better, to learn from local knowledge, and to notice when a system, not only a person, needs change.

Seen this way, participation is a civic habit, not a hobby for rare free weekends. Each contribution, however modest, is a vote for the kind of society you want to live in: one in which responsibility is shared, and strangers are not left entirely alone.
senior.translation:
志愿服务意味着在不期望报酬的情况下，贡献时间和精力帮助他人。它看起来可能只是小行动，但对帮助者和社区的影响都可以很深远。🤝

对于接受帮助的人，志愿者可以带来真正的改变。一个学生辅导低年级孩子英语，可能提高那个孩子的自信和成绩。一个清理公园的团体让整个社区更宜人。在自然灾害中，志愿者常常在官方帮助有限时提供食物、住所和情感支持。

对志愿者自己，益处同样宝贵。志愿服务培养沟通、团队合作和解决问题等技能。它也培养同理心——理解他人感受的能力。许多学生通过志愿工作发现新兴趣甚至未来职业方向。此外，帮助他人往往带来其他活动难以获得的目标感和幸福感。

学校和社区越来越鼓励青少年参与志愿服务。一些学校把社区服务纳入课程。在线平台让寻找匹配个人兴趣的机会更容易，无论是教学、环保还是照顾老人。

当然，志愿服务应该有意义且组织良好。短期、一次性行动很好，但长期承诺往往产生更深影响。志愿服务后的反思——思考学到了什么、可以改进什么——有助于把经历转化为个人成长。

在一个有时过于关注竞争和个人成功的社会里，志愿服务提醒我们共同的责任。当更多人选择贡献一点时间时，整个社区会变得更强大、更温暖。🌱

一份持久的贡献，常常比镜头里看起来的更安静。每个星期六回来和同一个孩子一起读书，或花一个学期整理捐赠物资，可能比戏剧性的一天更重要。你帮助的人会知道他们可以依靠你，而你会了解一个真正的组织如何运转——包括那些并不光鲜的部分。这种可靠本身就是给社区的一份礼物。

明智的做法是让工作匹配真正的兴趣，以及你能够坚持的日程。一个仅仅为了装饰申请材料而选择的项目可能让人觉得空洞，被帮助的人也会察觉。和组织者谈谈实际需要什么。有时最有用的任务，并不是照片里最好看的那一项。

志愿服务也教会我们帮助的限度。你会遇到一个下午无法解决的问题，你需要谦卑，也需要精力。这种张力不是停止的理由；它是更好倾听、向本地知识学习，并注意到何时需要改变的是一个系统、而不仅仅是一个人的理由。

这样看来，参与是一种公民习惯，而不是偶尔空闲周末的爱好。每一份贡献，无论多么谦逊，都是在为你想生活其中的那种社会投票：在那里责任被分担，陌生人不会被完全独自留下。

senior.title: 🤖 Artificial Intelligence: Opportunity and Responsibility
senior.content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is no longer science fiction. It recommends videos, translates languages, helps doctors diagnose diseases, and even drives cars. The speed of AI development brings both exciting opportunities and serious responsibilities. 🤖

On the opportunity side, AI can handle large amounts of data faster than humans. In education, adaptive learning systems can adjust difficulty for each student. In medicine, AI can detect early signs of disease from images. In environmental science, AI models help predict climate patterns and optimise energy use. These applications can improve efficiency and quality of life.

However, AI also raises difficult questions. Algorithms are trained on data created by humans, so they can inherit human biases. If a hiring system is trained on past decisions that favoured certain groups, it may continue unfair practices. Privacy is another concern: AI systems often need large amounts of personal data to work well. Who controls that data, and how is it protected?

Job markets will also change. Some routine tasks will be automated, which may displace certain jobs. At the same time, new roles will appear—AI trainers, ethics officers, and specialists who combine domain knowledge with AI tools. Education systems need to prepare students not only to use AI, but to think critically about it.

The key is responsible innovation. Developers, companies, governments, and users all share responsibility. Clear rules, transparent algorithms, and public discussion can help ensure that AI serves human values rather than undermining them. Technology is a tool; the direction it takes depends on the choices we make. 🌱

Automation is already changing ordinary workplaces, not only factories. A shop may use AI to predict stock; an office may use it to sort mail or draft a first letter. These tools can free people from repetitive work, but they can also hide decisions inside an algorithm that few employees can question. If a system denies a loan or flags a student as “at risk,” someone must be able to explain why, and to correct a mistake.

That is why societies need to regulate high-stakes uses of AI rather than trusting slogans about innovation. Rules about privacy, bias testing, and human review are not obstacles to progress; they are how progress stays accountable. Companies that collect data should say what they take, how long they keep it, and who else may see it. Users, including students, should practise the habit of asking those questions.

Education has a double task. Students need enough technical literacy to use new tools well, and enough ethical literacy to refuse uses that harm people. A class that only celebrates speed will miss the harder lesson: not every problem should be handed to a model, and not every score a model produces is fair.

AI will keep improving. The responsibility is to decide, in public, which kinds of automation we want, and which decisions must remain human. Opportunity without that debate is not a complete gift.
senior.translation:
人工智能（AI）不再是科幻。它推荐视频、翻译语言、帮助医生诊断疾病，甚至驾驶汽车。AI发展的速度既带来令人兴奋的机遇，也带来严肃的责任。🤖

机遇方面，AI能比人类更快处理大量数据。在教育中，自适应学习系统可以为每个学生调整难度。在医学中，AI可以从图像中发现疾病的早期迹象。在环境科学中，AI模型帮助预测气候模式并优化能源使用。这些应用可以提高效率和生活质量。

然而，AI也提出难题。算法用人类创造的数据训练，因此可能继承人类偏见。如果招聘系统用过去偏向某些群体的决策训练，它可能继续不公平做法。隐私是另一个问题：AI系统通常需要大量个人数据才能良好运行。谁控制这些数据，又如何保护？

就业市场也会改变。一些常规任务将被自动化，可能取代某些工作。同时会出现新角色——AI训练师、伦理官以及把领域知识与AI工具结合的专家。教育系统需要培养学生不仅会用AI，还能批判性思考它。

关键是负责任的创新。开发者、公司、政府和用户都分担责任。清晰规则、透明算法和公共讨论可以帮助确保AI服务于人类价值，而不是削弱它们。技术是工具；它的方向取决于我们做出的选择。🌱

自动化已经在改变普通的工作场所，而不仅仅是工厂。商店可能用人工智能预测库存；办公室可能用它分类邮件或起草第一封信。这些工具可以让人从重复劳动中解脱，但也可能把决定藏进很少有员工能够质疑的算法里。如果一个系统拒绝贷款，或把一名学生标记为“有风险”，必须有人能够解释原因，并纠正错误。

这就是为什么社会需要规范人工智能在高风险场合的使用，而不是信任关于创新的口号。关于隐私、偏见测试和人工复核的规则不是进步的障碍；它们是进步保持可问责的方式。收集数据的公司应当说明它们取了什么、保存多久、还有谁可能看见。包括学生在内的使用者，应当练习提出这些问题的习惯。

教育有双重任务。学生需要足够的技术素养来用好新工具，也需要足够的伦理素养来拒绝伤害人的用法。一个只赞美速度的课堂会错过更难的一课：不是每一个问题都应当交给模型，也不是模型给出的每一个分数都是公平的。

人工智能还会继续改进。责任在于公开决定我们想要哪一类自动化，以及哪些决定必须仍然由人来做。没有这场辩论的机会，并不是一份完整的礼物。

senior.title: 🌏 Cultural Diversity: Learning from Difference
senior.content:
The world is full of different languages, foods, festivals, and ways of thinking. This cultural diversity is not a problem to solve—it is a resource to value. 🌏

When we meet people from other cultures, we often notice differences first: how they greet, what they eat, or how they celebrate. These differences can feel strange at first. But if we stay curious instead of judging, we discover that every culture has its own logic and wisdom. A festival that seems unusual may express deep values about family, nature, or community.

Learning about other cultures also helps us understand our own. By comparing, we see which of our habits are universal and which are specific to our background. This broader perspective reduces stereotypes—oversimplified ideas about groups of people. Stereotypes often lead to misunderstanding and conflict; real contact and open conversation lead to respect.

In a globalised world, cultural skills are practical. Students may study abroad, work in international teams, or use online platforms where people from many countries meet. The ability to communicate across cultures—listening carefully, explaining clearly, and showing respect—is increasingly valuable.

Respect does not mean agreeing with everything. It means recognising that others have the right to their traditions and beliefs, just as we have the right to ours. Dialogue, not silence or force, is the way to handle disagreement.

Cultural diversity enriches human life. Music, literature, science, and food have all grown through exchange between cultures. By approaching difference with curiosity and respect, we prepare ourselves for a more connected and more peaceful future. 🤝

A global classroom or workplace makes these skills less optional than they once seemed. You may share a project with someone whose humour, timing, or idea of politeness is different from yours. Without tolerance — the patience to stay present before you judge — it is easy to read a difference as a flaw. With it, you have time to ask what the behaviour means in that person’s world.

Identity is part of the same conversation. Culture is not a costume you put on for a festival and then forget. It shapes food, family, and the stories you find moving. Learning from difference does not require you to abandon your own identity; it requires you to hold it more honestly, and to allow others the same right. A confident identity can be open; a frightened one often hides behind stereotypes.

Schools can practise this in ordinary ways: reading stories from more than one tradition, inviting students to explain a home custom without being treated as a representative of a whole nation, and correcting jokes that flatten people into types. The goal is not a bland sameness, but a habit of precise respect.

If diversity is truly a resource, then curiosity is how we spend it well. The future will be more mixed, not less. Those who can listen across difference will be better neighbours — and better partners in a global society.
senior.translation:
世界充满不同的语言、食物、节日和思维方式。这种文化多样性不是要解决的问题——它是值得珍视的资源。🌏

当我们遇到其他文化的人时，往往先注意到差异：他们如何问候、吃什么、如何庆祝。这些差异起初可能感觉奇怪。但如果我们保持好奇而不是评判，就会发现每种文化都有自己的逻辑和智慧。一个看似不寻常的节日，可能表达着关于家庭、自然或社区的深刻价值观。

了解其他文化也帮助我们理解自己的文化。通过比较，我们看到哪些习惯是普遍的，哪些是我们背景特有的。这种更广阔的视角减少刻板印象——对群体的过度简化看法。刻板印象常导致误解和冲突；真实接触和开放对话带来尊重。

在全球化世界中，文化技能是实用的。学生可能出国留学、在国际团队工作，或使用来自许多国家的人聚集的在线平台。跨文化交流的能力——仔细倾听、清晰解释、表达尊重——越来越有价值。

尊重并不意味着同意一切。它意味着承认他人有权拥有自己的传统和信仰，正如我们有权拥有自己的。对话，而不是沉默或强制，是处理分歧的方式。

文化多样性丰富人类生活。音乐、文学、科学和食物都通过文化间的交流成长。以好奇和尊重对待差异，我们为更互联、更和平的未来做好准备。🤝

一个全球性的教室或工作场所，使这些技能看起来不再像从前那样可有可无。你可能与一个幽默、时机或礼貌观念与你不同的人共事。如果没有宽容——那种在评判之前先留下来的耐心——就很容易把差异读成缺陷。有了它，你才有时间去问：这种行为在那个人的世界里意味着什么。

身份也是同一场对话的一部分。文化不是一套只在节日穿上、随后就忘掉的服装。它塑造食物、家庭，以及那些让你感动的故事。从差异中学习，并不要求你放弃自己的身份；它要求你更诚实地持有它，并允许别人拥有同样的权利。自信的身份可以是开放的；恐惧的身份则常常躲在刻板印象后面。

学校可以用平常的方式练习这一点：阅读来自不止一种传统的故事，邀请学生解释一种家庭习俗而不把他们当作整个国家的代表，并纠正那些把人压扁成类型的笑话。目标不是乏味的同一，而是一种精确尊重的习惯。

如果多样性真的是一种资源，那么好奇就是我们把它用好的方式。未来会更加混合，而不是更少。那些能够跨越差异去倾听的人，会成为更好的邻居——也会成为全球社会中更好的伙伴。

senior.title: 📝 Effective Note-Taking: A Skill for Lifelong Learning
senior.content:
Taking notes is not just writing down what the teacher says. Effective note-taking is an active learning strategy that improves understanding and long-term retention. 📝

Many students copy slides or textbooks word for word. This keeps the hand busy but the mind passive. Better notes focus on key ideas, relationships, and examples. Use your own words when possible—paraphrasing forces you to process the information, which strengthens memory.

Structure matters. Leave space between points so you can add comments later. Use headings, bullet points, and simple diagrams. Some students prefer the Cornell method: a main note area, a narrow column for keywords or questions, and a summary at the bottom. Others use mind maps to show connections between ideas.

Notes are most useful when you review them. Within 24 hours, spend a few minutes looking over what you wrote. Mark unclear parts and check them with the textbook or a classmate. Before exams, use your notes to test yourself: cover the details and try to recall them from keywords alone.

Digital tools can help organise and search notes, but handwriting still has advantages for memory. Whether you use paper or a tablet, the principles stay the same: be selective, use your own words, organise clearly, and review regularly.

Good note-taking is a skill that serves you far beyond school. In university, at work, and in lifelong learning, the ability to capture, organise, and revisit important information remains essential. Start refining your method now. 🌱

A good page of notes is a conversation with the lesson, not a photograph of the board. After class, add a question in the margin, a tiny sketch, or a link to something you already know. These marks turn a list of facts into a structure you can climb later. If a heading feels vague, rewrite it as a question you must be able to answer.

Different subjects invite different strategies, but the aim stays active. In science, a simple table of variables and results may serve better than long sentences. In history, a timeline with causes in your own words may serve better than copied dates. In language, example sentences and a short summary of a grammar point are usually more useful than a wall of rules. Choose the method that forces you to think, then keep it consistent enough to review.

Many students take notes and never return to them until the night before a test. That habit wastes the best part of the work. A short review the same evening, and another later in the week, turns the page into memory. Cover a section, say the idea out loud, and only then look. If you cannot recall it, the note was not finished; tighten the wording until a keyword can bring the idea back.

Over years, the value of this skill grows. Lectures, meetings, and books will keep arriving. Those who can capture what matters, organise it clearly, and return to it with a plan will keep learning after the last school exam is over. Note-taking is not decoration in a folder. It is a way of keeping ownership of what you have heard.
senior.translation:
记笔记不只是把老师说的话写下来。有效的记笔记是一种主动学习策略，能提高理解和长期记忆。📝

许多学生逐字抄幻灯片或课本。这让手很忙，但大脑是被动的。更好的笔记关注关键想法、关系和例子。尽可能用自己的话——改写迫使你处理信息，从而加强记忆。

结构很重要。在要点之间留出空间，以便以后添加注释。使用标题、项目符号和简单图表。有些学生喜欢康奈尔笔记法：主笔记区、窄栏写关键词或问题、底部写摘要。另一些人用思维导图显示想法之间的联系。

笔记在复习时最有用。24小时内花几分钟回顾所写内容。标出不清楚的部分，用课本或和同学核对。考试前用笔记自测：盖住细节，只凭关键词尝试回忆。

数字工具可以帮助组织和搜索笔记，但手写对记忆仍有优势。无论用纸还是平板，原则相同：有选择、用自己的话、组织清晰、定期复习。

好的记笔记是一项远超学校的技能。在大学、工作中以及终身学习中，捕捉、组织和回顾重要信息的能力始终至关重要。现在就开始改进你的方法吧。🌱

一页好的笔记是与这堂课的对话，而不是黑板的照片。课后，在空白处加上一个问题、一幅小小的草图，或一条连向你已知事物的线索。这些记号会把一份事实清单变成你稍后可以攀爬的结构。如果一个标题显得含糊，就把它改写成一个你必须能够回答的问题。

不同科目适合不同的策略，但目标始终是主动的。在科学里，一张变量和结果的简单表格可能比长句子更有用。在历史里，一条用自己的话写下原因的时间线，可能比抄来的日期更有用。在语言里，例句和语法点的短摘要，通常比一堵规则之墙更有用。选择那种迫使你思考的方法，然后保持足够一致，以便复习。

许多学生记了笔记，直到考试前一晚才再看。这种习惯浪费了这项工作最好的部分。当天晚上的短复习，再加上本周晚些时候的另一次，会把那一页变成记忆。盖住一节，把意思说出来，然后再看。如果你回忆不起来，笔记就还没有完成；把措辞收紧，直到一个关键词就能把想法带回来。

多年之后，这项技能的价值会增长。讲座、会议和书籍会不断到来。那些能够抓住要点、清楚组织，并带着计划回去看的人，会在最后一场学校考试结束之后继续学习。记笔记不是文件夹里的装饰。它是一种把你听过的东西保存在自己手里的方式。

senior.title: 🌐 Global Citizenship in a Connected World
senior.content:
We live in an interconnected world. A decision made in one country can affect the environment, economy, or health of people far away. Global citizenship means recognising this connection and taking responsibility beyond our immediate community. 🌐

Global citizens try to understand issues from multiple perspectives. Climate change, public health, and digital technology do not stop at national borders. Solving them requires cooperation, accurate information, and respect for different cultures and needs. Education plays a central role: learning foreign languages, studying world history and geography, and discussing current events all build the awareness needed for informed action.

Being a global citizen does not mean ignoring local duties. It means seeing how local actions—reducing waste, supporting fair trade, or treating classmates from different backgrounds with respect—link to larger patterns. It also means being careful with information: checking sources before sharing news, and recognising that complex problems rarely have simple slogans as answers.

Young people are already global in many ways. They use platforms that connect millions across countries. They can turn that connectivity into learning and positive contribution: joining online educational projects, supporting environmental campaigns, or simply practising empathy in daily interactions.

The challenges of the 21st century—climate, inequality, technology ethics—will need people who can think across borders and act with both local care and global awareness. Developing that capacity starts with curiosity, critical thinking, and the willingness to learn from others. Every student can begin today. 🌱

To contribute as a global citizen, you do not need a title or a plane ticket. You need the habit of asking who is affected by a choice that looks local. The clothes you buy, the energy you waste, and the jokes you repeat can travel farther than a classroom wall. A sustainable attitude begins with that kind of awareness: not guilt as a fashion, but responsibility that can be practised in ordinary days.

It also means being willing to hold two thoughts at once. A country may need development and still need to cut pollution. A technology may connect people and still spread harm. Global problems are rarely solved by a single slogan, which is why cooperation depends on listening as well as speaking. Students can practise this in a debate, a group project, or a careful reading of news from more than one place.

Some of the most useful contributions are quiet. Checking a source before you share a story protects people you will never meet. Welcoming a new classmate from another country is a small act of citizenship. Joining a campaign is valuable, but so is keeping a promise in your own street. The connected world is not only online; it is the web of effects that follow our habits.

The twenty-first century will keep producing challenges that cross borders. Those who can think with a wider perspective, and who still do the local work, will help more than those who only post opinions. Global citizenship is a way of paying attention — and then choosing to contribute rather than look away.
senior.translation:
我们生活在一个相互连接的世界。一个国家做出的决定可能影响远方人们的环境、经济或健康。全球公民意味着认识到这种联系，并承担超出眼前社区的责任。🌐

全球公民尝试从多个视角理解问题。气候变化、公共卫生和数字技术不会止于国界。解决它们需要合作、准确信息以及对不同文化和需求的尊重。教育起核心作用：学习外语、研究世界历史和地理、讨论时事，都能建立知情行动所需的意识。

成为全球公民并不意味着忽视本地责任。它意味着看到本地行动——减少浪费、支持公平贸易、或尊重来自不同背景的同学——如何与更大格局相连。它也意味着谨慎对待信息：分享新闻前核实来源，并认识到复杂问题很少有简单口号作为答案。

年轻人在许多方面已经是全球性的。他们使用连接各国数百万人的平台。他们可以把这种连接转化为学习和积极贡献：加入在线教育项目、支持环保运动，或只是在日常互动中练习同理心。

21世纪的挑战——气候、不平等、技术伦理——将需要能够跨边界思考、并以本地关怀和全球意识行动的人。培养这种能力始于好奇、批判性思维以及向他人学习的意愿。每个学生今天就可以开始。🌱

要作为全球公民去贡献，你并不需要一个头衔或一张机票。你需要的是一种习惯：去问一个看起来本地的选择会影响谁。你买的衣服、你浪费的能源，以及你重复的笑话，都可能传得比教室的墙更远。一种可持续的态度从这样的觉察开始：不是把愧疚当成时尚，而是可以在平常日子里练习的责任。

这也意味着愿意同时抓住两种想法。一个国家可能需要发展，却仍然需要减少污染。一项技术可能连接人们，却仍然传播伤害。全球问题很少被一句口号解决，这就是为什么合作既依赖倾听，也依赖发言。学生可以在辩论、小组项目，或仔细阅读来自不止一个地方的新闻中练习这一点。

一些最有用的贡献是安静的。在分享一则故事之前核对来源，保护的是你永远不会遇见的人。欢迎一位来自另一个国家的新同学，是一种小小的公民行为。参加一项运动是有价值的，但在自己的街道上遵守承诺同样如此。这个相互连接的世界不仅仅在网上；它是跟随我们习惯而来的那张效果之网。

二十一世纪将不断产生跨越边界的挑战。那些能够以更宽的视角思考、却仍然做本地工作的人，会比只发表意见的人帮助更多。全球公民身份是一种注意的方式——然后选择去贡献，而不是把目光转开。

senior.title: 🔬 Critical Thinking in the Age of Information
senior.content:
We live in an age of abundant information. News, opinions, and data reach us through phones, websites, and social media every day. Critical thinking—the ability to evaluate information carefully—has never been more important. 🔬

Critical thinking starts with questions. Who produced this information? What is their purpose? Is there evidence to support the claim? Are there other views that are ignored? Reliable sources usually provide clear evidence and acknowledge uncertainty. Unreliable sources often use emotional language, absolute statements, or no sources at all.

Bias is everywhere. Every writer has a perspective. That does not mean all information is false, but it means we should not accept every claim without checking. Compare different sources. Look for data, expert consensus, and logical arguments rather than only personal stories or strong slogans.

In school, critical thinking appears in many subjects. In science, we test hypotheses. In history, we compare documents. In language classes, we analyse arguments in essays. Practising these skills prepares students for a world where they must decide what to believe and how to act.

Critical thinking is not about being negative. It is about being careful and fair. It helps us avoid being misled, make better decisions, and communicate more clearly. In a noisy information environment, the ability to think critically is a form of self-protection and a foundation for responsible citizenship. 🧠

A careful thinker also watches the path from evidence to a conclusion. A story can be moving and still fail as proof. A chart can look precise and still hide a weak sample. When a claim jumps too quickly from one example to a rule about everyone, the logic is thin, even if the language is confident. Slowing down at that jump is one of the most useful habits you can learn.

It helps to separate three jobs that are often mixed together: describing what happened, explaining why it may have happened, and deciding what should be done. A news post may do all three in a few lines. If you name each job, you can ask for the right kind of support. Descriptions need reliable sources. Explanations need a chain that can be tested. Calls to action need values that are stated honestly, not smuggled in as if they were facts.

Friends, algorithms and headlines all push us toward speed. Critical thinking is a way of reclaiming a little time. You do not have to research every sentence, but you can pause before you believe, share, or vote with your emotions alone. Compare, look for missing views, and be willing to change your mind when better evidence arrives.

In an age of abundant information, the scarce skill is not finding more text. It is arriving at a fair conclusion, or admitting that you do not have one yet. That kind of logic is not coldness. It is respect for reality, and for the people who will live with the decisions we make.
senior.translation:
我们生活在信息丰富的时代。新闻、观点和数据每天通过手机、网站和社交媒体到达我们。批判性思维——仔细评估信息的能力——从未如此重要。🔬

批判性思维从提问开始。谁制作了这些信息？他们的目的是什么？有没有证据支持这个声称？有没有被忽略的其他观点？可靠来源通常提供清晰证据并承认不确定性。不可靠来源往往使用情绪化语言、绝对表述或根本没有来源。

偏见无处不在。每个写作者都有视角。这并不意味着所有信息都是假的，但意味着我们不应不经核查就接受每个声称。比较不同来源。寻找数据、专家共识和逻辑论证，而不仅仅是个人故事或强烈口号。

在学校，批判性思维出现在许多科目中。在科学中，我们检验假设。在历史中，我们比较文献。在语言课中，我们分析文章中的论点。练习这些技能为学生准备一个他们必须决定相信什么、如何行动的世界。

批判性思维不是关于消极。它是关于谨慎和公平。它帮助我们避免被误导、做出更好决定、更清晰地交流。在嘈杂的信息环境中，批判性思维的能力是一种自我保护，也是负责任公民的基础。🧠

一个谨慎的思考者，也会注视从证据通向结论的那条路。一个故事可以很动人，却仍然不能当作证明。一张图表可以看起来精确，却仍然隐藏一个薄弱的样本。当一个断言从单个例子过快地跳到关于所有人的规则时，即使语言很有把握，逻辑也是薄弱的。在那一跳上放慢速度，是你能学会的最有用的习惯之一。

把常常被混在一起的三件工作分开，会有帮助：描述发生了什么，解释它可能为何发生，以及决定应当做什么。一条新闻可能用几行做完这三件事。如果你给每件工作起了名字，就可以要求正确类型的支持。描述需要可靠的来源。解释需要一条可以被检验的链条。行动的号召需要被诚实说出的价值，而不是被偷偷当作事实运进来。

朋友、算法和标题都把我们推向速度。批判性思维是一种夺回一点时间的方式。你不必研究每一句话，但可以在仅仅凭情绪去相信、分享或表态之前停顿一下。比较，寻找缺失的观点，并愿意在更好的证据到来时改变想法。

在信息丰富的时代，稀缺的技能不是找到更多文本。而是得出一个公正的结论，或承认你还没有结论。那种逻辑不是冷漠。它是对现实的尊重，也是对那些将与我们做出的决定共存的人的尊重。

senior.title: 🌳 Urban Green Spaces: Why Cities Need Trees
senior.content:
Cities are full of buildings, roads, and cars. In such environments, trees and parks—urban green spaces—are more than decoration. They are essential for health, climate, and community life. 🌳

Trees absorb carbon dioxide and release oxygen. They also catch dust and other pollutants, improving air quality. In hot summers, tree shade lowers temperatures in streets and parks, reducing the urban heat island effect. This makes cities more comfortable and can lower energy use for cooling.

Green spaces support mental health. Studies show that walking in parks or even seeing trees from a window can reduce stress and improve mood. For students, a green campus or a nearby park offers a place to rest the mind after long hours of study.

Biodiversity also benefits. Parks and tree-lined streets provide habitats for birds and insects. When cities protect and expand green areas, they help maintain ecological balance even in dense urban settings.

Creating and protecting urban green spaces requires planning and public support. Planting trees, maintaining parks, and leaving space for nature in new developments are all part of sustainable city design. Citizens can contribute by caring for local trees, joining tree-planting events, and supporting policies that prioritise green space.

A city with more trees is not only more beautiful—it is healthier, cooler, and more livable. Every tree planted is an investment in the future of urban life. 🌱

Air pollution in a dense city is easy to treat as only a problem for engines and factories, yet plants are part of the same story. Leaves catch fine dust, and a well-placed row of trees can soften a noisy road as well as a hot one. None of this means that green space can replace cleaner fuels or better public transport. It means that trees are a practical partner in a wider plan, not a pretty afterthought.

Good planning looks at who can reach a park, not only at how many trees appear in a brochure. A large garden on the far side of a motorway may do little for a child who has no safe crossing. Smaller pockets of green near schools, clinics and housing can serve daily life better. Maintenance matters too: a neglected square with broken lights soon feels unsafe, and then the mental and community benefits fade.

Biodiversity in the city is not a luxury. Birds, insects and even soil life keep a park from becoming a silent lawn. Native species, less chemical spray, and a little wildness at the edge of a path can make a small site richer. Students can help by joining a planting day, adopting a street tree, or simply leaving a school garden less tidy than a carpet.

A sustainable city will still need buildings and roads. The question is whether nature is given room inside that design. When urban green space is treated as infrastructure — like water or electricity — health, temperature and belonging all have a better chance.
senior.translation:
城市充满建筑、道路和汽车。在这样的环境中，树木和公园——城市绿地——不只是装饰。它们对健康、气候和社区生活至关重要。🌳

树木吸收二氧化碳并释放氧气。它们还捕获灰尘和其他污染物，改善空气质量。在炎热的夏天，树荫降低街道和公园的温度，减轻城市热岛效应。这使城市更舒适，并可以降低制冷能耗。

绿地支持心理健康。研究表明，在公园散步甚至从窗户看到树木可以减轻压力、改善心情。对学生来说，绿色校园或附近的公园在长时间学习后提供休息心灵的地方。

生物多样性也受益。公园和林荫街道为鸟类和昆虫提供栖息地。当城市保护和扩大绿色区域时，即使在密集的城市环境中也能帮助维持生态平衡。

创建和保护城市绿地需要规划与公众支持。种树、维护公园、在新开发中为自然留出空间，都是可持续城市设计的一部分。公民可以通过照料本地树木、参加植树活动、支持优先考虑绿地的政策来做贡献。

有更多树木的城市不仅更美丽——它更健康、更凉爽、更宜居。每棵种下的树都是对城市生活未来的投资。🌱

在一座密集的城市里，空气污染很容易被仅仅当作引擎和工厂的问题，然而植物是同一个故事的一部分。叶子能挡住细尘，一排位置得当的树可以缓和一条嘈杂的路，也能缓和一条炎热的路。这并不意味着绿地可以代替更清洁的燃料或更好的公共交通。它意味着树木是更广泛计划中的切实伙伴，而不是事后添上的装饰。

好的规划会看谁能够到达一座公园，而不仅仅看宣传册上出现了多少棵树。高速公路另一侧的大花园，对一个没有安全人行横道的孩子可能没有多少用处。学校、诊所和住房附近更小的绿色口袋，反而能更好地服务日常生活。维护也很重要：一个灯坏了、被忽视的广场很快会让人觉得不安全，于是心理和社区的益处就会消退。

城市中的生物多样性不是奢侈品。鸟类、昆虫甚至土壤中的生命，能让公园不至于变成一片沉默的草坪。本地物种、更少的化学喷剂，以及小路边缘一点点野性，都可以让一块小场地更丰富。学生可以通过参加植树日、认养行道树，或仅仅让校园花园不那么像一块地毯那样整齐，来提供帮助。

一座可持续的城市仍然需要建筑和道路。问题在于自然是否在那一设计里被留出空间。当城市绿地被当作基础设施——像水或电一样——健康、温度和归属感都会有更好的机会。

senior.title: 📖 The Purpose of Education Beyond Exams
senior.content:
For many students, education seems to mean exams, grades, and rankings. These things matter, but they are not the whole purpose of education. A deeper view of education can make learning more meaningful. 📖

Exams test knowledge and skills at a certain moment. They can motivate study and provide feedback. However, if education only focuses on scores, students may learn to memorise rather than understand, and to fear failure rather than learn from it. Real learning includes curiosity, the ability to ask questions, and the courage to explore unfamiliar topics.

Education also shapes character. Through group projects, sports, and community service, students practise cooperation, honesty, and responsibility. These qualities are hard to measure with a single test, but they influence how people live and work in society.

In a changing world, knowledge becomes outdated quickly. What lasts longer is the ability to learn independently—finding information, evaluating it, and applying it to new problems. Schools that encourage reading, discussion, and projects help build this lifelong learning capacity.

Parents and teachers can support this broader purpose by valuing effort and understanding, not only high marks. Students can support it by asking “why” and “how”, not only “what is the answer”. Education is not a race to the next exam; it is preparation for a thoughtful and useful life. 🌱

To develop as a person, a student needs rooms that an exam cannot fully measure: time to be curious, time to practise a skill badly before practising it well, and time to discover what kind of work feels meaningful. A timetable packed only with tests can shrink those rooms until learning becomes a short-term performance. The score may rise, while the wish to keep studying quietly falls.

This is not an argument against standards. Clear goals and honest feedback help people grow. The problem begins when the grade is treated as the only purpose, and everything that cannot be ranked is pushed aside. Character, collaboration and independent judgement then become decorations in a speech, not habits in a week. Society later meets young adults who can sit a paper but hesitate when a problem has no mark scheme.

Schools can protect a broader purpose in ordinary ways: projects that last more than one lesson, discussions in which a good question is welcomed, and chances to serve or to make something that someone else will use. Parents can ask what was interesting today, not only what was scored. Students can keep a private list of questions that no test has asked yet.

Education should help people live thoughtfully with others, and keep learning when the course is over. If we remember that purpose, exams can remain useful tools instead of becoming the whole map. The aim is not to escape assessment, but to develop a mind that is larger than the next paper.
senior.translation:
对许多学生来说，教育似乎意味着考试、分数和排名。这些东西重要，但它们不是教育的全部目的。对教育更深入的看法可以让学习更有意义。📖

考试在特定时刻测试知识和技能。它们可以激励学习并提供反馈。然而，如果教育只关注分数，学生可能学会死记硬背而不是理解，害怕失败而不是从中学习。真正的学习包括好奇心、提问的能力，以及探索陌生主题的勇气。

教育也塑造品格。通过小组项目、运动和社区服务，学生练习合作、诚实和责任。这些品质很难用一次考试衡量，但它们影响人们在社会中如何生活和工作。

在变化的世界中，知识很快过时。更持久的是独立学习的能力——寻找信息、评估信息，并将其应用于新问题。鼓励阅读、讨论和项目的学校有助于建立这种终身学习能力。

家长和老师可以通过看重努力和理解、而不只是高分来支持这一更广泛的目的。学生可以通过问“为什么”和“怎么做”、而不只是“答案是什么”来支持它。教育不是奔向下一次考试的竞赛；它是为深思熟虑、有用的人生做准备。🌱

要作为一个完整的人去发展，学生需要一些考试无法完全测量的空间：好奇的时间，在把一项技能做好之前先把它做糟的时间，以及发现什么样的工作让人觉得有意义的时间。一张只塞满测验的时间表，会把这些空间挤小，直到学习变成一场短期表演。分数也许会上升，而继续安静学习的愿望却悄悄下降。

这并不是反对标准的论点。清楚的目标和诚实的反馈帮助人成长。问题开始于把分数当作唯一目的，并把一切无法排名的东西推到一边。于是品格、协作和独立判断变成演讲里的装饰，而不是一周里的习惯。社会随后遇到的是能够坐下来考试、却在一个没有评分标准的问题前犹豫的年轻人。

学校可以用平常的方式保护更广阔的目的：持续超过一节课的项目，欢迎好问题的讨论，以及服务他人或做出别人会使用的东西的机会。父母可以问今天什么有趣，而不仅仅问什么被打了分。学生可以私下保存一份还没有被任何考试问过的问题清单。

教育应当帮助人们与他人一起有思考地生活，并在课程结束之后继续学习。如果我们记得这个目的，考试就可以仍然是有用的工具，而不是整张地图。目标不是逃避评价，而是发展出一个比下一张试卷更大的头脑。

senior.title: 📱 Digital Minimalism: Using Technology on Purpose
senior.content:
Smartphones and apps are designed to hold our attention. Endless feeds, notifications, and short videos can fill every free minute. Digital minimalism is the idea of using technology deliberately—keeping tools that serve clear purposes and reducing the rest. 📱

Many students check their phones without thinking: while walking, during meals, or in the middle of homework. This constant switching makes deep focus harder. Research suggests that frequent interruptions reduce the quality of study and increase stress.

Digital minimalism does not mean rejecting all technology. It means choosing. Keep the apps you need for study, communication with family, and genuine hobbies. Remove or limit apps that only consume time without clear benefit. Turn off non-essential notifications. Set specific times to check messages instead of responding to every sound.

Practical steps can help. Put the phone in another room during focused study. Use grayscale mode or app timers to reduce the pull of colourful icons. Replace some scrolling time with reading, exercise, or conversation. Even small changes—one phone-free hour a day—can improve concentration and mood.

Technology is a tool. When we control it with intention, it supports our goals. When it controls us, it drains attention and time. Learning to use digital tools on purpose is a modern skill that protects the ability to think and live more fully. 🌱

A deliberate habit of attention is the heart of digital minimalism. The point is not to feel superior for owning fewer apps, but to protect the hours in which you can think. Distraction is cheap and always available; focus has to be arranged. If you wait to feel “ready,” the next notification will usually arrive first.

Balance does not mean a perfect average of online and offline time. It means that tools serve a purpose you could explain to a friend. A group chat that organises a project is different from a feed that you open only because your hand is restless. Naming the purpose makes it easier to close the tool when the purpose is done. Some students choose a phone-free breakfast, or a Sunday morning without feeds, not as a punishment but as a way to remember what their own thoughts sound like.

Environment still beats willpower. Charge the device outside the bedroom. Keep a paper book or a notebook where the phone used to sit. Tell a roommate or a parent the hours you mean to keep, so that the plan is not only a private wish. When you slip, restart the next block of time without a long speech of failure.

Used this way, technology can shrink back to a useful size. Digital minimalism is less a style than a repeated choice: I will give my attention on purpose, and I will not let a habit of checking spend it for me.
senior.translation:
智能手机和应用被设计成抓住我们的注意力。无尽的信息流、通知和短视频可以填满每一分钟空闲。数字极简主义是刻意使用技术的理念——保留服务明确目的的工具，减少其余的。📱

许多学生不假思索地看手机：走路时、吃饭时，或做作业中间。这种不断切换使深度专注更难。研究表明，频繁打断会降低学习质量并增加压力。

数字极简主义并不意味着拒绝所有技术。它意味着选择。保留学习、与家人沟通和真正爱好所需的应用。删除或限制只消耗时间而无明确益处的应用。关闭非必要通知。设定特定时间查看消息，而不是对每个声音都回应。

切实步骤有帮助。专注学习时把手机放在另一个房间。使用灰度模式或应用计时器减少彩色图标的吸引力。把一些刷屏时间换成阅读、锻炼或交谈。即使是小改变——每天一小时无手机——也能改善专注和心情。

技术是工具。当我们有意图地控制它时，它支持我们的目标。当它控制我们时，它消耗注意力和时间。学会有目的地使用数字工具，是保护思考与更充实地生活的现代技能。🌱

一种有意识的注意习惯，是数字极简主义的核心。重点不是因为少拥有几个应用而感到优越，而是保护那些你可以思考的小时。分心很便宜，而且随时可得；专注却必须被安排。如果你等待自己“准备好了”，下一条通知通常会先到。

平衡并不意味着线上和线下时间完美各半。它意味着工具服务于一个你可以对朋友解释的目的。一个组织项目的群聊，不同于仅仅因为手无处安放而打开的信息流。说出目的，会让你在目的完成时更容易关掉工具。有些学生选择一段没有手机的早餐，或一个没有信息流的星期日早晨，不是作为惩罚，而是为了记起自己的想法听起来是什么样的。

环境仍然胜过意志力。在卧室外面给设备充电。在手机曾经放着的地方放一本纸书或一个笔记本。把你打算遵守的时段告诉室友或父母，好让计划不只是一个私下的愿望。当你滑倒时，不要发表很长的失败演说，直接从下一段时间重新开始。

这样使用，技术就可以收缩回一个有用的尺寸。数字极简主义与其说是一种风格，不如说是一种重复的选择：我将有目的地给出我的注意力，而不会让一种查看的习惯替我把它花掉。
