senior.title: 🛤️ Coping That Moves You Through, Not Around, a Problem
senior.content:
When stress arrives, the mind reaches for a coping style the way a hand reaches for a familiar tool. Some tools move a person through the problem: naming it, breaking it into steps, seeking information, having a difficult conversation, or changing a schedule. Other tools move a person around it: endless scrolling, denial, sharp jokes that close the subject, overwork in a different area, or a promise to “deal with it later” that later never reaches. Psychological resilience is closely tied to this choice. Avoidance can be merciful for a night, when rest is needed before a clearer morning. When avoidance becomes the main method, problems grow in the dark, anxiety has more room, and self-trust shrinks because the person can no longer point to a history of facing things.

Psychologists often distinguish problem-focused coping, which tries to change the situation, from emotion-focused coping, which tries to change the intensity of feeling so that thought remains possible. Both can be healthy. A student who first sleeps, breathes, or talks until the panic drops, and then writes an email to a teacher, is using a sequence, not escaping. A student who only calms the feeling and never sends the email is stuck in the first half. The same is true of the reverse: a rush into action without any regulation can produce a messy confrontation that creates a second problem. Resilience is less a single heroic act than a flexible sequence that fits the moment.

Judging a strategy requires honesty about the goal. If the goal is to feel nothing, almost any distraction will seem to work and then fail. If the goal is to keep dignity, relationships and a path forward, the strategy must eventually touch the real difficulty. Writing a list, rehearsing a conversation, asking for a deadline, or leaving a harmful setting are examples of approach. So is choosing, after clear thought, to accept a loss that cannot be reversed, and to grieve it rather than bargain forever. Acceptance is not the same as avoidance. Avoidance pretends the loss is not there. Acceptance sees it and still walks.

Culture can push people toward stylish avoidance: a joke, a busy badge, a performance of being fine. Friends can interrupt that performance with a quiet, specific question and a willingness to stay after the answer. Schools can teach coping as a set of options, not as a single sermon about positivity. Students can keep a private record for a week: when stress rose, what I did, and whether the problem was smaller the next day. Patterns appear faster on paper than in mood.

If a person cannot approach a problem even in a small step, or if the only tools left are self-harm, substances, or complete withdrawal, professional help is part of coping, not a failure of it. Resilience is not the absence of fear. It is the practised return to a path that goes through the difficulty, at a pace a human being can survive, with enough support that the path does not have to be invented alone every time.
senior.translation:
当压力到来时，头脑会伸向一种应对风格，就像手伸向一件熟悉的工具。有些工具把人带过问题：给它命名，把它拆成步骤，寻求信息，进行一次困难的谈话，或改变一份时间表。另一些工具把人带著绕过它：无尽的滑动屏幕，否认，把话题关掉的尖锐笑话，在另一个领域里过度工作，或一个“稍后再处理”、而后来从未到达的承诺。心理韧性与这种选择紧密相连。回避在一个夜里可以是仁慈的，当更清楚的早晨之前需要休息时。当回避成为主要方法时，问题在黑暗中生长，焦虑有了更多空间，自我信任也会缩小，因为这个人不再能指向一段面对事物的历史。

心理学家常常区分问题聚焦的应对——试图改变情境，与情绪聚焦的应对——试图改变感觉的强度，好让思考仍然可能。两者都可以是健康的。一个学生先睡觉、呼吸或交谈，直到惊恐下降，然后再给老师写一封邮件，是在使用一种顺序，而不是在逃避。一个只平静感觉、却永远不发邮件的学生，卡在了前半段。反过来也是如此：没有任何调节就冲进行动，可能产生一次制造第二个问题的混乱对抗。韧性与其说是单独一个英雄式的行动，不如说是适合这一刻的灵活顺序。

判断一种策略，需要对目标保持诚实。如果目标是什么都感觉不到，几乎任何分心都会看起来有效，然后失败。如果目标是保持尊严、关系和一条向前的路，策略最终必须触碰到真正的困难。写一份清单，排练一次谈话，请求一个截止日期，或离开一个有害的环境，都是接近的例子。在清楚思考之后，选择接受一个无法逆转的失去，并哀悼它，而不是永远讨价还价，也是如此。接受并不等于回避。回避假装失去不在那里。接受看见它，却仍然向前走。

文化可能把人推向一种时髦的回避：一个笑话，一枚忙碌的徽章，一场“我很好”的表演。朋友可以用一个安静而具体的问题，以及在答案之后留下来的意愿，打断那场表演。学校可以把应对教成一套选项，而不是一篇关于积极思考的单独训词。学生可以保留一周的私人记录：压力何时上升，我做了什么，以及第二天问题是否更小。模式在纸上比在心情里出现得更快。

如果一个人即使在一小步里也不能接近一个问题，或如果剩下的唯一工具是自我伤害、成瘾物质，或完全退缩，那么专业帮助就是应对的一部分，而不是它的失败。韧性不是没有恐惧。它是一次次练习回到一条穿过困难的路，以一个人类能够存活的节奏，并带有足够的支持，好让这条路不必每次都被独自发明。

questions.q: 1. How do approach and avoidance differ as coping tools?
options: Avoidance always builds a history of facing things and raises self-trust
Scrolling, denial and ‘later’ are the best long-term tools
Approach names the problem and takes steps through it; avoidance goes around it, which may be merciful for a night but, as a main method, lets problems and anxiety grow

questions.q: 2. Why can both problem-focused and emotion-focused coping be healthy?
options: Only a rush into action without regulation is healthy
A sequence — first reducing panic so thought is possible, then acting, such as writing the email — fits the moment, while using only one half can leave a person stuck or create a second problem
Only calming the feeling, and never sending the email, counts as resilience
A single heroic act is always better than a flexible sequence
questions.exp: 文中举例先调节情绪再行动是健康顺序，只做一半或毫无调节地冲上会卡住或制造新问题。

questions.q: 3. How does acceptance differ from avoidance when a loss cannot be reversed?
options: Acceptance sees the loss and still walks; avoidance pretends the loss is not there
Acceptance is the same as pretending nothing happened
If the goal is to feel nothing, acceptance is just another distraction that always fails
Bargaining forever is the same as a path forward

questions.q: 4. What week-long record can help students see their pattern?
options: A sermon about positivity with no options listed
A performance of being fine, with no specific question from a friend
A private record that ignores whether the problem changed
When stress rose, what I did, and whether the problem was smaller the next day

options: When fear is present, because resilience means the absence of fear
When support is already enough that the path never needs to be walked
When a person cannot take even a small approach step, or when the only tools left are self-harm, substances or complete withdrawal
When the person can already invent the path alone every time

senior.title: 🛡️ Steelman, Not Strawman: Practising the Strongest Version of a View

steelmanning.cn: 钢人化；以最强形式重述

senior.content:
A common move in argument is the straw man: you restate an opposing view in a weaker, sillier form, then knock that form down and claim victory. The move is easy, popular, and almost useless as training for thought. It teaches speed, not accuracy, and it leaves you unprepared for a real opponent who does not actually hold the cartoon you defeated. The opposite exercise is sometimes called steelmanning: you state the other view in its strongest, fairest form, so strong that a thoughtful supporter might recognise it, and only then do you reply. Mental training of this kind is uncomfortable, because it may reveal that the other side has a point, or that your own case needs more work. That discomfort is a sign that thinking is happening.

The method has a simple sequence. First, listen or read long enough to understand the claim, the reasons, and the values underneath, not only a slogan. Second, restate the claim in your own words, including the best evidence or the most serious worry the other person offered. Third, ask whether they would accept your restatement. If they would not, you have not yet earned the right to attack. Fourth, answer the strong version, not a side issue. You may still disagree completely. The point is that your disagreement will then be aimed at the real target, which is the only kind that can change anyone’s mind, including yours.

Steelmanning is not the same as surrender, and it is not required in every setting. A bully, a scammer, or a flood of bad-faith noise does not deserve an unlimited charitable rewrite. The exercise is for conversations in which truth, or at least a workable decision, is the goal: a seminar, a team plan, a family dispute about a real choice, a news issue with two serious sides. In those rooms, a habit of fighting only the weakest version produces heat and no light. A habit of fighting the strongest version produces better plans, better essays, and a reputation for fairness that makes later disagreement easier to hear.

Students can practise in low-stakes ways. After a class debate, write one paragraph “as if I held the other view,” and have a classmate check it for fairness before you write your critique. When you read an opinion you dislike, pause and list the concern that would still matter even if every insult were removed. In a group project, appoint someone to steelman a rejected option for two minutes before the team drops it. These drills train attention, memory and intellectual honesty together.

A mind that can only win against a scarecrow will be helpless in a serious world. A mind that can rebuild another person’s case, and then still say no with reasons, has a kind of strength that volume cannot replace. Thinking, at its best, is not a sport of humiliation. It is a craft of getting closer to what is true, even when the shortest path would be to mishear.
senior.translation:
争论里一种常见的动作是稻草人：你把对立的观点重述成一种更弱、更可笑的形式，然后把那种形式打倒，并宣称胜利。这种动作容易、流行，作为思维训练却几乎无用。它教的是速度，不是准确，并让你对一个并不真的持有你所击败的漫画的真实对手毫无准备。相反的练习有时被叫做钢人化：你以最强、最公平的形式陈述另一方的观点，强到一位有思考的支持者也许会认出它，然后你才回答。这类思维训练是不舒服的，因为它可能揭示出另一方有一个要点，或你自己的论证需要更多工作。那种不适是思考正在发生的标志。

这种方法有一个简单的顺序。第一，听或读得足够久，以理解主张、理由和底下的价值，而不仅仅是一句口号。第二，用你自己的话重述主张，包括对方提供的最好证据或最严肃的担忧。第三，问他们是否会接受你的重述。如果他们不会，你就还没有赢得进攻的权利。第四，回答那个强的版本，而不是一个旁支问题。你仍然可以完全不同意。重点是，你的不同意那时会瞄准真正的目标，而那是唯一能够改变任何人心——包括你自己的心——的种类。

钢人化并不等于投降，也并不在每一种场合都被要求。一个霸凌者、一个骗子，或一场充满恶意噪音的洪水，不值得无限的善意改写。这种练习是为那些以真理、或至少一个可行决定为目标的谈话准备的：一次研讨课，一个团队计划，一场关于真实选择的家庭争论，一个有两方都严肃的新闻议题。在那些房间里，只与最弱版本战斗的习惯会产生热、没有光。与最强版本战斗的习惯会产生更好的计划、更好的文章，以及一种使后来的分歧更容易被听见的公平名声。

学生可以用低风险的方式练习。在一次课堂辩论之后，写一段“就好像我持有另一个观点”，并在写批评之前让同学检查它是否公平。当你读到一篇你不喜欢的评论时，停下来列出即使所有侮辱被去掉也仍然重要的那种关切。在小组项目里，指定某个人在团队放弃一个被拒绝的选项之前，用两分钟把它钢人化。这些训练同时训练注意力、记忆和智识上的诚实。

一个只能打败稻草人的头脑，在一个严肃的世界里会无能为力。一个能够重建另一个人的论证、然后仍然带着理由说不的头脑，拥有一种音量无法代替的力量。在最好的情况下，思考不是一场羞辱的运动。它是一种更接近真实的手艺，即使最短的路会是听错。

It teaches accuracy rather than speed

In the face of a bully, a scammer, or bad-faith noise that does not deserve an unlimited charitable rewrite
Whenever truth or a workable decision is the goal

options: The strength of winning only against a scarecrow
The strength of the shortest path, which is to mishear

senior.title: 👁️ Separating What You Saw from What You Concluded
senior.content:
A great deal of sloppy thinking begins with a small, almost invisible leap: we report a conclusion as if it were an observation. “He ignored me” may be what we felt; what we saw was that a message was not answered for three hours. “The experiment failed because the theory is wrong” may be a possible story; what we saw was that the liquid did not change colour. Mental training that separates observation from inference sounds pedantic until it prevents a fight, a bad lab report, or a rumour that runs through a class. The discipline is not a denial of intuition. It is a pause that asks, “What did I actually see, hear, or measure — and what did I add?”

The added part is often reasonable, and still should be labelled. Inferences are how we make sense of incomplete data; we cannot live by raw sense impressions alone. Trouble starts when the label falls off, and a guess hardens into “what happened.” Witnesses confidently describe a motive they did not see. Readers treat a headline’s frame as a fact. Friends hear a tone in a short text that may not have been there. In science, a result is an observation; the explanation is a model that must compete with others. In daily life the same split is available, if we are willing to use plainer sentences: I saw this; I think this; I am not sure.

A practical drill is to write two columns, or to say them aloud in a disagreement. Column A: the evidence available to more than my mood — words said, times recorded, measurements taken, a message that can be shown. Column B: my interpretations, fears, and preferred stories. Then ask what else could sit in column B given the same A. If several stories fit, certainty should drop. If a story cannot point back to A, it should not be presented as a report. This is not coldness. It is respect for the other person’s reality and for your own future self, who may have to revise the tale.

Teachers can require the split in essays and labs: first the data, then the claim, with a word such as “suggests” rather than “proves” when the leap is large. Students can practise it in smaller rooms — a sports disagreement, a group-chat conflict, a news clip. Ask, “If I had no theory, what would I still be willing to swear I observed?” The answer is usually shorter than the first angry paragraph, and more useful.

A mind trained in this way becomes slower in a good sense and faster in another: slower to accuse, faster to notice when someone else has smuggled a conclusion into a description. Thinking clearly is not the same as thinking unkindly. It is the habit of keeping the world and our story about the world in two hands, so that when new evidence arrives, we know which hand to open.
senior.translation:
大量潦草的思考，开始于一个几乎看不见的小小跳跃：我们把一个结论报告得仿佛它是一次观察。“他忽视了我”也许是我们所感觉到的；我们所看见的，是一条消息三个小时没有被回复。“实验失败是因为理论是错的”也许是一个可能的故事；我们所看见的，是液体没有变色。把观察与推论分开的思维训练，听起来像学究，直到它防止一场争吵、一份糟糕的实验报告，或一个跑过全班的谣言。这种纪律不是对直觉的否认。它是一次停顿，问：“我实际上看见、听见或测量了什么——以及我添加了什么？”

被添加的部分常常是合理的，却仍然应当被贴上标签。推论是我们理解不完整数据的方式；我们不能只靠原始的感觉印象生活。麻烦开始于标签掉落，而一个猜测硬化成“发生了什么。”证人自信地描述一个他们并未看见的动机。读者把标题的框架当作事实。朋友在一条短讯里听见一种也许并不存在的语气。在科学里，结果是观察；解释是必须与其他解释竞争的模型。在日常生活里，同一种分开也是可用的，只要我们愿意使用更朴素的句子：我看见了这个；我认为这个；我不确定。

一个实际的训练是写下两栏，或在一次分歧里把它们说出来。A栏：不只属于我的心情、也可以被他人使用的证据——说过的话，记录的时间，做过的测量，一条可以出示的消息。B栏：我的解释、恐惧和偏爱的故事。然后问，在同样的A之下，还有什么可以坐在B栏里。如果几个故事都适合，确定性就应当下降。如果一个故事不能指回A，它就不应当被当作报告来呈现。这不是冷漠。这是对另一个人的现实的尊重，也是对未来那个也许必须修正这个故事的自己的尊重。

老师可以在作文和实验里要求这种分开：先是数据，然后是主张，并在跳跃很大时使用“表明”而不是“证明”这样的词。学生可以在更小的房间里练习它——一次体育上的分歧，一场群聊冲突，一段新闻片段。问：“如果我没有理论，我仍然愿意发誓我观察到了什么？”答案通常比第一段愤怒的文字更短，也更有用。

以这种方式训练过的头脑，在一种好的意义上变得更慢，在另一种意义上变得更快：更慢去指责，更快注意到别人何时把一个结论偷运进一段描述。清楚的思考并不等于不善意的思考。它是把世界和我们关于世界的故事分拿在两只手里的习惯，好让新的证据到来时，我们知道该打开哪一只手。

questions.q: 1. What small leap does the passage say starts a great deal of sloppy thinking?
options: Reporting a conclusion as if it were an observation, such as ‘he ignored me’ when what was seen was an unanswered message
Refusing ever to add an inference to raw sense impressions
Treating ‘the liquid did not change colour’ as already proving a theory wrong
Denying intuition in every case, with no pause
questions.exp: 文中举例把“他忽视我”当作观察，而实际看见的只是消息三小时未回复。

questions.q: 2. Why should inferences still be used, but labelled?
options: We can live by raw sense impressions alone, so labels are unnecessary
A headline’s frame should be treated as a fact
A motive that was not seen can be confidently reported as observation
They help us make sense of incomplete data, yet trouble starts when a guess hardens into ‘what happened’ without a label
questions.exp: 文中说推论是理解不完整数据的方式，但标签掉落后猜测会硬化成“发生了什么”。

questions.q: 3. What belongs in column A and column B of the drill?
options: A: fears only; B: measurements only
A: any story that cannot point back to evidence; B: nothing
A: evidence available beyond mood, such as words, times, measurements, a message that can be shown; B: interpretations, fears and preferred stories
A and B as the same list, so certainty never drops
questions.exp: 文中把A栏定为可出示的证据，B栏定为解释与恐惧，并问同一A下还有哪些故事能成立。

questions.q: 4. What question can shrink an angry first paragraph?
options: Which conclusion can I smuggle into the description fastest?
If I had no theory, what would I still be willing to swear I observed?
How can I prove, not merely suggest, when the leap is large?
How can I keep data and claim unseparated in a lab report?
questions.exp: 文中建议问：若没有理论，我仍愿意发誓观察到了什么，答案通常更短也更有用。

questions.q: 5. What two-handed habit does the ending recommend?
options: Keeping the world and our story about the world in two hands, so that when new evidence arrives we know which hand to open
Thinking unkindly, because clear thinking requires coldness
Opening both hands at once, so a conclusion and an observation stay fused
Accusing faster, and noticing smuggled conclusions more slowly
questions.exp: 文中说清楚思考是把世界和我们关于世界的故事分拿在两只手里，好知道新证据来时打开哪一只。

senior.title: ✍️ Writing to Find Out What You Think
senior.content:
People often treat writing as the last step of thinking: first you know, then you type. Anyone who has tried to explain a difficult idea on paper has met the opposite truth. Sentences refuse to form, a hidden gap appears, two claims collide, or a word you were using turns out to be a fog. Writing, in this sense, is not decoration after thought. It is one of the most reliable tools for training thought, because it forces the vague to become visible. A feeling of understanding can survive in the head for days. It rarely survives a request to put the idea in a paragraph that another person could follow.

The method is humble and repeatable. Begin with a messy page: questions, fragments, examples, and the best sentence you can currently manage, even if it is wrong. Then walk through that page as an editor of your own mind. Circle a term that has not been defined. Mark a leap that has no reason. Ask whether each paragraph has one job, and whether the next paragraph really follows. Read the draft aloud; the ear catches knots that the eye forgives. Replace a vague verb with a more precise one, not to sound impressive, but to find out whether you actually know the action you are describing. If you cannot finish a sentence, you have found the exact edge of the thought.

Different forms train different muscles. A two-sentence summary tests whether you can name the core. A paragraph that includes an objection tests whether you have considered another side. A letter to a younger student tests whether you can leave jargon behind. A lab-style report tests whether evidence and claim have been kept in the right order. None of these is only a school task. Scientists, judges, designers and ordinary citizens who must make a decision all use some version of the same pressure: say it clearly enough that it can be checked.

There is a social dimension. Writing that will be read, even by one classmate, raises the standard of honesty, because a hole is harder to hide. At the same time, an early draft should be allowed to be ugly, or the fear of being seen will stop the thinking before it starts. A useful habit is to separate a private discovery draft from a later public one, and to give each its own time. Feedback is most helpful when it points to a specific unclarity, not only to taste.

Students can keep a thinking notebook that is not for marks: one idea, one page, twice a week. Date it, and return a month later to see whether the later you can still understand the earlier you. If not, the writing has already done part of its work: it has shown that the thought was not yet finished. To train the mind is, often, to give it a page and the courage to look at what the page refuses to pretend.
senior.translation:
人们常常把写作当作思考的最后一步：你先知道，然后再打字。任何曾经试图在纸上解释一个困难想法的人，都遇到过相反的真相。句子拒绝成形，一个隐藏的缺口出现，两个主张相撞，或一个你一直在使用的词原来是一团雾。在这个意义上，写作不是思考之后的装饰。它是训练思考最可靠的工具之一，因为它迫使模糊变得可见。一种理解的感觉可以在头脑里存活许多天。它很少能在“把这个想法放进另一个人能够跟随的一段里”这一要求下存活。

这种方法是谦逊而可重复的。从凌乱的一页开始：问题，碎片，例子，以及你当前能够管理的最好句子，即使它是错的。然后作为自己头脑的编辑，走过那一页。圈出一个尚未被定义的术语。标记一次没有理由的跳跃。问每一段是否有一个任务，以及下一段是否真的跟得上。把草稿读出声；耳朵会抓住眼睛原谅的结。用一个更精确的动词替换一个模糊的动词，不是为了听起来惊人，而是为了弄清你是否真的知道自己正在描述的那个动作。如果你不能完成一个句子，你就找到了这个想法的精确边缘。

不同的形式训练不同的肌肉。两句摘要测试你是否能说出核心。一段包含异议的文字测试你是否考虑过另一面。一封写给更小学生的信测试你是否能把行话留下。一份实验式的报告测试证据和主张是否被放在正确的顺序里。这些都不只是学校任务。必须做出决定的科学家、法官、设计师和普通公民，都在使用某种版本的同样压力：把它说得足够清楚，以便能够被检查。

这里有一种社会的层面。将被阅读的写作，即使只被一位同学阅读，也会提高诚实的标准，因为一个洞更难隐藏。同时，早期草稿应当被允许是难看的，否则害怕被看见会在思考开始之前就把它停下。一个有用的习惯是把私人的发现草稿和稍后的公开稿分开，并给每一份它自己的时间。当反馈指向一个具体的不清楚之处、而不仅仅是趣味时，它是最有帮助的。

学生可以保留一本不算分的思考笔记本：一个想法，一页纸，每周两次。写上日期，并在一个月后回来看，后来的你是否仍然能理解较早的你。如果不能，写作已经做了它工作的一部分：它已经显示，这个想法当时还没有完成。训练头脑，常常就是给它一页纸，以及去看这页纸拒绝假装什么的勇气。

questions.q: 1. Why can writing be a tool for training thought, not only a last step after thinking?
options: You always know first, and then you simply type
It forces the vague to become visible: gaps, collisions and foggy words appear, and a feeling of understanding may not survive a clear paragraph
A feeling of understanding in the head is already enough for another person to follow
Sentences that refuse to form are only decoration problems
questions.exp: 文中说写作迫使模糊可见，头脑里的理解感很少能在写成他人可跟随的段落时存活。

questions.q: 2. What should you do with a messy first page?
options: Edit it as your own mind: circle undefined terms, mark leaps without reasons, check that paragraphs follow, read aloud, and use a more precise verb to test whether you know the action
Keep every vague verb, so that the action stays unexamined
Avoid reading aloud, because the ear is less strict than the eye
Finish every sentence even when you have not found the edge of the thought
questions.exp: 文中建议作为自己的编辑：圈未定义术语、标记无理由跳跃、检查段落、读出声，并用更精确的动词检验是否真懂。

questions.q: 3. How do different forms train different muscles?
options: Only school tasks use the pressure to say something clearly enough to be checked
Jargon should stay in a letter to a younger student
Evidence and claim should be kept in a mixed order in a report
A two-sentence summary, a paragraph with an objection, a letter without jargon, and a lab-style report each test a different clarity, and all apply beyond school
questions.exp: 文中列举两句摘要、含异议的段落、给年幼学生的信和实验报告各自训练不同能力。

questions.q: 4. Why separate a private discovery draft from a later public one?
options: Feedback is best when it points only to taste, never to a specific unclarity
Every draft should be public from the first line
An early draft should be allowed to be ugly, or fear of being seen will stop the thinking, while a later reader still raises the standard of honesty
Writing that will be read makes holes easier to hide
questions.exp: 文中建议把私人发现草稿和稍后公开稿分开：早期允许难看，以免害怕被看见而停住思考。

questions.q: 5. What can a dated thinking notebook show a month later?
options: That marks are the only reason to write one idea twice a week
Whether the later you can still understand the earlier you — and if not, that the thought was not yet finished
That a finished thought never needs a page
That the page should pretend the thought was complete
questions.exp: 文中建议一本不算分的笔记本，一个月后看后来的自己是否还能理解；若不能，说明当时想法尚未完成。

senior.title: 🏆 Survivorship Bias: What We Miss When We Study Only the Winners
senior.content:
Advice about success is often built from portraits of people who made it: the founder who dropped out and became rich, the athlete who trained at dawn, the artist who was rejected twenty times and then celebrated. These stories can be inspiring, and they can also be systematically misleading. Survivorship bias is the error of drawing a lesson from the cases that remain visible, while the many similar cases that failed have quietly left the stage. If we only interview the survivors, we may praise habits that were common among the unsuccessful too, or we may miss the role of luck, timing, and conditions that no longer exist. Critical thinking asks a blunt question of every success story: what about the people who did the same thing and did not appear in the magazine?

The bias is not only a matter of celebrity. In medicine, a treatment may look effective if we study only the patients who returned for a follow-up, because those who worsened may have disappeared from the records. In history, we read the letters that were saved, not the ones that were thrown away. In school, we hear from graduates who entered famous universities, and less often from equally hard-working students whose results were ordinary. A graph of “companies that lasted a hundred years” cannot, by itself, tell you the chance that a new company will last, because the dead companies are not in the picture. Whenever a sample is selected by outcome, the lesson is at risk.

The correction is not cynicism. It is a demand for a better denominator: how many tried, under what conditions, and what happened to the rest? Sometimes the data exist and are ignored because they are less glamorous. Sometimes the data cannot be fully recovered, which should make our claims more modest, not more certain. Comparing winners with a fair control group, looking for disconfirming cases, and asking whether a factor was present in failures as well as in successes are ordinary tools of critical thought. They take a little of the shine off a myth, and they give a clearer map to anyone who actually has to decide.

Students can practise on everyday claims. A classmate says a certain app, diet, or study trick “worked for everyone I know.” Ask how the circle was formed, and whether those who quietly stopped would still be in it. A news feature follows three start-ups that bloomed; search, if you can, for how many similar start-ups were launched in the same year. A historical hero is praised for a risky choice; ask how many made that choice and vanished. The point is not to sneer at success. The point is to learn from a fuller set of lives than the ones that remain in the light.

Critical thinking, here, is a kind of respect for the invisible. The world is full of silent data: the books that did not sell, the treatments that did not work, the applications that were not accepted. A mind that remembers those absences will be slower to copy a glamorous method, and faster to ask for evidence that includes the missing. That slowness is not a lack of ambition. It is how ambition avoids building a plan on a stage from which the unsuccessful have already been cleared.
senior.translation:
关于成功的建议，常常建立在那些成功了的人的肖像上：退学后变得富有的创始人，黎明训练的运动员，被拒绝二十次然后被庆祝的艺术家。这些故事可以鼓舞人，也可以系统地误导人。幸存者偏差，是从仍然可见的案例中引出一课、而许多曾经相似、却已安静离开舞台的失败案例被忽略的错误。如果我们只采访幸存者，我们也许会赞美那些在不成功的人当中也同样常见的习惯，或我们也许会错过运气、时机，以及那些已不再存在的条件的作用。批判思维对每一个成功故事提出一个直率的问题：那些做了同样的事、却没有出现在杂志里的人呢？

这种偏差不仅仅是名流的问题。在医学里，一种治疗可能看起来有效，如果我们只研究那些回来复查的病人，因为那些恶化的人可能已经从记录里消失。在历史里，我们阅读被保存下来的信，而不是被扔掉的信。在学校里，我们听到进入名牌大学的毕业生，却较少听到同样努力、结果却平常的学生。一张“存在了一百年的公司”的图，本身并不能告诉你一家新公司将会存在下去的机会，因为死去的公司不在图画里。每当一个样本是按结果被选出来的，这一课就处于风险之中。

纠正并不是犬儒。它是对一个更好的分母的要求：有多少人尝试过，在什么条件下，其余的人发生了什么？有时数据存在，却因为不那么光彩而被忽略。有时数据不能被完全恢复，而这应当使我们的主张更谦逊，而不是更确定。把成功者与一个公平的对照组比较，寻找反例，并询问一个因素是否在失败和成功里都存在，是批判思考的平常工具。它们会从神话上取走一点光泽，却给任何真正必须做决定的人一张更清楚的地图。

学生可以在日常主张上练习。一位同学说某个应用、饮食或学习窍门“对我认识的每个人都有效。”问这个圈子是如何形成的，以及那些安静停下来的人是否还会在里面。一篇新闻特写跟随三家绽放的初创公司；如果可以，就去搜索同一年里有多少相似的公司被创办。一位历史英雄因一次冒险的选择被赞美；问有多少人做了那个选择然后消失了。重点不是嘲笑成功。重点是从比仍留在光里的那些更完整的一组生命中学习。

在这里，批判思维是一种对不可见者的尊重。世界充满沉默的数据：没有卖出去的书，没有起作用的治疗，没有被接受的申请。一个记得那些缺席的头脑，会更慢去复制一种光彩的方法，也更快去要求包括失踪者的证据。那种慢并不是缺少抱负。它是抱负如何避免把计划建立在一个不成功者已经被清理出去的舞台上。

questions.q: 1. What is survivorship bias, according to the passage?
options: Interviewing only the unsuccessful, and never the people in the magazine
A rare error that appears only in celebrity stories, never in medicine or school
Drawing a lesson from visible winners while similar cases that failed have left the stage, so we may praise habits that failures also had, or miss luck and vanished conditions
Proof that every dawn-training habit is sufficient for success
questions.exp: 文中把幸存者偏差定义为只从可见成功者取教训，而失败的相似案例已离开舞台。

questions.q: 2. Why can a graph of hundred-year companies not, by itself, give the chance a new company will last?
options: Because follow-up patients always include those who worsened
Because the sample is selected by outcome, and the dead companies are not in the picture
Because saved letters are a complete historical record
Because ordinary students are always as visible as famous graduates
questions.exp: 文中说明按结果选出的样本有风险，百年公司图里没有死去的公司。

questions.q: 3. What ‘better denominator’ does critical thinking demand?
options: How many tried, under what conditions, and what happened to the rest, plus comparison with failures and a fair control group when possible
More certainty when the data cannot be fully recovered
Ignoring less glamorous data that already exist
Copying the myth without looking for disconfirming cases
questions.exp: 文中要求更好的分母：多少人尝试、在什么条件下、其余人如何，并与失败案例和对照比较。

questions.q: 4. How can students practise on the claim that a trick ‘worked for everyone I know’?
options: Sneer at all success, and refuse to learn from any life
Accept the circle as a complete sample
Follow only the three start-ups that bloomed, with no search for the rest
Ask how the circle was formed, and whether those who quietly stopped would still be in it; similarly, ask how many similar start-ups launched in the same year
questions.exp: 文中建议追问圈子如何形成、退出者是否仍被计算，并对同年创办的相似公司进行搜索。

questions.q: 5. Why is remembering ‘silent data’ a form of respect, not a lack of ambition?
options: Ambition should ignore books that did not sell and applications that were not accepted
Speed in copying winners is the best map for anyone who has to decide
A mind that includes the missing will be slower to copy a glamorous method and less likely to build a plan on a stage already cleared of the unsuccessful
Invisible failures should stay invisible, so that myths keep their shine
questions.exp: 文中说记得缺席的沉默数据，是避免把计划建立在已清理掉失败者的舞台上，这不是缺少抱负。

senior.title: 👤 Why One Vivid Story Is Not the Same as Evidence
senior.content:
A single vivid story can move a room faster than a careful table of numbers. A neighbour’s child who improved after a certain treatment, a traveller who was cheated in one city, a classmate who studied all night and scored highly — such cases feel close, memorable, and therefore true. Critical thinking does not ask us to throw stories away. It asks us to know what they can and cannot do. An anecdote can raise a question, illustrate a mechanism, or remind us of a human cost. It cannot, by itself, establish how common a pattern is, what caused it, or whether the same action would work for someone else. When a story is asked to carry that heavier load, error is likely, because memory selects, emotion colours, and the unusual is more likely to be retold than the ordinary.

The problem is not that people lie, though sometimes they do. Even honest reports are samples of one, often without a clear comparison. The child might have improved anyway. The traveller’s bad day may be rare in that city. The classmate’s grade may have come from earlier work, not from the sleepless night. Without a base rate — how often the outcome happens when the action is absent — the story floats. Without attention to other cases that went the other way, it can survive as a rule. Advertising, rumours and some political speeches rely on this weakness: they offer a face, a name, and a dramatic before-and-after, and they hope the audience will not ask for the rest of the file.

A more careful habit is to let the story and the statistics sit side by side, each doing its proper job. If a medical claim is serious, look for reviews that collect many patients, not only a testimonial. If a school policy is said to “always work,” ask for numbers, including the students for whom it did not work. If a personal decision is being made with little data, a story may still be a reasonable starting clue, provided it is labelled as a clue. The standard should match the cost of being wrong. A restaurant tip can rest on one review; a health or safety choice should not.

Students can practise by rewriting a viral post in two columns: what the story actually says, and what it is being used to prove. Then add one question that a systematic study would have to answer. In class, they can be asked to invent a counter-anecdote that would fit a different conclusion, which shows how easy stories are to reverse. The exercise is not cynicism about people. It is respect for them: no one should have a life-changing decision hung on a tale that has not been tested against other lives.

Critical thinking, in the presence of a powerful story, is the ability to be moved and still to count. Feel the case; then ask how many, compared with what, and what else could be true. A mind that can do both will be harder to stampede and kinder in argument, because it will neither dismiss a person’s experience nor let that experience pretend to be a complete map of the world.
senior.translation:
一个生动的单独故事，可以比一张仔细的数字表更快地打动一间房间。邻居的孩子在某种治疗后好转，一位旅行者在一座城市里被骗，一位同学通宵学习并得了高分——这些案例感觉亲近、难忘，因此也感觉真实。批判思维并不要求我们把故事扔掉。它要求我们知道它们能做什么、不能做什么。一件轶事可以提出一个问题，说明一种机制，或提醒我们一种人的代价。它本身不能确定一种模式有多么常见，是什么导致了它，或同样的行动是否会对别人有效。当一个故事被要求去承担那更重的负荷时，错误就很可能，因为记忆会选择，情感会着色，而不寻常的事比平常的事更可能被重述。

问题并不在于人们说谎，尽管有时他们会。即使诚实的报告也是一份样本为的样本，常常没有清楚的比较。那个孩子也许本来就会好转。旅行者糟糕的一天在那座城市里也许很少见。同学的分数也许来自更早的工作，而不是那个不眠之夜。没有一个基础率——当行动不存在时，这个结果有多常发生——故事就会漂浮。如果不注意那些走向相反方向的其他案例，它就可以作为一条规则存活下去。广告、谣言和一些政治演说依赖这种弱点：它们提供一张脸、一个名字，以及一个戏剧性的前后对比，并希望听众不去要求档案的其余部分。

一个更小心的习惯，是让故事和统计并排而坐，各做各的本职。如果一项医学主张是严肃的，就寻找汇集许多患者的综述，而不仅仅是一份见证。如果一项学校政策被说成“总是有效”，就要求数字，包括那些对它无效的学生。如果一个个人决定是在很少数据的情况下做出的，一个故事仍然可以是一个合理的起始线索，只要它被标注为线索。标准应当匹配做错的代价。一条餐厅建议可以建立在一篇评论上；一个健康或安全的选择不应当如此。

学生可以通过把一条病毒式的帖子改写成两栏来练习：故事实际上说了什么，以及它被用来证明什么。然后再加上一个系统研究必须回答的问题。在课堂上，可以要求他们发明一个符合不同结论的反轶事，这会显示故事是多么容易被反转。这个练习不是对人的犬儒。它是对人的尊重：不应当让一个改变生活的决定，悬挂在一个尚未对照其他生命被检验过的故事上。

在一个有力的故事面前，批判思维是能够被打动、却仍然去计数的能力。感受这个案例；然后问有多少、与什么相比，以及还有什么可能是真的。一个能做这两件事的头脑，会更难被驱赶，在争论里也更善意，因为它既不会驳回一个人的经历，也不会让那段经历假装成为世界的完整地图。

options: It can, by itself, prove a general rule, because vivid stories are always typical
It should be thrown away, because stories never have a human cost

It can raise a question, illustrate a mechanism or remind us of a human cost, but it cannot establish how common a pattern is, what caused it, or whether it would work for someone else

senior.title: 🧱 Finding the Hidden Assumption Under an Argument
senior.content:
Every argument rests on more than the sentences it says out loud. Underneath, there are assumptions: claims that are taken as given, so that the visible reasoning can move. Some assumptions are fair and shared. Some are shaky, narrow, or invisible even to the speaker. Critical thinking is, in large part, the habit of finding those hidden beams and asking whether they will hold. “We should start classes later because teenagers need more sleep” assumes that the main cause of tiredness is the clock, that later hours are possible for transport and families, and that sleep would actually increase. Those may be true, or partly true, or true only for some students. Until they are named, the debate is fighting in the dark.

A practical way in is to ask a few standard questions. What would have to be true for this conclusion to follow? Who is included in the word “we”? What is being counted as a cost, and what is being left out? Is a rule that works in one place being treated as a law of nature? Does the speaker assume that there are only two options, or that past trends will continue, or that people will behave as the plan hopes? If any of these fails, the argument may still have value, but it needs a narrower claim or a stronger repair. The point is not to destroy every case with a trick question. The point is to make the foundation discussable.

Hidden assumptions often hide in value words and in the frame of the problem. “Efficient,” “fair,” “realistic,” and “normal” already contain a picture of what matters. A proposal to cut a programme to “save money” may assume that the programme’s benefits are small, or that the saved money will go to a better use, or that no one will pay the cost in another form. A slogan about “personal responsibility” may assume a playing field that is more level than it is. Naming the value does not end the argument. It prevents two people from thinking they disagree about facts when they disagree about what should be protected.

Students can practise with short texts: an advertisement, a school notice, a comment under a news video. Underline the conclusion, list the stated reasons, then write one sentence beginning “This takes for granted that…” Share the sentence and see whether classmates accept the assumption. If they do not, the original argument needs either evidence for that beam or a more careful wording. In their own essays, students can add a short concession: “This depends on…, which may not hold if…” That sentence is a sign of strength, not of weakness, because it shows the writer can see the edges of the case.

A mind that can surface assumptions becomes harder to manipulate and easier to work with. It will not be trapped as often by a false dilemma or by a definition that quietly does the arguing. It will also be humbler about its own views, because those views, too, stand on beams that can be questioned. Critical thinking, at this depth, is less a performance of doubt than a kind of intellectual housekeeping: know what your house rests on, and test the wood before you ask others to come inside.
senior.translation:
每一个论证，所依赖的都不只是它大声说出的那些句子。在底下，有一些假设：被当作给定的主张，好让可见的推理能够移动。“我们应该更晚开始上课，因为青少年需要更多睡眠”假设疲惫的主要原因是时钟，假设对交通和家庭来说更晚的时间是可能的，并假设睡眠实际上会增加。这些也许是真的，或部分为真，或只对一些学生为真。在它们被命名之前，辩论是在黑暗中作战。

一个实际的入口，是问几个标准问题。要使这个结论跟得上，什么必须是真的？“我们”这个词里包括了谁？什么被算作成本，什么又被留下？一条在一个地方有效的规则，是否被当成了自然法则？说话的人是否假设只有两个选项，或过去的趋势将会继续，或人们会按计划所希望的那样行动？如果其中任何一项不成立，论证也许仍然有价值，但它需要一个更窄的主张，或一次更强的修补。重点不是用一道巧问题摧毁每一个案例。重点是让地基变得可以讨论。

隐藏的假设常常藏在价值词语里，也藏在问题的框架里。“高效”“公平”“现实”和“正常”已经包含着一幅关于什么重要的图画。一个为了“省钱”而削减项目的提议，可能假设项目的益处很小，或省下的钱会走向更好的用途，或没有人会以另一种形式支付代价。一句关于“个人责任”的口号，可能假设一个比实际更平坦的场地。把价值命名出来，并不会结束论证。它防止两个人以为他们在为事实争执，而他们其实在为应当被保护的东西争执。

学生可以用短文本练习：一则广告，一份学校通知，一条新闻视频下的评论。在结论下画线，列出已说出的理由，然后写一句以“这把……视为理所当然”开头的话。分享这句话，看同学是否接受这个假设。如果他们不接受，原来的论证就需要为那根梁提供证据，或更小心的措辞。在他们自己的文章里，学生可以加上一句简短的让步：“这取决于……，如果……就可能不成立。”那句话是力量的标志，而不是软弱，因为它显示写的人能看见这个论证的边缘。

一个能够把假设浮出水面的头脑，会更难被操纵，也更容易与之共事。它不会那么经常被一个虚假的两难，或一个悄悄完成争论的定义困住。它对自己的观点也会更谦逊，因为那些观点同样站在可以被提问的梁上。在这一深度上，批判思维与其说是一场怀疑的表演，不如说是一种智识上的家政：知道你的房子靠在什么上面，并在邀请别人进来之前先测试那些木头。

senior.title: 🕳️ Dark Patterns: When a Design Is Built to Trick You
senior.content:
Not every ethical problem in technology is a dramatic leak or a biased algorithm. Some of the most ordinary harms are built into the surface of a screen: a button that looks like a choice but is hard to refuse, a subscription that is easy to start and a maze to cancel, a countdown that is not really a deadline, a pre-ticked box that shares more data than a hurried person notices. Designers and researchers call many of these tricks dark patterns. They work because human attention is limited, because we hate losing a bargain, and because we often click first and understand later. Technical ethics, in this everyday form, is about whether a product respects a user’s ability to decide, or treats that ability as an obstacle to a business plan.

The moral issue is not that companies want to be used. A clear offer, honestly priced, can still be persuasive. The issue is deception and friction placed on purpose in the path of a “no.” If the language of consent is tiny, if the colourful button always means spend, and if leaving requires a chat with a bot that “does not understand” the word cancel, the design has stopped being neutral. It has become a kind of quietly engineered pressure. Children and tired adults are especially exposed, which is why some regulators now name and forbid particular patterns, and why a few firms have been fined for making exit harder than entry.

Defenders sometimes say that users can simply read more carefully, or that competition will punish the worst designs. Both replies are only partly true. Reading every clause is a heavy demand in a life full of necessary clicks, and markets do not always reward the fairest button if the trick increases short-term sign-ups. Ethics adds a duty that goes beyond “it is legal until someone sues.” Teams can test a design not only for conversion, but for whether a reasonably hurried person can understand the choice and reverse it without humiliation. A good test is simple: would you be comfortable explaining this screen to a parent, a student, or a regulator without shrinking the font?

Students can train an eye for these patterns without becoming cynical about every app. Before joining a service, look for the exit as carefully as the entrance. Take a screenshot of a price and a tick box. Ask who benefits if you feel rushed. In class, compare two sign-up flows and mark where the design helps a decision and where it hides one. The habit is a civic skill, not only a consumer tip, because public services and school platforms can use the same tricks.

A technology that needs to trick you in order to grow is already making a confession. Ethical design is slower, sometimes less profitable in a quarter, and more respectful of the person at the other end of the glass. The smallest button can be a test of whether an industry still believes that consent should be real.
senior.translation:
并非技术里的每一个伦理问题，都是一次戏剧性的泄露或一种有偏见的算法。一些最平常的伤害，被做进屏幕的表面里：一个看起来像选择、却很难拒绝的按钮，一份容易开始、取消却像迷宫的订阅，一个其实并非截止的倒计时，一个匆忙的人注意不到、却会分享更多数据的预勾选框。设计师和研究人员把许多这类把戏叫做黑暗模式。它们之所以有效，是因为人的注意力是有限的，因为我们讨厌失去一笔便宜，也因为我们常常先点击、后理解。技术伦理在这种日常形式里，关乎一件产品是否尊重用户做决定的能力，或是把那种能力当作商业计划的障碍来对待。

道德问题并不在于公司希望被使用。一个清楚、诚实标价的提议，仍然可以是有说服力的。问题在于欺骗，以及被故意放在“不”这条路上的摩擦。如果同意的语言非常小，如果彩色按钮总是意味着花钱，如果离开需要和一个“听不懂取消这个词”的机器人聊天，设计就已经不再中立。它变成了一种被悄悄工程化的压力。儿童和疲倦的成年人尤其容易暴露其中，这就是为什么一些监管者现在点名并禁止特定模式，以及为什么有些公司因为让退出比进入更难而被罚款。

辩护者有时会说，用户可以简单地读得更仔细，或竞争会惩罚最糟糕的设计。两种回答都只是部分为真。在充满必要点击的生活里，阅读每一条款是一种沉重的要求，而如果把戏能增加短期注册，市场并不总是奖赏最公平的按钮。伦理加上了一种超越“在有人起诉之前都合法”的义务。团队不仅可以测试转化，也可以测试一个相当匆忙的人是否能够理解这个选择，并无羞辱地撤回它。一个好的测试很简单：你是否愿意向一位家长、一名学生或一位监管者解释这块屏幕，而不把字体缩小？

学生可以训练出一双看见这些模式的眼睛，而不必对每一个应用都变得犬儒。在加入一项服务之前，像看入口一样仔细地看出口。给价格和勾选框截一张图。问如果自己感觉被催促，谁从中受益。在课堂上，比较两套注册流程，并标出设计在何处帮助决定、在何处隐藏决定。这种习惯是一种公民技能，而不仅仅是消费者提示，因为公共服务和学校平台也可能使用同样的把戏。

一种需要欺骗你才能生长的技术，已经是在供认。伦理的设计更慢，在一个季度里有时更少利润，却更尊重玻璃另一端的那个人。最小的一个按钮，也可以成为一次测试：一个行业是否仍然相信，同意应当是真实的。

senior.title: 🎭 Deepfakes, Consent, and a Face That Can Be Borrowed
senior.content:
A face and a voice used to be among the strongest signs that a person was present in a recording. New tools can now borrow both with alarming ease, stitching a likeness onto words the person never said, or a body onto a scene they never entered. Some of these deepfakes are jokes, art, or clearly labelled fiction. Others are made to humiliate, to sway an election, to extract money, or to put a private person into a sexual image they did not consent to. Technical ethics here is not only about whether the software is impressive. It is about consent, harm, and a public world in which seeing may no longer be believing.

The ethical centre is the person whose likeness is used. A celebrity may have lawyers; a classmate usually does not. Non-consensual images can follow a victim through school and work, and “it was only a joke” does not restore a reputation or a sense of safety. Political deepfakes can move faster than fact-checkers, especially in a language or a region with few trusted media. Fraud can sound like a relative on the telephone. In each case the technology lowers the cost of impersonation, while the cost of being impersonated remains brutally high. A responsible ethics asks who bears that imbalance, and what duties fall on makers, platforms, and viewers.

Responses will not be a single ban on all synthetic media, because the same tools can also be used for film, accessibility, or satire that is clearly signalled. More plausible duties include: labelling generated or altered media when it could reasonably deceive; refusing to host sexual fakes of real people; giving victims a fast path to removal; and teaching the public that a clip, however sharp, is no longer self-proving. Law is beginning to catch up in some countries, unevenly. Technical watermarks help only if they survive editing and if platforms actually check them. None of this works if viewers still share first and think later.

Students can practise a slower kind of looking. Before forwarding a shocking clip of a public figure, ask whether a reliable source has confirmed it, and whether the account that posted it has a history of tricks. Never create or share a sexual or cruel fake of a real person, even as a “test.” If a friend is targeted, help them keep records and tell a trusted adult; do not circulate the file in order to “warn” others. Curiosity about the tool is understandable. Using a classmate’s face as raw material is not a neutral experiment.

A society that cannot trust a voice on a phone or a face on a screen will look for other anchors: official confirmation, personal contact, and a habit of delay. Ethics in this field is, finally, about whether we still treat a person’s likeness as part of their dignity, or as a toy that anyone with software may borrow. The answer will be written not only in labs, but in what we refuse to make and refuse to share.
senior.translation:
一张脸和一个声音，曾经是一个人出现在一段录音里的最强标志之一。新的工具现在可以以令人不安的轻易借用两者，把一个相貌缝到这个人从未说过的话上，或把一具身体缝到他们从未进入的场景上。这些深度伪造里，有一些是玩笑、艺术，或被清楚标明的虚构。另一些则被用来羞辱，影响一场选举，榨取金钱，或把一个私人放进他们并未同意的性图像里。这里的技术伦理，不仅关乎软件是否惊人。它关乎同意、伤害，以及一个看见可能不再等于相信的公共世界。

伦理的中心是那位被使用了相貌的人。一位名人也许有律师；一位同学通常没有。未经同意的图像可以跟着受害者走过学校和工作，“这只是玩笑”并不能恢复名誉或安全感。政治深度伪造可以比事实核查传得更快，尤其是在一个很少有可信媒体的语言或地区里。诈骗可以在电话里听起来像一位亲戚。在每一种情况里，技术降低了假冒的成本，而被假冒的成本仍然残酷地高。一种负责任的伦理会问，谁承担这种不平衡，以及制作者、平台和观众身上落着怎样的义务。

回应不会是对所有合成媒体的一刀切禁止，因为同样的工具也可以用于电影、无障碍，或被清楚标明的讽刺。更可行的义务包括：在生成或被改动的媒体可能合理地欺骗时给它贴上标签；拒绝托管针对真人的性伪造；给受害者一条快速删除的路径；并教导公众，一段无论多么清晰的片段，都不再是自我证明的。法律在一些国家开始追赶，却并不均匀。技术水印只有在能在编辑后存活、并且平台真正检查它们时才有帮助。如果观众仍然先分享、后思考，这些就都不会起作用。

学生可以练习一种更慢的看。在转发一段关于公众人物的令人震惊的片段之前，问一个可靠来源是否已经确认它，以及发布它的账号是否有把戏的历史。即使作为“测试”，也永远不要制作或分享针对真人的性或残忍的伪造。如果一位朋友被盯上，帮助他们保留记录并告诉一位可信的成年人；不要为了“警告”别人而传播那份文件。对工具的好奇是可以理解的。把同学的脸当作原材料，并不是一次中立的实验。

一个不能信任电话里的声音或屏幕上的脸的社会，会寻找其他锚：官方确认，亲自接触，以及一种延迟的习惯。这个领域里的伦理，最终关乎我们是否仍然把一个人的相貌当作其尊严的一部分，或当作任何有软件的人都可以借用的玩具。答案将不仅写在实验室里，也写在我们拒绝制作、拒绝分享的东西里。

senior.title: 📷 Facial Recognition in Public: Who Gets to Know Your Face?
senior.content:
A camera on a street, at a station, or at a school gate can now do more than record a scene. Linked to software, it can try to name the faces in the crowd, match them to a database, and alert someone in another room. Supporters say this helps find a missing child, catch a wanted person, or let a passenger walk through a gate without a ticket in hand. Critics hear a different story: a public space in which you can be identified without being told, stored for longer than you know, and perhaps misidentified because the system is weaker on some faces than on others. Technical ethics in this case is about power, error, and the kind of society we accept when a walk down a street becomes a search query.

The ethical problems begin with consent and notice. In a shop you may, in theory, go elsewhere; on a public pavement the choice is thinner. If signs are small or absent, if the database includes ordinary people who have committed no crime, and if the data is shared across agencies or companies, the person in the street has become a subject of investigation without a warrant in any traditional sense. Function creep is a related risk: a system built for security at a sports event is later used to watch political gatherings or to score a citizen’s “risk.” Once the cameras and the models are paid for, new uses are tempting, and they may be added quietly.

Error is not a small print issue. A false match can lead to a humiliating stop, a missed flight, or worse. Independent tests have found uneven accuracy across age, gender and skin tone in some systems, which means the burden of mistakes may fall more heavily on already vulnerable groups. Even a highly accurate system changes the atmosphere of a place: people may avoid a protest, a clinic, or a religious site if they believe their presence will be logged. Freedom is not only the right to be correctly named. It is sometimes the right not to be named at all while you go about lawful business.

Policy can set limits: bans in especially sensitive places, a requirement of a warrant for identification searches, short retention of images, audits for bias, and a real way to appeal a mistake. Some cities have already restricted police use of the tool; others have expanded it. Companies that sell the systems have duties too, including honest reporting of error rates and a refusal to sell to clients who will clearly abuse them. None of these rules is anti-safety. It is a claim that safety which cannot explain itself, and cannot be challenged, is a different kind of order.

Students can ask, of any camera they pass, what it is for, how long a face is kept, and who can query the database. They can support rules that make those answers public. A face is not only a password. It is part of a person walking through a shared world, and a technology that claims that world should have to justify itself in the open, not only in a security brochure.
senior.translation:
街上、车站或学校门口的一台摄像机，现在可以做的不只是记录一个场景。连接到软件后，它可以试图为人群里的脸命名，把它们与一个数据库匹配，并提醒另一个房间里的某人。支持者说，这有助于找到失踪的孩子，抓住被通缉的人，或让乘客不用手里拿着票就走过闸门。批评者听到的是一个不同的故事：一个你可以在未被告知的情况下被识别、被储存得比你知道的更久、并也许因为系统对某些面孔较弱而被误认的公共空间。这个情形里的技术伦理，关乎权力、错误，以及当沿街一走变成一次搜索查询时，我们所接受的那种社会。

伦理问题从同意和告知开始。在一家商店里，你理论上可以去别处；在公共人行道上，选择更薄。如果标牌很小或不存在，如果数据库包括没有犯罪的普通人，如果数据在机构或公司之间被分享，街上的人就已经在任何传统意义上没有令状的情况下，成了调查对象。功能蔓延是一个相关的风险：一套为体育赛事安全而建的系统，后来被用来观看政治集会，或给公民的“风险”打分。一旦摄像机和模型已经被付费，新的用途就会显得诱人，并且它们可能被悄悄地加上。

错误并不是小字条款的问题。一次错误匹配可以导致一次羞辱的拦查、一次误机，或更糟。独立测试发现，一些系统在年龄、性别和肤色上的准确度并不均匀，这意味着错误的负担可能更重地落在已经脆弱的群体上。即使一套高度准确的系统，也会改变一个地方的气氛：如果人们相信他们的出现会被记录，他们也许会避开一次抗议、一家诊所或一处宗教场所。自由不仅仅是被正确命名的权利。它有时是在你进行合法事务时，根本不被命名的权利。

政策可以设定限度：在特别敏感的地方禁止，识别搜索需要令状，图像的短保留期，对偏见的审计，以及一条真正可以申诉错误的路。一些城市已经限制警察使用这种工具；另一些则扩大了它。销售这些系统的公司也有义务，包括诚实报告错误率，并拒绝卖给将明显滥用它们的客户。这些规则没有一条是反安全的。它是一种主张：一种不能解释自己、也不能被挑战的安全，是另一种秩序。

学生可以对任何他们经过的摄像机问：它是做什么的，一张脸被保留多久，以及谁可以查询这个数据库。他们可以支持让那些答案公开的规则。一张脸不仅仅是一个密码。它是一个走在共享世界里的人的一部分，而一种声称拥有那个世界的技术，应当在公开中证明自己，而不仅仅在一份安全手册里。

senior.title: 🧩 Continental Drift: Why a Good Idea Waited Decades
senior.content:
In the early twentieth century, a German scientist named Alfred Wegener argued that the continents had once fitted together and had slowly drifted apart. He pointed to the jigsaw shape of the coasts, to similar fossils and rock layers on lands now separated by oceans, and to traces of a cold climate in places that are now warm. Many geologists rejected the idea, sometimes with mockery. The problem was not only conservatism. Wegener could not offer a convincing mechanism for how solid continents could plough through the ocean floor. In the history of science, a pattern is often visible here: a hypothesis may collect striking evidence and still fail, for a time, because it lacks a workable “how,” or because it threatens a picture that organises a whole field.

The later turning did not come from a single dramatic apology. From the 1950s onward, new tools changed what could be measured. Magnetic patterns in rocks on the seabed, the ages of crust spreading from mid-ocean ridges, and the record of earthquakes along trenches began to fit a new model: the surface is broken into plates that move. Continents do not sail like ships through a static floor; they ride plates that are created and destroyed. Wegener was right about motion, and incomplete about the engine. Science history is full of such partial victories. Credit is rarely a straight medal to the first person who guessed the conclusion.

The delay has lessons that are easy to misuse. It does not prove that every rejected idea is a future classic, or that experts should be ignored. Most rejected ideas are rejected because they are wrong. It does show that a field can be limited by its tools, its training, and its sense of what counts as a serious mechanism. It also shows the value of independent lines of evidence. Once magnetism, seismology and dating began to agree, resistance became harder to justify, and textbooks changed — not overnight, but with a speed that still surprises students who imagine science as a calm climb.

Students of science history can practise a fairer telling. Read a piece of Wegener’s case and a piece of his critics’ case, and list what each could see with the instruments of their day. Then add what later instruments made visible. Ask which objections were fair, and which were social — a dislike of an outsider, a fear of upheaval. The point is not to turn the story into a simple moral about genius versus a crowd. The point is to see science as a human institution that can correct itself, sometimes slowly, when new measurements arrive and when people are willing to reopen a closed question.

A map of the world that once looked fixed is now a snapshot of moving plates. That change did not happen because someone shouted louder. It happened because evidence accumulated until the old picture could no longer hold the data. The history of continental drift is, among other things, a reminder that being early is not the same as being complete, and that a discipline’s greatest strength may be its ability, eventually, to admit a more restless Earth.
senior.translation:
在二十世纪早期，一位名叫阿尔弗雷德·魏格纳的德国科学家主张，大陆曾经拼在一起，并缓慢地漂移分开。他指出海岸的拼图形状，指出现在被海洋隔开的土地上相似的化石和岩层，以及现在温暖的地方里寒冷气候的痕迹。许多地质学家拒绝了这个想法，有时还带着嘲笑。问题不仅仅是保守。魏格纳不能提供一个令人信服的机制，说明坚固的大陆如何能够犁过洋底。在科学史里，一种模式常常在这里可见：一个假说也许收集了惊人的证据，却仍然在一段时间里失败，因为它缺少一个可行的“如何”，或因为它威胁着组织整个领域的那幅图画。

后来的转变，并不是来自一次戏剧性的道歉。从二十世纪五十年代起，新的工具改变了能够被测量的东西。海底岩石里的磁性图案，从大洋中脊展开的地壳年龄，以及海沟沿线的地震记录，开始拟合一个新的模型：地表被破碎成移动的板块。大陆并不像船一样在静止的洋底上航行；它们乘坐在被生成也被销毁的板块上。魏格纳关于运动是对的，关于引擎却是不完整的。科学史充满了这样的部分胜利。功劳很少是一枚直线发给第一个猜出结论的人的奖牌。

这段延迟有一些容易被误用的教训。它并不证明每一个被拒绝的想法都是未来的经典，或专家应当被忽视。大多数被拒绝的想法被拒绝，是因为它们是错的。它确实表明，一个领域可能受限于它的工具、它的训练，以及它对什么算作严肃机制的感觉。它也表明独立证据线的价值。一旦磁性、地震学和年代测定开始一致，抵抗就变得更难辩护，课本也改变了——不是一夜之间，却以一种仍然让那些把科学想象成平静攀登的学生吃惊的速度。

科学史的学生可以练习一种更公平的讲述。读一段魏格纳的论证和一段批评者的论证，并列出每一方用他们那个时代的仪器能够看见什么。然后再加上后来的仪器使什么变得可见。问哪些反对是公平的，哪些是社会性的——对一个局外人的不喜欢，对动荡的恐惧。重点不是把故事变成天才对人群的简单道德。重点是把科学看成一个能够纠正自己的人类制度，当新的测量到来、当人们愿意重新打开一个已关闭的问题时，有时会很慢。

一幅曾经看起来固定的世界地图，现在是移动板块的一张快照。那种改变并不是因为有人喊得更响。它发生是因为证据积累到旧图画再也装不下这些数据。大陆漂移的历史，除了别的以外，也是一个提醒：早并不等于完整，而一个学科最大的力量，也许是它最终承认一个更不安分的地球的能力。

senior.title: 📏 How the World Agreed, Slowly, on What a Metre Is
senior.content:
Trade, science and tax all depend on a quiet agreement: that a unit means the same thing in different hands. For most of history it did not. A foot, a pound or a bushel could change from one market town to the next, which was convenient for some sellers and disastrous for comparison. The long effort to define shared measures is a central story in the history of science, because it is not only about rulers and scales. It is about who has the authority to fix a standard, how that standard is kept stable, and how a laboratory decision becomes a law, a textbook, and a habit in a shop.

The metric system, born in a revolutionary period in France, tried to replace local custom with units tied to nature — a fraction of the Earth’s meridian for the metre, a cube of water for the kilogram. The idea was political as well as scientific: a measure that would belong to “all people,” not to a king’s body or a guild’s privilege. In practice the first physical bars and weights had to be made, copied, and guarded, and other countries had to be persuaded or pressured to adopt them. Some resisted for national reasons; some adopted the language of metres and still used old habits in the market. Science history shows that a beautiful definition does not automatically travel.

Later decades exposed a further problem: even a carefully made metal bar changes slightly, and a standard that depends on a unique object in a vault is a fragile empire. In the twentieth and twenty-first centuries, units were increasingly tied to constants of nature and to reproducible experiments, so that a laboratory far from Paris could, in principle, realise the same metre. The redefinition of the kilogram, for example, moved it away from a unique cylinder and toward a fixed value of a fundamental constant. The change was almost invisible in daily life, and huge in the philosophy of measurement: the standard became a method, not a relic.

Behind the technical story sit arguments about fairness, empire and trust. A shared unit can protect a customer from a short measure; it can also be a tool of state power, of colonial administration, or of industrial efficiency that ignores local ways of knowing. Scientists who met in international conferences were not only calculating. They were negotiating who would host the official copies, whose instruments would count, and how disputes would be settled. A metre is a length. It is also a treaty written in metal and, later, in laser light.

Students can see this history in the tools around them: a kitchen scale, a road sign, a chemistry flask. Ask who set the mark, how it is checked, and what would break if two labs used different “metres.” The story of measurement is a reminder that science is a social achievement as well as a discovery. Agreement had to be built, maintained, and sometimes rebuilt, so that a number on a page could mean the same thing tomorrow, and on the other side of an ocean.
senior.translation:
贸易、科学和税收都依赖于一个安静的约定：一个单位在不同的手里意味着同样的东西。在历史的大部分时间里，它并不是这样。一尺、一磅或一蒲式耳，可以从一个集镇到下一个集镇发生变化，这对一些卖家是方便的，对比较却是灾难性的。定义共享度量的漫长努力，是科学史里的一个中心故事，因为它不仅仅关于尺和秤。它关于谁有权力去固定一个标准，那个标准如何保持稳定，以及一个实验室的决定如何变成法律、课本，和商店里的习惯。

在法国一个革命时期诞生的公制，试图用与自然相连的单位来替换地方习俗——米是地球子午线的一个分数，千克是一立方的水。这个想法既是政治的，也是科学的：一种属于“所有人”的度量，而不是国王的身体或行会的特权。在实践中，最初的物理尺和砝码必须被制造、复制和守卫，其他国家必须被说服或被施加压力来采用它们。有些出于国家理由而抵抗；有些采用了米的语言，却仍然在市场里使用旧习惯。科学史表明，一个美丽的定义并不会自动旅行。

后来的几十年暴露了进一步的问题：即使一根被仔细做成的金属尺也会轻微变化，而一个依赖于保险库里一件独特物体的标准，是一个脆弱的帝国。在二十和二十一世纪，单位越来越多地与自然常数和可重复的实验相连，好让一间远离巴黎的实验室原则上可以实现同一个米。例如千克的重新定义，把它从一根独特的圆柱移向一个基本常数的固定值。这种改变在日常生活里几乎看不见，在测量的哲学里却是巨大的：标准变成了一种方法，而不是一件遗物。

在技术故事后面，坐着关于公平、帝国和信任的争论。一个共享的单位可以保护顾客不受缺斤短两之害；它也可以是国家权力、殖民行政，或忽略地方认知方式的工业效率的工具。在国际会议上会面的科学家，不仅仅在计算。他们在协商谁将保管官方复制件，谁的仪器将被算数，以及争端将如何被解决。一米是一个长度。它也是一份用金属、后来又用激光写成的条约。

学生可以在身边的工具里看见这段历史：厨房的秤，路牌，化学烧瓶。问是谁设定了这个标记，它如何被检查，以及如果两间实验室使用不同的“米”，什么会破裂。测量的故事是一个提醒：科学既是一种发现，也是一种社会成就。约定必须被建造、被维持，有时还被重建，好让纸上的一个数字在明天、以及在大洋的另一侧，能够意味着同样的东西。

questions.q: 1. Why is the effort to define shared measures a central story in the history of science?
options: It is only about rulers and scales, with no questions of authority
It is about who may fix a standard, how it is kept stable, and how a laboratory decision becomes law, a textbook and a habit in a shop
A foot or a bushel always meant the same thing from town to town
Trade, science and tax do not depend on agreed units
questions.exp: 文中说共享度量不仅关乎尺秤，也关乎谁有权固定标准、如何保持稳定，以及实验室决定如何变成法律与习惯。

questions.q: 2. What was political as well as scientific about the early metric system?
options: It tried to tie units to nature and to belong to ‘all people,’ not to a king’s body or a guild’s privilege, yet bars had to be copied and countries persuaded
A beautiful definition automatically travelled to every market
No country ever resisted for national reasons
Physical bars and weights never needed to be guarded
questions.exp: 文中指出公制既要把单位连于自然，也要属于所有人而非国王或行会，但实物标准仍须被复制，国家须被说服。

questions.q: 3. Why were units later tied to constants of nature rather than a unique object in a vault?
options: The kilogram’s redefinition was huge in daily shopping and invisible in the philosophy of measurement
A unique cylinder is a more reliable empire than a reproducible experiment
Laboratories far from Paris can never realise the same metre
Even a metal bar changes slightly, and a standard that depends on one object is fragile; a method based on constants can, in principle, be realised far from Paris
questions.exp: 文中说明金属尺会微变，依赖库中唯一物体的标准脆弱，于是单位被改绑在自然常数和可重复实验上。

questions.q: 4. What arguments sit behind the technical story of a metre?
options: Scientists at conferences were only calculating, never negotiating
A shared unit can never become a tool of administration
Fairness for customers, but also state power, colonial administration and negotiations about official copies, instruments and disputes — a treaty written in metal and later in laser light
A metre is only a length, never a political agreement
questions.exp: 文中指出共享单位既可保护顾客，也可成为权力工具，会议上的科学家也在协商官方复制件与争端解决。

questions.q: 5. What should students ask of a kitchen scale or a road sign?
options: Whether a number on a page can mean something different tomorrow, on purpose
Who set the mark, how it is checked, and what would break if two labs used different ‘metres,’ because agreement had to be built and maintained
Whether science is only discovery, never a social achievement
Whether an ocean’s distance makes agreement unnecessary
questions.exp: 文中建议询问谁设定标记、如何检查，以及若两间实验室使用不同的“米”会怎样，因为约定必须被建造和维持。

senior.title: 🦠 Germ Theory: When Disease Became Something You Could Catch
senior.content:
For a long time, many doctors explained epidemics with bad air, imbalance in the body, or a punishment that had no microscopic cause. People still washed, still isolated the sick at times, and still noticed that illness could run through a house; but the ruling picture was not that of a living germ passing from one body to another. The rise of germ theory in the nineteenth century is one of the great rearrangements in the history of science. It changed what counted as an explanation, what a laboratory was for, and, eventually, what a city should do with its water, its hands, and its wounds.

The change was not a single moment of light. Earlier observers had seen tiny creatures under lenses, and some doctors had argued, against resistance, that childbed fever or cholera could be reduced by hygiene. What slowly assembled was a method: isolate a microorganism, associate it with a disease, and, where possible, show that introducing it can produce the illness and that controlling it can reduce it. Names such as Pasteur and Koch stand in textbooks because they helped turn a debate into a programme of experiments, vaccines and industrial processes such as the heating of milk. They did not work alone, and they were not instantly believed. Instruments, staining methods, and the authority of institutions all mattered, as did the visible success of antiseptic surgery and, later, of public sanitation.

Opposition had more than one source. The new picture threatened older medical identities and was, at first, hard to see: most germs are invisible to the unaided eye, and correlation in a crowded, filthy city could be read in several ways. Some hygienists already believed in cleanliness without accepting a specific microbe. Some communities resisted official rules about quarantine or water, for reasons of livelihood or distrust. Science history that remembers only the heroes can forget this friction, and can also forget how often early germ theory was mixed with harsh social judgments about the poor. A better telling keeps both the triumph of a method and the politics of its use.

The consequences reached far beyond the clinic. Sewer systems, food inspection, vaccination campaigns, and the ritual of handwashing in hospitals all rest, in part, on the idea that an invisible living cause can be interrupted. Later discoveries — viruses, antibiotics, the limits of those antibiotics — have complicated the picture without erasing it. Students can read a mid-century objection to germ theory and list what evidence later answered it, and what questions, such as the role of the host’s condition, still matter.

To study this chapter is to see science as a change in the furniture of the world: once “a germ” became a usable object, new tools, laws and habits could be built around it. The history is not only that we learned we could catch a disease. It is that we learned, imperfectly and with delay, that we could sometimes stop one from being caught.
senior.translation:
很长一段时间里，许多医生用污浊的空气、身体里的失衡，或一种没有微观原因的惩罚来解释流行病。人们仍然会清洗，有时仍然会隔离病人，也仍然注意到疾病可以穿过一户人家；但占统治地位的图画，并不是一种活的微生物从一个身体传到另一个身体。十九世纪微生物理论的兴起，是科学史里一次重大的重新安排。它改变了什么算作解释，实验室是做什么的，以及最终一座城市应当怎样对待它的水、它的手和它的伤口。

这一变化并不是单单一刻的光。更早的观察者已经在透镜下看见过微小的生物，一些医生也曾在抵抗之中主张，产褥热或霍乱可以通过卫生来减少。慢慢组装起来的，是一种方法：分离一种微生物，把它与一种疾病联系起来，并在可能的情况下表明，引入它可以产生这种病，而控制它可以减少这种病。巴斯德和科赫这样的名字出现在课本里，是因为他们帮助把一场辩论变成一套实验、疫苗，以及如加热牛奶这样的工业流程的纲领。他们并非独自工作，也并非立刻被相信。仪器、染色方法，以及机构的权威都重要，抗菌手术以及后来公共卫生的可见成功也是如此。

反对有不止一个来源。这幅新图画威胁着更古老的医学身份，而且起初很难看见：大多数微生物对肉眼是不可见的，而在一座拥挤、肮脏的城市里，相关关系可以用几种方式来读。一些卫生学家已经相信清洁，却并不接受一种特定的微生物。一些社区抵制关于隔离或水的官方规则，出于生计或不信任的理由。只记住英雄的科学史，会忘记这种摩擦，也会忘记早期微生物理论多么经常与关于穷人的苛刻社会判断混合在一起。一种更好的讲述，既保留一种方法的胜利，也保留其使用中的政治。

后果远远超出诊所。下水道系统、食品检查、疫苗运动，以及医院里洗手的仪式，都部分建立在这样一个想法上：一种看不见的活的原因可以被打断。后来的发现——病毒、抗生素，以及那些抗生素的限度——使这幅图画更复杂，却没有擦除它。学生可以读一段世纪中叶对微生物理论的反对，并列出后来什么证据回答了它，以及哪些问题，例如宿主状况的作用，仍然重要。

研究这一章，就是把科学看成世界家具的一次改变：一旦“一种微生物”成为一个可用的对象，新的工具、法律和习惯就可以围绕它被建造。这段历史不仅仅是我们学会了我们可能染上一种病。它是我们不完美地、带着延迟地学会了，我们有时可以阻止一种病被染上。

questions.q: 1. What ruling picture of disease did germ theory eventually rearrange?
options: A picture in which people never washed or isolated the sick
A world that already treated a laboratory as the centre of every explanation
Explanations based on bad air, imbalance or punishment, rather than a living germ passing from one body to another
A city that already knew exactly what to do with water, hands and wounds
questions.exp: 文中说此前主导解释是污浊空气、失衡或惩罚，而不是活的微生物在身体间传递。

questions.q: 2. What method slowly assembled around germ theory?
options: A single moment of light, with no earlier observers or hygiene arguments
Isolate a microorganism, associate it with a disease, and where possible show that introducing it can produce the illness and controlling it can reduce it
A programme that Pasteur and Koch carried out entirely alone and were instantly believed
A rejection of staining methods, institutions, and antiseptic surgery
questions.exp: 文中把方法概括为分离微生物、将其与疾病关联，并在可能时显示引入可致病、控制可减少。

questions.q: 3. Why did opposition have more than one source?
options: The picture threatened older medical identities, germs were hard to see, correlations could be read in several ways, and some communities resisted official rules for livelihood or distrust
Hygienists who already believed in cleanliness automatically accepted a specific microbe
Science history should remember only heroes and forget harsh social judgments
Early germ theory was never mixed with politics or judgments about the poor
questions.exp: 文中列举对旧身份的威胁、微生物难见、相关关系可有多种读法，以及出于生计或不信任的抵制。

questions.q: 4. Which later practices rest in part on interrupting an invisible living cause?
options: A complete erasure of germ theory by later discoveries
A clinic-only story, with no consequences for cities
A world in which the host’s condition no longer matters
Sewer systems, food inspection, vaccination campaigns, and handwashing in hospitals, later complicated by viruses and the limits of antibiotics
questions.exp: 文中指出下水道、食品检查、疫苗和医院洗手都部分建立在可打断看不见的活的原因这一想法上。

questions.q: 5. What does it mean to see this chapter as a change in the furniture of the world?
options: Science never changes what objects a society can build tools around
The only lesson is that we learned we could catch a disease, never that we could sometimes stop one
Once ‘a germ’ became a usable object, new tools, laws and habits could be built around it, including the imperfect, delayed lesson that a disease can sometimes be stopped from being caught
Furniture, in this metaphor, is unrelated to laws and habits
questions.exp: 文中说一旦“微生物”成为可用对象，新工具、法律和习惯便可围绕它建造，我们也延迟地学会有时可以阻止传染。

senior.title: ⌚ What a Wrist Tracker Measures — and What It Misses
senior.content:
A watch or a ring that counts steps, estimates sleep, and graphs a heartbeat has become an ordinary object in daily life. For many people it is motivating: a closed ring, a reminder to stand, a slightly better night after a walk. Technology of this kind can make hidden patterns visible, and it can support a conversation with a doctor when something is clearly unusual. It can also quietly change the way a person inhabits their own body. Hours become scores. Rest becomes a number to improve. A walk taken for a friend may be judged, on a screen, as “not enough.” The ethical and practical question in technology and everyday life is not whether the device can measure. It is what we decide a measurement is for, and what we forget when we treat the graph as the whole of health.

The numbers are estimates, not courtroom facts. Algorithms infer sleep stages from motion and pulse; they guess strain from incomplete signals; they may misread a restless night or a watch worn loose. Different brands disagree. A medical-grade test, when it is needed, is still a different tool. Trouble begins when a worried user treats a low score as a diagnosis, or when a high score is used to ignore pain, mood, or a life that cannot be captured in a step count. Some people become more anxious, checking the app in the night, which then disturbs the sleep the app is supposed to protect. Others feel guilty on a rest day that their doctor actually recommended.

There are social effects too. Insurers, employers and schools have sometimes been tempted to reward or demand this kind of data. A step challenge can be playful in a club and coercive at work. Data stored on a company’s server raise questions of privacy and of who profits from a year’s pulse. Even without those actors, family members can start to police one another’s rings. Technology that enters the home as a coach can start to feel like a supervisor.

A healthier use is bounded and curious. Wear the device if it helps you notice a useful pattern — afternoon slumps, a bedtime that keeps drifting, a week with almost no walking — and then look up from the screen. Combine the number with how you feel, what you eat, whom you see, and what a professional says when something is wrong. Take planned days off the wrist. Remember that a good life includes uncounted hours: a conversation, a meal, a sleep that was not perfect and was still enough.

Students can treat a tracker as a short experiment, not as a new identity. Write, for one week, both the numbers and a sentence about the day that the numbers cannot see. If the device makes you more fearful than informed, it is the wrong tool for now. Science and life meet most usefully when a measurement is a servant. When it becomes the master of a night’s rest or a friend’s walk, the technology has asked for more authority than a wrist should have.
senior.translation:
一块数步、估计睡眠、并把心跳画成图的手表或戒指，已经成为日常生活里一件平常的物品。对许多人来说它是有激励作用的：一个合上的圆环，一个站起来的提醒，一次散步之后略好的夜晚。这类技术可以使隐藏的模式变得可见，并在某些明显异常的时候支持与医生的谈话。它也可以悄悄改变一个人居住在自己身体里的方式。小时变成分数。休息变成一个要去改进的数字。一次为朋友而走的路，也许会在屏幕上被判定为“不够。”科技与日常生活里的伦理和实际问题，并不在于设备是否能够测量。而在于我们决定一种测量是为了什么，以及当我们把这张图当作健康的全部时，我们忘记了什么。

这些数字是估计，不是法庭上的事实。算法从运动和脉搏推断睡眠阶段；它们从不完整的信号猜测负荷；它们可能误读一个不安的夜晚，或一块戴得松的表。不同品牌会不同意。在需要的时候，一次医疗级的测试仍然是另一种工具。麻烦开始于一个担忧的用户把一个低分当作诊断，或一个高分被用来忽略疼痛、情绪，或一种无法被步数捕捉的生活。有些人变得更焦虑，在夜里查看应用，而这又打扰了应用本应保护的睡眠。另一些人在医生实际建议的休息日里感到内疚。

也有社会的影响。保险公司、雇主和学校有时会受到诱惑，去奖励或要求这类数据。一场步数挑战在社团里可以是好玩的，在工作里却可以是强制的。储存在公司服务器上的数据，提出了隐私以及谁从一年的脉搏中获利的问题。即使没有这些行动者，家庭成员也可能开始彼此监督圆环。作为教练进入家里的技术，可能开始感觉像一位监督者。

一种更健康的使用是有界限的、好奇的。如果设备帮助你注意到一种有用的模式——下午的低落，不断后移的睡觉时间，几乎没有步行的一周——就戴着它，然后再从屏幕上抬起头来。把数字与你的感觉、你吃什么、你见谁，以及当有问题时专业人员说什么结合起来。计划一些从手腕上取下来的日子。记住，一种好的生活包括未被计数的小时：一次交谈，一顿饭，一场并不完美、却仍然足够的睡眠。

学生可以把追踪器当作一次短的实验，而不是一种新的身份。用一周写下数字，以及一句数字看不见的、关于这一天的话。如果设备使你更恐惧而不是更知情，它就暂时是错误的工具。当一种测量是仆人时，科学与生活最有用地相遇。当它成为一夜休息或一次朋友散步的主人时，这项技术就已经要求了比一只手腕所应拥有的更多权威。

options: Whether a closed ring can never motivate a walk
Whether a tracker should replace a conversation with a doctor when something is unusual
Whether hours should always become scores, and a friend’s walk judged as ‘not enough’
Not whether the device can measure, but what we decide a measurement is for, and what we forget when the graph is treated as the whole of health

questions.q: 2. Why are the numbers estimates rather than courtroom facts?
options: A low score is already a diagnosis, and a high score means pain can be ignored
A watch worn loose is always read perfectly
Algorithms infer sleep and strain from incomplete signals, brands disagree, and a medical-grade test is still a different tool when needed
Checking the app at night never disturbs the sleep it is supposed to protect
questions.exp: 文中说明算法从不完整信号推断，品牌会不一致，需要时仍应用医疗级测试。

questions.q: 3. What social risks appear once this data leaves a playful club?
options: A step challenge is never playful, even in a club
Insurers, employers or schools may demand it, a challenge can become coercive, servers raise privacy questions, and family members may start to police one another’s rings
Data on a company’s server never raise questions of who profits
Technology that enters the home as a coach can never feel like a supervisor
questions.exp: 文中指出保险、雇主、学校可能要求数据，挑战可能变成强制，以及家人可能互相监督。

questions.q: 4. What does a bounded, curious use look like?
options: Notice a useful pattern, then look up from the screen; combine the number with feeling, food, friendship and professional advice, and take planned days off the wrist
Treat uncounted hours such as a meal or a conversation as failures
Wear the device as a new identity, with no days off

questions.exp: 文中建议用数字发现有用模式后抬起头，结合感觉与专业意见，并计划取下手腕上的设备。

questions.q: 5. How should students treat a tracker in a one-week experiment?
options: Let the measurement become the master of rest and of a friend’s walk
Refuse any experiment, because science and life can never meet in a servant measurement
Give a wrist more authority than a graph should have
Write both the numbers and a sentence about the day the numbers cannot see, and stop if the device makes you more fearful than informed
