senior.title: 🌾 Community Composting: Turning Food Scraps into Local Soil
senior.content:
In many kitchens, vegetable peels, coffee grounds and leftovers that never became a meal go straight into a bag that will be collected with the rest of the rubbish. In a landfill, that organic matter can decay with little air and release methane, a potent greenhouse gas. Community composting is a practical answer that does not wait for a perfect national system: neighbours, a school, a market or a housing block collect food scraps, mix them with dry leaves or shredded paper, and let microbes, insects and time turn the pile into dark soil. That soil can then feed a garden, a row of street trees, or a farm at the edge of town. The loop is short, visible, and educational. People see that “waste” was always material in the wrong place.

The action looks simple and still needs care. A good pile needs a balance of wet, nitrogen-rich scraps and dry, carbon-rich matter, enough air, and a size that can hold heat. Meat, oily food and diseased plants are often kept out of small community piles, not because nature cannot digest them, but because pests and smells can end a project faster than a lecture can save it. Volunteers turn the heap, watch the temperature, and explain the rules without shaming a neighbour who arrived with the wrong bag. Sites need a stable corner, a water source, and a plan for the finished compost, so that the pile does not become a monument to good intentions. When a market or a canteen joins, the volume jumps, and the system must grow with it — more bins, a schedule, perhaps a small paid coordinator.

The environmental numbers can be modest at the scale of one courtyard and still worth doing. Less organic waste in the general bin means fewer truck journeys for material that did not need to travel far, and the compost reduces the need for bought fertiliser in the places that receive it. The social numbers matter too. A shared pile is a reason to talk, a classroom without walls, and a sign that climate action can be local and bodily, not only a petition. Children who see peels become soil are less likely to treat the earth as a distant abstraction.

Barriers are familiar: landlords who forbid outdoor bins, summers that invite flies, winters that slow the process, and the fear of doing it “wrong.” Cities can help with a legal nod, a drop-off point, and training, without taking the project away from the people who run it. Students can start with a classroom caddy and a partnership with a garden, and can keep a simple log of kilograms diverted. The goal is a habit that survives after the first enthusiasm.

Community composting will not, by itself, repair a climate. It is one form of environmental action that turns a daily leftover into care for soil, and that gives a neighbourhood a job it can do with its hands. When the dark earth goes back under a tree, the story of the peel is complete, and the next week’s scraps have a place to go.
senior.translation:
在许多厨房里，蔬菜皮、咖啡渣和从未成为一餐的剩菜，会直接进入一只将与其余垃圾一起被收走的袋子。在填埋场里，那些有机物可能在很少空气的情况下腐烂，并释放甲烷，一种强有力的温室气体。社区堆肥是一种不等待完美国家系统的实际回答：邻居、一所学校、一个市场或一栋住宅楼收集食物残渣，把它们与干树叶或切碎的纸混合，让微生物、昆虫和时间把这堆东西变成深色的土壤。那土壤然后可以喂养一座园子、一排行道树，或城边的一个农场。这个环是短的、可见的，并且是教育性的。人们看到，“废物”一直是放错地方的材料。

这种行动看起来简单，仍然需要照料。一堆好的堆肥需要潮湿、富含氮的残渣与干燥、富含碳的物质之间的平衡，足够的空气，以及一个能够保持热量的体量。肉类、油腻的食物和带病的植物，常常被留在小型社区堆之外，不是因为自然不能消化它们，而是因为害虫和气味结束一个项目的速度，可能比一场讲座挽救它更快。志愿者翻动堆，看着温度，并解释规则，而不羞辱一个带着错误袋子到来的邻居。场地需要一个稳定的角落、一个水源，以及一个关于成品堆肥的计划，好让这堆东西不变成对良好意图的纪念碑。当一个市场或食堂加入时，量会跳升，系统必须随之生长——更多箱子，一个时间表，也许一位小规模的受薪协调人。

在一个院子的尺度上，环境数字可以是谦逊的，却仍然值得做。普通垃圾箱里更少的有机废物，意味着那些本不必走远的材料更少的卡车行程，而堆肥减少了接收它的地方对买来的肥料的需要。社会数字也很重要。一个共享的堆是一个交谈的理由，一间没有墙壁的教室，以及一个信号：气候行动可以是本地的、身体的，而不仅仅是一份请愿。看见果皮变成土壤的孩子，不太可能把地球当作一种遥远的抽象。

障碍是熟悉的：禁止户外箱子的房东，招来苍蝇的夏天，减慢过程的冬天，以及把事情做“错”的恐惧。城市可以以法律上的点头、一个投放点和培训来帮助，而不把项目从运作它的人们那里拿走。学生可以从一只教室小桶和与一座园子的合作开始，并可以保留一份关于被转移的千克数的简单日志。目标是一种在第一次热情之后仍能存活的习惯。

社区堆肥不会独自修复一个气候。它是一种环境行动，把每日的剩余变成对土壤的照料，并给一个街区一份可以用手来做的工作。当深色的土回到一棵树下时，果皮的故事就完成了，而下周的残渣也有了去处。

senior.title: 🌊 Floodplains, Housing and Who Is Left on Risky Land
senior.content:
Rivers and coasts have always flooded. What has changed is how many people live on the low ground, and who those people are. In a growing city, a floodplain can look like empty land that is cheap to build on, until a wet year arrives and the ground remembers it is a river’s room. Climate change is making some of those years more extreme, but the social pattern is older: safer, higher, or better-defended ground is usually more expensive, so households with less money, less information, or less political voice are more likely to live where the water will come. After a flood, the same inequality appears in who can leave, who can wait for insurance, and who returns to a damp room because there is nowhere else to go.

The problem is not only “natural.” Filling a wetland, narrowing a channel, or paving a hillside can send water toward streets that used to stay dry. New towers on stilts can be marketed as resilient, while older housing a few blocks away has no such protection and no say in the plan. Informal settlements often grow on leftover land precisely because it was left — a slope, a river edge, a reclaimed marsh — and then the occupants are blamed for “choosing” risk. A fairer account would ask who was priced out of safer districts, and whose development upstream changed the flow.

Responses that only tell people to move can be cruel if they ignore work, schools, and the cost of a new rent. Responses that only build a wall can protect one district and push water into another, or can create a false sense of safety that invites still more building. Better practice mixes several tools: honest maps that are public and updated, rules that stop new housing in the most dangerous bands, funding to raise or retrofit homes that will stay, and planned relocation that is negotiated, not dumped on a community in a week. Early warning and a place to go for a night matter as much as concrete. So does the slow work of restoring a floodplain’s room, even when that room is now valuable real estate.

Students can compare two neighbourhoods after the same storm: depth of water, time without power, speed of official help, and whether tenants had a voice. They can also look at a proposed riverside project and ask who benefits from the view, and who will receive the overflow. The environment here is not a backdrop. It is a set of physical facts that a housing market and a planning office can either respect or deny.

A society that treats flood risk as a private misfortune will keep discovering, after each disaster, that the same groups were in the path. A society that treats the river as a public neighbour, and housing as a shared responsibility, still cannot command the rain. It can, however, stop pretending that the map of risk is only a map of weather.
senior.translation:
河流和海岸一直都会泛滥。已经改变的是，有多少人住在低地上，以及那些人是谁。在一座增长的城市里，一片洪泛区可能看起来像一块便宜的空地，直到一个潮湿的年份到来，土地记起它是河流的房间。气候变化正使其中一些年份更加极端，但社会模式更老：更安全、更高、或被更好地防护的土地通常更贵，所以钱更少、信息更少、或政治声音更弱的家庭，更可能住在水将会到来的地方。洪水之后，同一种不平等出现在谁能够离开，谁能够等待保险，以及谁因为无处可去而回到一间潮湿的房间。

这个问题不仅仅是“自然的”。填平一块湿地，收窄一条河道，或铺砌一座山坡，可以把水送向曾经保持干燥的街道。新建的架空塔楼可以被营销为有韧性，而几个街区之外的旧住房没有这样的保护，在计划里也没有发言权。非正式居住区常常正好生长在被剩下的土地上——一个斜坡，一条河边，一块被填出的沼泽——然后居住者被责备为“选择了”风险。一种更公平的叙述会问，谁被更安全的区域的价格赶了出来，以及谁在上游的开发改变了水流。

只告诉人们搬走的回应，如果忽视工作、学校和新租金的成本，可能是残忍的。只建一堵墙的回应，可以保护一个区域并把水推到另一个区域，或造成一种虚假的安全感，从而招来更多的建造。更好的做法混合几种工具：公开且更新的诚实地图，阻止在最危险地带新建住房的规则，用于抬高或改造将留下的房屋的资金，以及经过协商、而不是在一周内抛给一个社区的有计划搬迁。预警和一个可以过夜的地方，与混凝土同样重要。恢复洪泛区的空间这份缓慢的工作也是如此，即使那空间现在已是值钱的地产。

学生可以在同一场风暴之后比较两个街区：水的深度，没有电的时间，官方帮助的速度，以及租户是否有声音。他们也可以看一个拟议的河边项目，问谁从景观中受益，谁将接收溢流。这里的环境不是一幅背景。它是一套物理事实，一个住房市场和一个规划办公室可以尊重，也可以否认。

一个把洪水风险当作私人不幸的社会，会在每一次灾难之后继续发现，同一群人在路径上。一个把河流当作公共邻居、把住房当作共享责任的社会，仍然不能命令雨水。它却可以停止假装，风险的地图只是一张天气的地图。

senior.title: 🧹 Invisible Hands: Informal Waste Workers and the City’s Recycling
senior.content:
Before a city boasts about its recycling rate, it is worth asking who actually sorts the material. In many places, informal waste workers — often called waste pickers, recyclers, or recuperators — walk routes, open bags, and pull out plastic, paper, metal and glass that can be sold. They do, for little pay and little safety, a large part of the work that keeps useful matter out of dumps. Their labour is environmental and social at once: it reduces the volume that landfills and oceans must receive, and it is also a livelihood for people who were not offered a formal job. A fair conversation about the city’s environment cannot treat these workers as a background inconvenience.

The conditions are often harsh. Traffic, cuts, fumes, and the stigma of handling other people’s discards are daily risks. Middle buyers may pay little, and a sudden change in the global price of plastic can empty a week’s effort. When a city “modernises” collection with a single contracted company, or locks waste into bins that only a truck can open, the official cleanliness can hide a social cost: families lose access to the material they used to live on, and the company may still send mixed loads to a distant site. Inclusion is possible. Some cities have recognised cooperatives of waste workers, given them identity cards, gloves, a place to sort, and a contract to collect from buildings or markets. The streets become cleaner, and the people who already knew the streams of material are not pushed aside by a slogan about green progress.

There are tensions that should not be romanticised. Child labour in waste is not a charming picture of recycling; it is a failure of schools and of household income, and it should be ended while adult work is made safer. Health services, tetanus protection, and a living payment for sorted material are not extras. Residents can help in small, concrete ways: rinse and separate, leave recyclables where agreed, and refuse to treat a person at a bin as someone without a name. Students can map who captures value in the chain — the picker, the middle buyer, the factory — and ask whether a public policy could shorten the chain or raise the first price.

The wider lesson is about how a society and its environment are tied. A city that wants less waste in the river cannot look only at household virtue or at a new machine. It must look at the people who already stand in the flow of discarded things, and decide whether they will be partners or casualties of the next environmental plan. Making their work safer and more visible does not solve every pollution problem. It does tell the truth about who has been doing part of the city’s ecological job, unpaid by official praise, for a long time.
senior.translation:
在一座城市夸耀它的回收率之前，值得问一问实际上是谁在分拣这些材料。在许多地方，非正式的废物工作者——常常被称为拾荒者、回收者，或回收工——走路线，打开袋子，抽出可以出售的塑料、纸、金属和玻璃。他们以很少的报酬和很少的安全，做了很大一部分使有用物质远离垃圾场的工作。他们的劳动同时是环境的和社会的：它减少了填埋场和海洋必须接收的体积，它也是那些未被提供正式工作的人的生计。一场关于城市环境的公平谈话，不能把这些工作者当作一种背景上的不便。

条件常常是严酷的。交通、割伤、烟气，以及处理别人弃物的污名，是日常的风险。中间买家可能给得很少，塑料全球价格的一次突然变化，可以掏空一周的努力。当一座城市用一家单一的承包公司来“现代化”收集，或把废物锁进只有卡车才能打开的箱子时，官方的清洁可能隐藏一种社会成本：家庭失去对他们曾经赖以为生的材料的通路，而公司仍可能把混合的荷载送到一个遥远的地点。包容是可能的。一些城市已经承认废物工作者的合作社，给他们身份卡、手套、一个分拣的地方，以及一份从建筑或市场收集的合同。街道变得更干净，而那些已经了解材料流的人，没有被一句关于绿色进步的口号推到一边。

有些张力不应当被浪漫化。废物中的童工并不是一幅关于回收的迷人图画；它是学校和家庭收入的失败，应当在使成人工作更安全的同时被结束。健康服务、破伤风防护，以及对分拣材料的一份可生活的付款，不是额外的东西。居民可以用小小的、具体的方式帮忙：冲洗并分开，把可回收物留在约定的地方，并拒绝把一个在箱子旁的人当作没有名字的人。学生可以绘制链条中谁捕获价值——拾拣者，中间买家，工厂——并问一项公共政策是否可以缩短链条或提高第一价格。

更宽的教训，是关于一个社会与它的环境如何被绑在一起。一座希望河里废物更少的城市，不能只看家庭美德或一台新机器。它必须看那些已经站在被丢弃之物的流动中的人，并决定他们将成为下一个环境计划的伙伴，还是伤亡者。使他们的工作更安全、更可见，并不能解决每一个污染问题。它确实说出了真相：谁在很长一段时间里，未经官方赞美的付款，一直在做这座城市生态工作的一部分。

options: They are only a background inconvenience with no effect on landfills or oceans
Official praise has always paid them well

They often do, for little pay and little safety, a large part of the work that keeps useful matter out of dumps, and their labour is both environmental and a livelihood

options: Household virtue or a new machine is the only thing a city should look at

senior.title: 🪐 Hunting for Planets Around Other Stars
senior.content:
For most of human history, the only planets we could name were the ones that share our Sun. The question of whether other stars had worlds was a matter of philosophy, not of measurement. That has changed with startling speed. Astronomers now confirm thousands of exoplanets — planets that orbit stars other than the Sun — and the count continues to rise. The methods are indirect and ingenious, because a planet is usually a faint point drowned in a star’s glare. One widely used approach, the transit method, watches a star’s brightness dip by a tiny fraction when a planet crosses in front of it. Another, the radial-velocity method, detects a slight wobble in the star’s motion as a planet’s gravity tugs it. In special cases, a planet’s light can be separated, or a gravitational lens in space can magnify a distant system. Each method has limits of size, distance and angle, so the catalogue we have is not a random sample of all worlds. It is a sample of the worlds our instruments can currently catch.

Even so, the catch has already revised the imagination of science. Planets come in sizes and orbits that our own system did not prepare us to expect: worlds larger than Earth but smaller than Neptune, planets that race around their stars in days, systems packed more tightly than ours. A few sit in a “habitable zone,” where, in principle, liquid water could exist on a surface. That phrase is a starting condition, not a discovery of oceans or life. A planet can be in the right range of light and still have the wrong atmosphere, the wrong history, or no surface at all. The next stage of exploration is to read atmospheres, where possible, by watching starlight filter through a planet’s gases, and to look for patterns of molecules that are hard to explain without biology — while remembering that geology and chemistry can also surprise us.

The work is slow, expensive, and shared across countries and telescopes, including space observatories designed for this hunt. It requires patience with uncertainty: a candidate may be withdrawn after better data, and a headline about “Earth 2.0” is almost always too early. Students can follow one confirmed system and list what is actually known — mass or radius, period, distance — and what is still a guess. They can also ask how a biased sample should shape our claims: if we are better at finding large, close planets, we should not conclude that small, far ones are rare.

Scientific exploration at this scale is not a tour. It is a disciplined attempt to turn a neighbourless night sky into a map of other neighbourhoods, using shadows, wobbles and spectra as our only hands. Whether or not life is eventually found, the hunt has already taught a humbling fact: our solar system is one arrangement among many, and the universe is richer in worlds than a single set of textbooks once allowed us to picture.
senior.translation:
在人类历史的大部分时间里，我们能够叫出名字的行星，只有那些与我们共享太阳的。其他恒星是否拥有世界，是一个哲学问题，而不是测量问题。这一点已经以令人吃惊的速度改变了。天文学家现在确认了数千颗系外行星——围绕太阳以外的恒星运行的行星——而且这个计数还在上升。方法是间接而巧妙的，因为一颗行星通常是一个淹没在恒星眩光中的微弱点。一种被广泛使用的方法，凌日法，观察当一颗行星从恒星前方经过时，恒星亮度发生的微小下降。另一种，径向速度法，探测当行星的引力拉拽恒星时，恒星运动中的轻微摇摆。在特殊情况下，一颗行星的光可以被分开，或太空中的一个引力透镜可以放大一个遥远的系统。每一种方法都有大小、距离和角度上的限度，所以我们拥有的目录并不是所有世界的一个随机样本。它是我们的仪器目前能够抓住的世界的一个样本。

即使如此，这些收获已经修正了科学的想象。行星以我们自己的系统并未让我们准备好去期待的大小和轨道出现：比地球大却比海王星小的世界，在数天内就绕其恒星跑一圈的行星，比我们的系统包装得更紧的系统。少数坐落在“宜居带”中，在那里，原则上，液态水可以存在于表面上。那个短语是一个起始条件，而不是对海洋或生命的发现。一颗行星可以处在正确的光的范围内，却仍然有错误的大气、错误的历史，或根本没有表面。探索的下一阶段，是在可能的情况下，通过观察星光穿过一颗行星的气体来阅读大气，并寻找没有生物学就很难解释的分子模式——同时记住，地质和化学也可以让我们吃惊。

这项工作是缓慢的、昂贵的，并且在国家和望远镜之间共享，包括为这次搜寻而设计的太空观测站。它需要对不确定性保持耐心：一个候选者可能在更好的数据之后被撤回，而关于“地球2.0”的标题几乎总是来得太早。学生可以跟踪一个已确认的系统，并列出实际已知的东西——质量或半径，周期，距离——以及仍然是猜测的东西。他们也可以问，一个有偏差的样本应当如何塑造我们的主张：如果我们更善于发现大而近的行星，我们就不应当断定小而远的行星是稀少的。

这种尺度上的科学探索不是一次旅游。它是一次有纪律的尝试，用影子、摇摆和光谱作为我们唯一的手，把一片没有邻居的夜空变成一张其他邻里的地图。无论最终是否找到生命，这次搜寻已经教会一个令人谦卑的事实：我们的太阳系是许多安排中的一种，而宇宙在世界方面，比曾经允许我们去想象的单一套教科书更丰富。

options: A planet is usually a faint point drowned in a star’s glare, so astronomers watch tiny dips in brightness, slight stellar wobbles, or, in special cases, separated light or a gravitational lens
Every planet can be photographed easily as a bright disc beside its star
The only available method is philosophy, not measurement
The catalogue is already a random sample of all worlds, so indirect methods are unnecessary

questions.q: 2. Why is the current catalogue not a random sample of all worlds?
options: Instruments catch every size and orbit equally
All confirmed planets share the same size and year as Earth
The count has stopped rising
Each method has limits of size, distance and angle, so the list is a sample of the worlds our instruments can currently catch

questions.q: 3. What has the catch already revised in the scientific imagination?
options: Every new planet is already known to have oceans and life
The habitable zone is a discovery of oceans, not a starting condition
Planets come in unexpected sizes and orbits, including worlds between Earth and Neptune in size, very short periods, and tightly packed systems
A planet in the right range of light always has the right atmosphere and a surface

questions.q: 4. What is the next stage of exploration described here, and what caution comes with it?
options: Declaring Earth 2.0 in a headline as soon as a candidate appears

Reading atmospheres, where possible, by watching starlight filter through gases, and looking for molecules hard to explain without biology, while remembering that geology and chemistry can also surprise us
Withdrawing from all space observatories
Ignoring atmospheres entirely and searching only for surfaces by tour

questions.q: 5. How should a biased sample shape students’ claims?
options: If we are better at finding large, close planets, we should not conclude that small, far ones are rare; students can list what is known about one system and what is still a guess
We should conclude that small, far planets are rare because they are missing from a biased list
A headline about Earth 2.0 is never too early
Exploration at this scale is a tour, not a disciplined use of shadows, wobbles and spectra

senior.title: 🌋 Life in Extreme Places: What Earthly Extremes Teach Explorers of Other Worlds
senior.content:
Life, for a long time, was imagined as a tender guest of mild climates: sunlight, liquid water at a comfortable temperature, and a gentle chemistry. Fieldwork has steadily undone that picture. In boiling springs, in ice, in rock kilometres down, in water so salty that it would parch an ordinary cell, and around deep-sea vents that never see the sun, organisms persist. They are often microbes, and they use chemical energy, unusual enzymes, or protective coatings to stay intact. Scientists call many of them extremophiles — lovers of the extreme — though from their point of view the “extreme” is simply home. Their existence does not prove that other planets are inhabited. It does change the map of places worth searching, and it trains the questions that a probe or a telescope should ask.

Each earthly habitat is a lesson with a limit. A vent at the ocean floor shows that sunlight is not the only possible engine of an ecosystem, which matters for a moon with a hidden ocean under ice. A dry valley in Antarctica shows how life can wait in stone for a little moisture, which matters for the surface of Mars. A highly acidic river tests the edges of biochemistry, and a subglacial lake tests how a community might survive in the dark for long ages. The lesson is not “therefore life is everywhere.” Conditions can still be too harsh, too unstable, or too short-lived. The lesson is that the search should not be confined to a postcard version of Earth, and that “follow the water” is a useful slogan only if we also follow the chemistry, the energy source, and the time a habitat has had to work.

Exploration of this kind is both local and planetary. Teams sample carefully, so that they do not contaminate a rare site or carry one world’s microbes to the next in a spacecraft. They compare DNA, metabolism and minerals, and they design instruments that could, one day, look for similar signatures far from home. Students can choose one extreme habitat, list what the organisms use for energy, and then name a place in the solar system that shares a feature — ice, salt, heat, or darkness — without leaping to a conclusion about inhabitants. The honesty of the comparison is part of the science.

There is a human side to the work as well. Some of these sites are culturally important, fragile, or already stressed by tourism and mining. Scientific exploration that treats the Earth only as a rehearsal stage for Mars can damage the very examples it needs. Protecting a spring or a vent is not a distraction from the search for other life. It is a way of keeping the library open.

The universe may or may not be thick with living worlds. Until that question is settled, the extremes of our own planet remain among the best laboratories we have: not because they are alien, but because they show how wide the idea of “a place for life” can become when we actually go and look.
senior.translation:
在很长一段时间里，生命被想象成温和气候的娇嫩客人：阳光，舒适温度下的液态水，以及一种温和的化学。田野工作已经稳定地拆解了那幅图画。在沸腾的泉里，在冰里，在数公里深的岩石里，在咸得会使普通细胞干枯的水里，以及在从未见过太阳的深海喷口周围，生物持续存在着。它们常常是微生物，它们使用化学能、不寻常的酶，或保护性的涂层来保持完整。科学家称它们中的许多为嗜极生物——极端的爱好者——尽管从它们的观点来看，“极端”只是家。它们的存在并不能证明其他行星有人居住。它确实改变了值得搜寻的地点的地图，并训练一艘探测器或一架望远镜应当问的问题。

每一个地球上的栖息地都是一个带有限度的教训。海底的一个喷口显示，阳光并不是一个生态系统唯一可能的引擎，这对一颗在冰下藏着海洋的卫星很重要。南极的一条干燥山谷显示，生命可以在石头里等待一点点湿气，这对火星的表面很重要。一条高酸性的河测试生物化学的边缘，一个冰下湖测试一个群落如何可能在黑暗中生存漫长的年代。教训并不是“因此生命到处都是。”条件仍然可能太严酷、太不稳定，或持续得太短。教训是，搜寻不应当被限制在明信片版本的地球上，而且“跟随水”只有在我们也跟随化学、能源，以及一个栖息地已经工作的时间时，才是一句有用的口号。

这种探索既是本地的，也是行星的。团队小心取样，以免污染一个稀有地点，或在一艘航天器里把一个世界的微生物带到下一个世界。他们比较DNA、新陈代谢和矿物，并设计有朝一日可以在远离家乡的地方寻找相似签名的仪器。学生可以选择一个极端栖息地，列出生物用什么作为能量，然后说出太阳系中一个共享某种特征——冰、盐、热或黑暗——的地方，而不跳到关于居住者的结论。比较的诚实是科学的一部分。

这项工作也有人性的一面。这些地点中的一些在文化上很重要，脆弱，或已经受到旅游和采矿的压力。把地球只当作火星的一次排练舞台的科学探索，可能损害它所需要的那些例子本身。保护一处泉或一个喷口，并不是对寻找其他生命的干扰。它是一种让图书馆保持开放的方式。

宇宙也许充满生命世界，也许并不。直到那个问题被解决之前，我们自己行星上的极端，仍然属于我们拥有的最好实验室之列：不是因为它们是外星的，而是因为它们显示，当我们真的去看时，“一个生命的地方”这个想法可以变得多么宽。

Because they are alien, and not part of our own planet

senior.title: 🪱 Living Soil: The Hidden Ecology Under Our Feet
senior.content:
Soil is easy to treat as dirt: a brown background for plants, a surface to pave, a thing to wash off a shoe. Science describes it as a living system. A handful of healthy soil can contain more organisms than there are people on Earth — bacteria, fungi, insects, worms, and the roots that trade with them. These lives break down leaves and bodies, lock and release nutrients, bind particles into crumbs that hold water and air, and store a large share of the planet’s carbon. When the community is intact, rain soaks in instead of running off, plants find food without a constant imported dose, and the ground can recover after a dry spell. When the community is broken by repeated ploughing, bare exposure, contamination or compaction, the same land can harden, wash away, or lose the ability to feed a crop without ever heavier inputs.

The science is practical and still incomplete. Researchers measure organic matter, microbial diversity, the structure of pores, and the time it takes water to sink. They trace how a fungus can extend a root’s reach, and how a shortage of one element can limit the whole web. They also study how long carbon stays in the soil, which matters for climate as well as for fertility. Simple field tests — a spade, a jar of water, a count of earthworms — can already tell a farmer or a student whether the ground is a habitat or only a powder. Satellite data and laboratory sequences add scale, but they do not replace the need to look at a particular field after rain.

Environmental choices follow from the biology. Cover crops, mixed planting, less aggressive tillage, and the return of compost or manure are not only traditions; they are ways of feeding the underground city. Pesticides and fertilisers can raise a harvest in the short term and still thin the community that would have done part of the work for free. Sealing soil under a parking lot is a permanent loss of that service in that place. Restoration is possible, and it is slow. A field that has been stripped does not become a sponge in a season, and a city that has left only thin, compacted strips along a road will have to invent new ways to give soil room.

Students can compare two nearby patches — a lawn treated as a carpet, a neglected hedge bottom, a vegetable bed with mulch — and record colour, smell, infiltration, and visible life. The contrast is a lesson in environmental science that needs no distant wilderness. Soil will not speak in a press conference. It will, if we measure and wait, show whether a landscape is being used as a living partner or as a surface to be spent.
senior.translation:
土壤很容易被当作尘土：植物的棕色背景，一块可以铺砌的表面，一种要从鞋子上洗掉的东西。科学把它描述为一个活的系统。一小把健康的土壤里可以含有比地球上的人还多的生物——细菌、真菌、昆虫、蠕虫，以及与它们交易的根。这些生命分解叶子和躯体，锁定并释放养分，把颗粒粘成能够保持水和空气的团粒，并储存地球碳的很大一部分。当这个群落完整时，雨水渗入而不是流走，植物在没有持续进口剂量的情况下找到食物，土地可以在一段干旱之后恢复。当这个群落被反复耕作、裸露、污染或压实打破时，同一块地可能变硬、被冲走，或失去在没有越来越重的投入时喂养作物的能力。

这门科学是实际的，却仍然不完整。研究者测量有机质、微生物多样性、孔隙的结构，以及水沉下去所需的时间。他们追踪一种真菌如何延伸一根根的到达范围，以及一种元素的短缺如何限制整个网。他们也研究碳在土壤中停留多久，这对气候和肥力都重要。简单的田间测试——一把锹，一罐水，一次蚯蚓的计数——已经可以告诉一位农民或一个学生，这片地是一个栖息地，还是只是一种粉末。卫星数据和实验室序列增加了尺度，但它们并不能代替在雨后看一块特定田地的需要。

环境上的选择跟随着生物学。覆盖作物、混合种植、较少攻击性的耕作，以及堆肥或粪便的返回，不仅仅是传统；它们是喂养这座地下城市的方式。农药和肥料可以在短期内提高收成，却仍然可能削薄那个本会免费做一部分工作的群落。把土壤封闭在一个停车场下，是那种服务在那个地方的永久损失。恢复是可能的，它也是缓慢的。一块被剥去的田不会在一个季节里变成一块海绵，一座只沿着道路留下细而压实的条带的城市，将必须发明新的方式来给土壤空间。

学生可以比较附近的两块地——一块被当作地毯对待的草坪，一条被忽视的树篱底部，一个有覆盖物的菜畦——并记录颜色、气味、下渗，以及可见的生命。这种对比是一堂不需要遥远荒野的环境科学课。土壤不会在新闻发布会上说话。如果我们测量并等待，它会显示，一片风景是正在被当作一个活的伙伴来使用，还是当作一个将被花掉的表面。

questions.q: 1. How does science describe soil, in contrast to treating it as dirt?
options: As a brown background that never holds water or carbon
As a powder that cannot contain more organisms than a handful of people
As a living system whose organisms break down matter, lock and release nutrients, bind crumbs that hold water and air, and store a large share of the planet’s carbon
As a surface whose only use is to be washed off a shoe
questions.exp: 文中把土壤描述为活的系统：生物分解物质、锁定并释放养分、形成保持水与空气的团粒，并储存大量碳。

questions.q: 2. What happens when the underground community is broken?
options: Rain still soaks in, and plants find food without imported doses
Repeated ploughing, bare exposure, contamination or compaction can make the land harden, wash away, or lose the ability to feed a crop without ever heavier inputs
The ground always recovers after a dry spell, even when the community is gone
A constant imported dose becomes unnecessary
questions.exp: 文中说反复耕作、裸露、污染或压实可能使土地变硬、被冲走，或失去在没有更重投入时养活作物的能力。

questions.q: 3. What do researchers measure, and what can a simple field test already tell?
options: Organic matter, microbial diversity, pore structure and the time water takes to sink; a spade, a jar of water and a count of earthworms can already show whether the ground is a habitat or only a powder
Only satellite data, which replace any need to look at a particular field after rain
The time carbon stays in the soil, with no interest in fertility
A press conference in which soil speaks for itself
questions.exp: 文中提到测量有机质、微生物多样性、孔隙结构和下渗时间；锹、一罐水和蚯蚓计数已能判断土地是栖息地还是粉末。

questions.q: 4. Which environmental choices follow from the biology of soil?
options: Pesticides and fertilisers never thin the community that does part of the work
A stripped field becomes a sponge in a single season
A city needs no new ways to give soil room if only thin compacted strips remain

Cover crops, mixed planting, less aggressive tillage and the return of compost or manure feed the underground city, while sealing soil under a parking lot is a permanent loss of that service in that place
questions.exp: 文中指出覆盖作物、混合种植、较少攻击性耕作和归还堆肥是在喂养地下城市；把土壤封闭在停车场下则是该地服务的永久损失。

questions.q: 5. What nearby contrast can students record as a lesson in environmental science?
options: A distant wilderness only, with no local patch
Colour and smell, without infiltration or visible life

Two patches, such as a lawn treated as a carpet and a mulched vegetable bed, compared for colour, smell, infiltration and visible life, to see whether a landscape is used as a living partner or as a surface to be spent
A single carpet lawn, with no contrast
questions.exp: 文中建议比较附近两块地的颜色、气味、下渗和可见生命，看风景是被当作活的伙伴还是被花掉的表面。

senior.title: 💧 When Lakes Choke: Nutrients, Algae and Freshwater in Trouble
senior.content:
A lake can look calm and still be in trouble. When too many nutrients, especially phosphorus and nitrogen from farms, sewage and some detergents, wash into still water, microscopic algae can multiply until the surface turns green or brown. In the worst cases a bloom uses up oxygen as it dies and decays, and fish, plants and the animals that depend on them suffocate. Some blooms also release toxins that make drinking water, swimming and even the air near the shore unsafe. Scientists call this chain eutrophication: a lake is being overfed, and the extra fertility becomes a form of choking. The process is environmental science in a tight loop — chemistry, biology, weather and human waste meeting in one basin.

The sources are often scattered, which makes them hard to see and politically hard to name. A field that loses soil after rain, a leaky septic system, a factory pipe, or a city storm drain can all deliver a little too much. Warm, still weather can then give the algae an advantage, which is why late summer is a familiar season for warnings, and why a warming climate can make an old problem more frequent. Shallow lakes, and lakes with long residence times — water that stays for months or years — are especially vulnerable. A single dramatic dump is not required. Years of modest surplus can shift the system into a new state, with murky water and little of the clear, plant-rich life that used to live on the bottom. Returning from that state can take more than a pause in the surplus, because nutrients stored in the mud can keep feeding blooms.

The science of response is as important as the science of diagnosis. Measuring phosphorus, oxygen, algal types and toxins tells a city when to close a beach or change a water treatment. Cutting the load at the source — better sewage treatment, buffer strips along streams, careful fertiliser timing, bans on certain phosphates — is slower to appear in a headline and more decisive over a decade. In some lakes, extra tools are used: mixing the water, adding a substance that binds phosphorus in the sediment, or restoring wetlands that can intercept runoff. Each tool has a cost and a limit, and none replaces the need to stop the surplus at the gate.

Students can follow one local lake or reservoir through a year of public data, if those data exist, and can ask where the nutrients likely come from. They can also learn to read a green surface with care: not every colour is a toxic bloom, and not every clear lake is healthy. Freshwater is not a decoration around a city. It is a living system with a budget of nutrients. When the budget is ignored, the lake keeps the accounts in a language of oxygen, light and silence where fish used to be.
senior.translation:
一座湖可以看起来平静，却仍然处于麻烦之中。当太多养分，尤其是来自农场、污水和某些洗涤剂的磷和氮，冲进静止的水里时，微小的藻类可以繁殖，直到表面变成绿色或棕色。在最坏的情况下，一次水华在死亡和腐烂时用尽氧气，鱼、植物和依赖它们的动物就会窒息。有些水华还会释放毒素，使饮用水、游泳，甚至岸边的空气变得不安全。科学家称这串链条为富营养化：一座湖正在被喂得过多，额外的肥力变成一种窒息。这个过程是一个紧密环中的环境科学——化学、生物学、天气和人类废物在一个流域里相遇。

来源常常是分散的，这使它们难以被看见，在政治上也难以被命名。一块在雨后失去土壤的田，一个泄漏的化粪系统，一根工厂管道，或一条城市雨水排水沟，都可以输送稍微过多的养分。温暖而静止的天气然后可以给藻类一种优势，这就是为什么夏末是一个熟悉的警告季节，以及为什么变暖的气候可以使一个老问题更频繁。浅湖，以及停留时间很长——水会停留数月或数年——的湖，特别脆弱。并不需要一次戏剧性的倾倒。多年适度的盈余就可以把系统推进一种新状态，水色浑浊，底部曾经生活着的清澈、植物丰富的生命所剩无几。从那种状态返回，可能需要的不仅仅是盈余的一次暂停，因为贮存在泥里的养分可以继续喂养水华。

应对的科学与诊断的科学同样重要。测量磷、氧气、藻类种类和毒素，告诉一座城市何时关闭海滩或改变水处理。在源头削减负荷——更好的污水处理，溪流沿岸的缓冲带，谨慎的施肥时机，对某些磷酸盐的禁止——在标题里出现得更慢，在十年里却更有决定性。在一些湖里，会使用额外的工具：混合水体，加入一种在沉积物中结合磷的物质，或恢复可以拦截径流的湿地。每一种工具都有成本和限度，没有一种可以代替在入口处停止盈余的需要。

学生可以在公共数据存在的情况下，跟随本地的一座湖或水库度过一年的数据，并可以问养分可能来自哪里。他们也可以学习谨慎地阅读一片绿色的表面：不是每一种颜色都是有毒水华，也不是每一座清澈的湖都是健康的。淡水不是一座城市周围的装饰。它是一个有着养分预算的活系统。当预算被忽视时，湖会用氧气、光，以及曾经有鱼的地方的沉默这种语言，来记账。

questions.q: 1. What is eutrophication, as described in the passage?
options: A lake that looks calm is always healthy
Fish suffocate only when there are too few nutrients
Algae never change the colour of a surface
A lake is overfed with nutrients, especially phosphorus and nitrogen, so algae can bloom, use up oxygen as they decay, and sometimes release toxins
questions.exp: 文中把富营养化描述为湖被磷和氮等养分喂得过多，藻类繁殖，腐烂时耗尽氧气，有时还释放毒素。

questions.q: 2. Why are the sources often hard to see and politically hard to name?
options: A single dramatic dump is always required before a lake can shift state
Only one obvious pipe is ever responsible
They are scattered: a field after rain, a leaky septic system, a factory pipe or a city storm drain can each deliver a little too much
Warm, still weather never gives algae an advantage
questions.exp: 文中说来源分散：雨后的田、泄漏的化粪系统、工厂管道或城市雨水管都可以各自输送稍微过多的养分。

questions.q: 3. Why can returning from a murky new state take more than a pause in the surplus?
options: A modest surplus can never shift the system
Nutrients stored in the mud can keep feeding blooms, especially in shallow lakes or lakes where water stays for months or years
Clear, plant-rich life on the bottom always returns in a week
A warming climate makes the old problem less frequent
questions.exp: 文中指出泥中储存的养分可以继续喂养水华，因此仅暂停盈余可能不够，浅湖或停留时间长的湖尤其脆弱。

questions.q: 4. Which responses does the writer say are decisive over a decade, even if they are slower to appear in a headline?
options: Cutting the load at the source: better sewage treatment, buffer strips, careful fertiliser timing, and bans on certain phosphates
Only mixing the water, with no cut at the gate
Closing a beach forever, without measuring phosphorus, oxygen or toxins
Replacing all source cuts with a single substance in the sediment
questions.exp: 文中认为在源头削减负荷——更好的污水处理、缓冲带、谨慎施肥时机和限制某些磷酸盐——在十年尺度上更有决定性。

questions.q: 5. How should students read a green surface, and what budget does freshwater have?
options: Every green surface is a toxic bloom
Every clear lake is healthy
Freshwater is only a decoration around a city, with no nutrient budget

Not every colour is a toxic bloom, and not every clear lake is healthy; freshwater is a living system with a budget of nutrients, and when the budget is ignored the lake keeps accounts in oxygen, light and silence where fish used to be
questions.exp: 文中提醒并非每一种颜色都是有毒水华，也并非每座清澈的湖都健康；淡水是有养分预算的活系统。

senior.title: 🛂 Passports and Visas: An Unequal Map of Who May Move
senior.content:
A classroom map often shows countries in even colours, as if each were equally open to a visitor. A passport tells a different story. Depending on the document a person holds, a border may be a brief stamp, a long queue for a visa, a costly interview, or a wall that does not open at all. Scholars and journalists have described this as a hierarchy of mobility: some nationalities can travel for tourism, study or work with little friction, while others must plan for months, pay fees they can barely afford, and still risk a refusal that needs no detailed explanation. The inequality is legal, not a matter of personal virtue. Two students with the same grades and the same invitation can face opposite odds because of the booklet in their pocket.

A global view has to include this map, because so many of the world’s opportunities — a conference, a hospital, a university, a family wedding, a safer place during a crisis — sit on the other side of a checkpoint. Visa policy is often justified as a way to manage security, labour markets and public services, and those aims are not imaginary. The ethical problem appears when the burden of proof falls so heavily on people from poorer or more troubled countries that talent, kinship and ordinary curiosity are treated as suspicious by default. Long delays can make a scholarship expire, a job vanish, or a parent miss a funeral. Informal brokers then sell help, and the already expensive process becomes a maze that rewards those who can pay.

There is also a quieter effect on how people imagine the world. A young person who can book a ticket on a whim learns that the planet is available. A young person who has never been allowed a short trip may still study the same geography, but the planet remains a picture. Exchange programmes, scientific meetings and even sports are thinner when only some passports clear the gate. Companies and universities that call themselves global sometimes discover that their staff and students cannot actually gather.

Reform is not a single slogan. It can mean faster, clearer decisions, lower fees, more multi-entry visas for study and research, and rules that do not punish an entire nationality for the act of a few. It can also mean honesty about why some doors stay narrow. Students can compare two passports’ visa-free lists, or follow one refused application and ask what evidence would have been enough. They can also listen to classmates whose holidays are not a simple purchase.

A connected world is often praised as if connection were evenly shared. The passport line is one of the places where that praise can be tested. Global citizenship, if the phrase is to mean anything, has to notice who is still waiting at the window, and whose journey was over before the plane was booked.
senior.translation:
教室里的地图常常用均匀的颜色显示国家，仿佛每一个都同样向访客开放。一本护照讲述一个不同的故事。取决于一个人所持的文件，边界可能是一个简短的印章，一长队签证，一次昂贵的面试，或一堵根本不打开的墙。学者和记者把这描述为一种流动的等级：一些国籍可以几乎没有摩擦地为旅游、学习或工作而旅行，而另一些必须计划数月，支付他们几乎负担不起的费用，并且仍然冒着一次不需要详细解释的拒绝的风险。这种不平等是法律上的，而不是个人美德的问题。两个成绩相同、邀请相同的学生，可能因为口袋里的那本小册子而面对相反的机会。

一种全球视野必须包括这张地图，因为世界上如此多的机会——一次会议，一家医院，一所大学，一场家庭婚礼，危机中一个更安全的地方——坐落在一个检查站的另一边。签证政策常常被证明为管理安全、劳动力市场和公共服务的一种方式，而这些目标并不是想象出来的。当证明的负担如此沉重地落在来自更穷或更动荡国家的人身上，以致才能、亲缘和普通的好奇被默认视为可疑时，伦理问题就会出现。漫长的延误可以使一份奖学金过期，一份工作消失，或一位父母错过一场葬礼。非正式的中介然后出售帮助，而已经昂贵的过程变成一座奖励那些能够付钱的人的迷宫。

它对人们如何想象世界还有一种更安静的影响。一个可以一时兴起就订票的年轻人，会学到行星是可获得的。一个从未被允许一次短途旅行的年轻人，也许仍然学习同一门地理，但行星仍然是一幅图画。交流项目、科学会议，甚至体育，在只有一些护照能通过大门时，会变得更稀薄。那些自称全球的公司和大学，有时会发现它们的员工和学生实际上无法聚集。

改革不是一句单一的口号。它可以意味着更快、更清楚的决定，更低的费用，更多用于学习和研究的多次入境签证，以及不因少数人的行为而惩罚整个国籍的规则。它也可以意味着对为什么一些门仍然狭窄保持诚实。学生可以比较两本护照的免签名单，或跟踪一次被拒绝的申请并问什么证据本来会足够。他们也可以倾听那些假期并不是一次简单购买的同学。

一个相互连接的世界常常被赞美，仿佛连接是被均匀分享的。护照队列是那句赞美可以被测试的地方之一。全球公民，如果这个短语要有任何意义，就必须注意到谁还在窗口等待，以及谁的旅程在飞机被预订之前就已经结束了。

options: A hierarchy of mobility, in which some nationalities travel with little friction while others face long queues, costly visas and refusals, so that two similar students can meet opposite odds because of the booklet in their pocket
That every country is equally open to a visitor
That inequality of movement is a matter of personal virtue, not law
That a brief stamp, a long queue and a closed wall are the same experience

A scholarship, a job and a funeral are never affected by delay
Only tourism sits on the other side of a border
Many opportunities — a conference, a hospital, a university, a wedding, a safer place in a crisis — sit on the other side of a checkpoint

When fees are low and decisions are always fast and clear
When the burden of proof falls so heavily on people from poorer or more troubled countries that talent, kinship and ordinary curiosity are treated as suspicious by default
When an entire nationality is never affected by the act of a few
questions.exp: 文中认为当证明负担沉重地落在较穷或更动荡国家的人身上，才能、亲缘和普通好奇被默认视为可疑时，伦理问题就出现了。

questions.q: 4. What quieter effect on the imagination of the world does the writer describe?
options: Exchange programmes and scientific meetings become thicker when only some passports clear the gate
A young person who can book a ticket on a whim learns that the planet is available, while one who has never been allowed a short trip may still study geography with the planet remaining a picture
Companies that call themselves global always find that staff can gather
A short trip is equally simple for every classmate
questions.exp: 文中对比可以一时兴起订票的年轻人与从未被允许短途旅行的年轻人：后者学的地理里，行星仍可能只是一幅图画。

options: Faster clearer decisions, lower fees, more multi-entry visas for study, and rules that do not punish a whole nationality; students can compare visa-free lists or listen to classmates whose holidays are not a simple purchase

senior.title: ⚡ The Energy Transition: Why Clean Power Is a Social Project, Not Only a Technical One
senior.content:
Replacing coal, oil and gas with cleaner electricity — from wind, solar, water, and, in some plans, nuclear power or carefully used gas as a bridge — is often described as a technical race: better panels, bigger turbines, smarter grids. The technology matters, and it has already become cheaper and more capable than many forecasts once allowed. Sustainable development, however, is not only a question of whether a country can generate enough clean kilowatt-hours. It is a question of who pays for the change, who works in the new system, whose land holds the new machines, and whether the lights stay on in a poor neighbourhood while a richer one enjoys the first benefits. An energy transition that lowers emissions but deepens inequality, or that leaves workers from closing plants without a path, has not yet earned the word sustainable.

The social project has several layers. Grids must be extended and balanced, because wind and sun do not arrive on demand; that is engineering, and it is also public investment and regulation. Homes and buses must be able to use the new power, which means wiring, charging points, and prices that ordinary families can bear. Mining for the metals in batteries and turbines raises its own duties to land and labour, sometimes far from the cities that will use the electricity. Communities asked to host a wind farm or a transmission line deserve a real say and a real share, not only a letter after the route is fixed. And the workers who now keep fossil plants running need training, time, and a wage they can plan a life on, not a slogan about the future and a sudden empty locker.

There are honest disagreements: how fast to close a plant, how much to rely on one source, how to keep power affordable in a cold week. Denying those tensions does not make a plan more green. A durable path names them and still moves, with public data, staged targets, and help for the households that would otherwise face a higher bill first. Students can trace one local change — a new solar field, a coal plant’s last years, a bus route going electric — and list who gained, who waited, and what was promised. They can also compare two countries’ transitions and ask whether “cheap clean power” included the people who live beside the equipment.

Sustainable development asked, from the beginning, that present needs be met without stealing from the future. In energy, the future is the climate. The present includes towns that fear silence in the factory, and towns that fear a new tower on the ridge. A transition worthy of the name treats both as part of the same project: building a system that can last, and a society that can live with the building of it.
senior.translation:
用更清洁的电力——来自风、太阳、水，以及在一些计划中，核能，或被谨慎用作桥梁的天然气——取代煤、石油和天然气，常常被描述为一场技术竞赛：更好的电池板，更大的涡轮机，更聪明的电网。技术很重要，并且它已经变得比许多预测曾经允许的更便宜、更有能力。然而，可持续发展不仅仅是一个国家是否能够产生足够的清洁千瓦时的问题。它是一个谁为这一变化付钱，谁在新系统中工作，谁的土地容纳新机器，以及当更富的街区享受第一批益处时，穷街区的灯是否仍然亮着的问题。一场降低排放却加深不平等，或让关闭工厂的工人没有出路的能源转型，还没有赢得可持续这个词。

这个社会项目有几层。电网必须被延伸和平衡，因为风和太阳并不是按需到来的；那是工程，它也是公共投资和监管。住宅和公共汽车必须能够使用新的电力，这意味着线路、充电点，以及普通家庭能够承受的价格。为电池和涡轮机中的金属而进行的采矿，对土地和劳动提出了它自己的责任，有时远离将使用这些电的城市。被要求接待一座风电场或一条输电线路的社区，应当得到真正的发言权和真正的份额，而不仅仅是在路线被确定之后的一封信。而现在让化石工厂运行的工人需要培训、时间，以及一份他们可以用来计划生活的工资，而不是一句关于未来的口号和一只突然空了的储物柜。

存在诚实的分歧：关闭一座工厂要多快，对一种来源要依赖多少，如何在一个寒冷的星期里保持电力可负担。否认这些张力并不会使一项计划更绿。一条持久的路径会叫出它们，却仍然前进，带着公共数据、分阶段的目标，以及对那些否则会首先面对更高账单的家庭的帮助。学生可以追踪一次本地的变化——一片新的太阳能场地，一座煤厂的最后几年，一条正在电气化的公交线路——并列出谁获得了，谁等待了，以及什么被承诺了。他们也可以比较两个国家的转型，并问“便宜的清洁电力”是否包括了住在设备旁边的人。

可持续发展从一开始就要求，当前的需要被满足，而不从未来偷窃。在能源上，未来就是气候。当前包括那些担心工厂沉默的城镇，和那些担心山脊上新塔的城镇。一场配得上这个名称的转型，把两者都当作同一个项目的一部分：建造一个能够持久的系统，以及一个能够与建造它这件事一起生活的社会。

senior.title: 🖼️ Dual Coding: Learning with Words and Pictures Together
senior.content:
A difficult idea often arrives as a wall of sentences. Dual coding is a study method that gives the idea a second door: you represent the same meaning in words and in a visual form, and you practise moving between the two. The visual might be a simple diagram of a process, a labelled map, a timeline, a comparison table, or a sketch of a machine’s parts. It is not a decoration in the margin, and it is not a page covered with clip art. The point is that the brain can hold verbal and visual traces that support each other at the moment of recall. When one path is blocked in an exam or in a conversation, the other may still be open. Research on learning has repeatedly found that well-matched words and graphics can improve understanding, especially for processes, structures and comparisons, provided the two are actually about the same idea.

The method asks for care in the making. Copying a textbook figure without saying what each arrow means is only half the work. A useful practice is to hide the figure and redraw it from memory, then hide the drawing and write a short explanation, then check both against the source. If a label cannot be explained, it was not yet learned. If the drawing is prettier than it is accurate, it may mislead later. Students can also take a dense paragraph and turn it into three boxes and two arrows, or take a diagram and tell it as a story in complete sentences. The translation in both directions is the exercise. Colour can help if it carries a meaning — one colour for inputs, another for outputs — and it can distract if it is only a habit of the highlighter.

There are limits. Some material is almost purely verbal, such as a precise legal definition, and a picture may add little. A graphic that is too crowded can overload attention, which is the opposite of help. Dual coding should not become an excuse to avoid practice questions, because using the idea is still the test that matters. In a group, one student can talk through a diagram while another draws, then they switch, which quickly reveals gaps.

Teachers can model a spare, clear figure on the board and then wipe it, asking the class to rebuild it. Students can keep a small bank of their own diagrams, revised after mistakes, rather than a museum of downloaded images. Over a term, the bank becomes a personal language for the course.

A learning method earns its place when it changes what you can retrieve on a blank page. Dual coding is a disciplined way of refusing to let an idea live in only one form. Words keep the precision; pictures keep the shape. Together, they give memory more than one way home.
senior.translation:
一个困难的想法常常作为一堵句子的墙到来。双编码是一种给这个想法第二扇门的学习方法：你用词语和一种视觉形式表示同一意义，并练习在两者之间移动。视觉形式可能是一个过程的简单图解，一张带标签的地图，一条时间线，一张比较表，或一幅机器部件的草图。它不是页边的装饰，也不是一页贴满剪贴画的纸。要点是，大脑可以保存彼此在回忆时刻相互支持的语言痕迹和视觉痕迹。当一条路在考试或谈话中被堵住时，另一条可能仍然开放。关于学习的研究一再发现，匹配良好的词语和图形可以改善理解，尤其是对于过程、结构和比较，只要这两者实际上是关于同一个想法的。

这种方法在制作上要求小心。复制一幅教材插图却不说出每一支箭头意味着什么，只是一半的工作。一种有用的练习是，藏起那幅图并从记忆中重画它，然后藏起那幅画并写一段短的解释，再对照来源检查两者。如果一个标签不能被解释，它就还没有被学会。如果那幅画比它准确的程度更漂亮，它稍后可能误导。学生也可以把一段密集的文字变成三个方框和两支箭头，或把一幅图解用完整的句子讲成一个故事。两个方向上的翻译才是练习。如果颜色携带一种意义——一种颜色代表输入，另一种代表输出——它可以帮忙；如果它只是荧光笔的一种习惯，它可能分心。

也有限度。有些材料几乎是纯粹语言的，例如一个精确的法律定义，一幅图画可能增加得很少。一幅太拥挤的图形可能使注意超载，这与帮助相反。双编码不应当变成回避练习题的借口，因为使用这个想法仍然是要紧的测试。在小组里，一个学生可以一边讲一幅图解，另一个画，然后他们交换，这会很快揭示缺口。

老师可以在黑板上示范一幅俭省而清楚的图，然后擦掉它，要求全班重建它。学生可以保留一个他们自己的图解的小库，在错误之后修订，而不是一座下载图像的博物馆。在一个学期里，这个库会变成这门课的一种个人语言。

一种学习方法在它改变了你在一张空白页上能够提取的东西时，才赢得它的位置。双编码是一种有纪律的方式，拒绝让一个想法只生活在一种形式里。词语保持精确；图画保持形状。一起，它们给记忆多于一条回家的路。

senior.title: 🌱 Self-Efficacy: The Quiet Confidence That You Can Learn This
senior.content:
A student can want a goal, understand a lesson, and still stall, because a quieter question has not been answered: “Can I actually do this?” Psychologists call that judgement self-efficacy — the belief that you can organise and carry out the actions a task requires. It is not the same as general self-esteem, which is a broader feeling of worth, and it is not the same as a wish. It is closer to a practical estimate: given this problem, these tools, and this much time, do I expect to make progress? Research has linked stronger self-efficacy in a domain to greater effort, more persistence after a setback, and a calmer reading of difficulty as information rather than as a verdict on the self. Growth, in this sense, is not only the arrival of a new skill. It is the changing story you tell about your ability to acquire the next one.

Self-efficacy is built, not issued. The most reliable source is a mastery experience: a task that was effortful and then completed, even in part. A teacher or a parent who only praises, without arranging a success that the student can recognise as their own work, may give comfort and still leave the estimate unchanged. Watching a peer who is similar to you succeed can also help, because it answers “people like me can do this.” Verbal encouragement matters when it is specific and believable; a sweeping “you can do anything” often collapses at the first hard page. The body speaks too. A racing heart can be read as danger or as readiness, and learning to name the feeling without leaving the desk is part of the skill.

There are traps. Inflated confidence that has not been tested can lead to careless work, and a single public failure can shrink the estimate too far if it is treated as a global sentence. The useful move is to shrink the task, not the person: a shorter passage, a worked first step, a second attempt after a night of sleep. Keeping a brief record of “I could not do this on Monday; I can do this much on Friday” gives the mind evidence that compliments cannot invent.

Students can choose one subject in which they feel ineffective and design a week of small, completable pieces, with a review of what actually improved. They can also notice the difference between “this is hard” and “I am not the kind of person who can.” The first sentence leaves the door open. The second closes it in advance.

Psychological growth includes learning how to trust your future effort without pretending that the work is already done. Self-efficacy is that trust in a usable form. It does not guarantee a high score. It makes it more likely that you will still be at the desk when the score is being decided.
senior.translation:
一个学生可以想要一个目标，理解一课，却仍然停住，因为一个更安静的问题还没有被回答：“我实际上能做这个吗？”心理学家称那种判断为自我效能——一种你能够组织并实施一项任务所需行动的信念。它与一般的自尊不同，后者是一种更宽的价值感，它也与一个愿望不同。它更接近一种实际的估计：面对这个问题、这些工具和这么多的时间，我是否期待取得进展？研究已经把一个领域里更强的自我效能，与更大的努力、挫折之后更多的坚持，以及把困难更平静地读作信息而不是对自我的判决联系起来。在这个意义上，成长不仅仅是一项新技能的到达。它是你关于自己有能力获得下一个技能所讲述的、正在变化的故事。

自我效能是被建造的，不是被颁发的。最可靠的来源是一次掌握的经验：一项曾经费力、然后被完成的任务，即使只是部分完成。一位只赞美、却不安排一次学生能够认作自己工作的成功的老师或父母，可能给予安慰，却仍然使这个估计保持不变。观看一个与你相似的同伴成功，也可以帮忙，因为它回答了“像我这样的人可以做这个。”口头鼓励在具体且可信时重要；一句空泛的“你什么都能做”常常在第一页难的地方倒塌。身体也会说话。一颗快速跳动的心可以被读作危险，或被读作准备就绪，学会给这种感觉命名、却不离开桌子，是这种技能的一部分。

也有陷阱。未经测试的膨胀自信可能导致粗心的工作，而一次公开的失败，如果被当作一句全局的判决，可能把估计收缩得太远。有用的举动是缩小任务，而不是缩小人：一段更短的文章，一个已被做出的第一步，经过一夜睡眠之后的第二次尝试。保留一份简短的记录——“星期一我还不能做这个；星期五我已经能做这么多”——会给头脑提供赞美所不能发明的证据。

学生可以选择一个他们感觉低效的科目，并设计一周小小的、可完成的部分，再回顾什么实际上改进了。他们也可以注意到“这很难”和“我不是那种能做这件事的人”之间的差别。第一句让门开着。第二句提前关上它。

心理上的成长，包括学会如何信任你未来的努力，而不假装工作已经被做完。自我效能就是那种信任的一种可用形式。它不保证一个高分。它使你在分数正在被决定时，更可能仍然坐在桌边。

senior.title: 🎯 When Perfect Becomes a Trap: Softening Perfectionism
senior.content:
High standards can be a form of care: you revise a paragraph, check a calculation, and refuse to hand in work you know is careless. Perfectionism begins to harm growth when the standard is no longer a guide and becomes a gate that nothing may pass. A draft is delayed because it is not yet flawless. A hobby is abandoned because a first attempt is clumsy. A person waits to speak until the sentence is ideal, and the conversation moves on without them. The feeling underneath is often not pride but fear — fear of a visible flaw, of being judged, of being only ordinary. Psychological research has distinguished striving for excellence, which can coexist with learning, from a harsher pattern in which self-worth is made to depend on a performance that is never allowed to be merely good.

The costs are practical as well as emotional. Time is spent polishing the already adequate and is stolen from the next problem, the night’s sleep, or a friendship. Feedback is hard to hear, because a correction sounds like a verdict on the whole self. Some people procrastinate not out of laziness but because starting would expose an imperfect page. Others work late, again and again, and still feel they have only barely escaped failure. In the long run, the pattern can shrink curiosity: if a new skill cannot be approached except at a professional level, fewer skills will be approached at all.

Softening perfectionism is not a call to become careless. It is a set of experiments in good enough. A student can set a timer and send the essay when it rings, then note whether the world ended. They can keep a “practice only” notebook whose only rule is that the handwriting may be messy. They can ask, before a fourth revision, “What would make this clearer, and what is only my anxiety speaking?” Sharing an early draft with a trusted person trains the nervous system to survive being seen mid-work. A teacher can grade a process, not only a shine, and can say aloud that a first version is supposed to look unfinished.

Comparison, especially online, feeds the trap, because other people’s finished highlights are mistaken for their ordinary Tuesday. A more accurate comparison is with yesterday’s own attempt. Friends can help by refusing to praise only the flawless, and by honouring a finished, honest piece of work.

Psychological growth, here, is the courage to let a real thing exist in the world before it is ideal. Perfect, as a direction, can still be useful. Perfect, as a condition of beginning or of being worthy, is a lock. The key is often smaller than it looks: one finished page, one unpolished lesson, one evening when “good and done” is allowed to count as enough.
senior.translation:
高标准可以是一种照料的形式：你修订一段文字，检查一次计算，并拒绝交上你知道是粗心的作业。当标准不再是一个向导，而变成一扇什么都不可以从中通过的门时，完美主义就开始伤害成长。一份草稿被推迟，因为它还不够无瑕。一项爱好被放弃，因为第一次尝试是笨拙的。一个人等到句子理想才开口，而谈话在没有他们的情况下继续向前。底下的感觉常常不是骄傲，而是恐惧——对可见瑕疵的恐惧，对被评判的恐惧，对仅仅普通的恐惧。心理学研究已经区分了对卓越的追求——它可以与学习共存——和一种更严厉的模式，在那种模式里，自我价值被弄得依赖于一种从不被允许仅仅是好的表现。

代价既是实际的，也是情绪的。时间被花在打磨已经足够的东西上，并从下一个问题、夜里的睡眠，或一段友谊那里被偷走。反馈很难听进去，因为一次改正听起来像是对整个自我的判决。有些人拖延，不是出于懒惰，而是因为开始会暴露一页不完美的纸。另一些人一次又一次地工作到很晚，却仍然觉得自己只是勉强逃脱了失败。从长远看，这种模式可能缩小好奇：如果一项新技能除了以专业水平接近之外就不能被接近，更少的技能会被接近。

软化完美主义，并不是一种变成粗心的号召。它是一组关于足够好的实验。一个学生可以设定一个计时器，并在它响时把文章发出去，然后注意世界是否结束了。他们可以保留一本“只练习”的笔记本，唯一的规则是字迹可以凌乱。他们可以在第四次修订之前问：“什么会让这个更清楚，而什么只是我的焦虑在说话？”与一个受信任的人分享一份早期草稿，训练神经系统在工作中途被看见时仍然存活。一位老师可以给过程打分，而不仅仅是光亮，并可以大声说，第一版本来就应该看起来未完成。

比较，尤其是线上的比较，会喂养这个陷阱，因为别人完成的高光被误认为是他们普通的星期二。一种更准确的比较，是与昨天自己的尝试相比。朋友可以通过拒绝只赞美无瑕的东西，并通过尊重一份完成的、诚实的作品来帮忙。

这里的心理成长，是让一件真实的事物在它变得理想之前就存在于世界中的勇气。完美，作为一种方向，仍然可以有用。完美，作为开始或配得上的条件，是一把锁。钥匙常常看起来比它实际更小：一页完成的纸，一堂未打磨的课，一个允许“好并且做完了”算作足够的晚上。

questions.q: 1. When do high standards begin to harm growth, according to the passage?
options: When the standard is no longer a guide and becomes a gate that nothing may pass, so that drafts are delayed, hobbies abandoned, and speech held until a sentence is ideal
When a student revises a paragraph and refuses to hand in careless work
When striving for excellence coexists with learning
When self-worth is never made to depend on a performance
questions.exp: 文中说当标准不再是向导而变成什么都过不了的门时，完美主义开始伤害成长。

questions.q: 2. What feeling often sits underneath this pattern, and how has research distinguished it?
options: Pride only, with no fear
A pattern that always coexists easily with learning
A standard that remains only a guide

Fear of a visible flaw, of being judged, or of being only ordinary; research distinguishes striving for excellence from a harsher pattern in which self-worth depends on a performance that may never be merely good
questions.exp: 文中指出底下常常是对瑕疵、被评判或仅仅普通的恐惧，并区分对卓越的追求与自我价值绑定于从不被允许仅仅是好的表现。

questions.q: 3. What practical and emotional costs does the writer name?
options: Laziness as the only cause of delay
A professional-level first attempt at every new skill, which expands curiosity

Time stolen from the next problem, sleep or friendship; feedback heard as a verdict on the self; procrastination because starting would expose an imperfect page; and, in the long run, shrunken curiosity
Feedback that is always easy to hear
questions.exp: 文中列举时间被从下一题、睡眠或友谊中偷走，反馈被听成对自我的判决，因害怕暴露不完美而拖延，以及长期来看好奇被缩小。

questions.q: 4. What experiments in ‘good enough’ can soften perfectionism without becoming careless?
options: Revise a fourth time without asking whether anxiety is speaking
Send an essay when a timer rings, keep a messy practice-only notebook, ask what would make a draft clearer versus what is only anxiety, and share an early draft with a trusted person
Let a teacher grade only shine, never process
Wait to be seen until the work is already ideal
questions.exp: 文中建议计时器响就交、保留字迹可乱的练习本、区分何使文章更清楚与何只是焦虑，以及与信任的人分享早期草稿。

questions.q: 5. What comparison is more accurate than other people’s finished highlights online?
options: A comparison with yesterday’s own attempt; friends can honour a finished honest piece, and growth here is the courage to let a real thing exist before it is ideal
A comparison only with flawless highlights, which should be mistaken for an ordinary Tuesday
Treating perfect as a condition of beginning or of being worthy
Refusing to let ‘good and done’ count as enough, even for one evening
questions.exp: 文中认为更准确的是与昨天自己的尝试相比；此处的成长是让真实事物在理想之前就存在于世界中的勇气。

senior.title: ♿ Inclusive Classrooms: When Disability Is Treated as a Design Problem
senior.content:
Fairness in education is often discussed as a matter of money, geography or gender. It is also a matter of whether a student with a disability can actually take part in the same lesson. Inclusive design begins with a simple claim: the barrier is frequently in the room, not only in the person. A class that offers information only by speech leaves out the student who cannot hear it; a test that must be completed with a pencil in a short, crowded hour may measure pain or motor difficulty rather than knowledge; a building with stairs and no lift quietly decides who belongs on the upper floor. When these obstacles are treated as personal misfortunes, the student is asked to adapt endlessly. When they are treated as design problems, the school is asked to change the path so that more than one kind of body and mind can travel it.

Good practice is specific. Materials can be available in more than one form — text, audio, large print, captions. Instructions can be written as well as spoken. Extra time, a quiet room, or a reader can be ordinary tools, not favours granted after a long fight. Technology can help, and it can also fail if it is the only plan and the only licence sits on one broken machine. Teachers need time and training, not only a poster about inclusion. Classmates need a culture in which asking for a different route is normal, and in which help is offered without pity or a public announcement of someone’s medical history. The student should be part of the planning, because they know the points where the day actually breaks.

Inclusion is not the same as placing a desk in a corner of a mainstream room and calling the work done. A student can be physically present and still be left out of the group’s thinking, or can be protected so carefully that no difficult work is ever offered. Fairness includes high expectation and the right support, together. There are real constraints — budgets, specialist staff, buildings that cannot be rebuilt in a week — and naming them is honest. What is not honest is using those constraints as a permanent reason to do nothing cheap or immediate, such as facing the class when speaking, sharing slides in advance, or choosing a ground-floor room for a course that several students must attend.

Families and students can keep a record of what works, and can ask, at a meeting, for changes that can be tested in a month. Schools can audit one week of lessons for barriers that were invisible to people who do not meet them. Educational equity, if it is to be more than a phrase, has to include the right to learn in a room that was designed with more than one kind of student in mind from the start, not only after a complaint.
senior.translation:
教育中的公平常常被讨论为金钱、地理或性别的问题。它也是一个有残障的学生是否能够真正参与同一堂课的问题。包容性设计始于一个简单的主张：障碍常常在房间里，而不仅仅在人身上。一堂只通过说话提供信息的课，会把听不到它的学生留在外面；一场必须在短而拥挤的一小时里用铅笔完成的考试，测量的可能是疼痛或动作困难，而不是知识；一座有楼梯却没有电梯的建筑，安静地决定了谁属于楼上。当这些障碍被当作个人不幸时，学生被要求无尽地适应。当它们被当作设计问题时，学校被要求改变这条路，好让多于一种身体和心智能够走它。

好的做法是具体的。材料可以用多于一种形式提供——文本、音频、大字印刷、字幕。指示可以写下来，也可以说出来。额外的时间、一间安静的房间，或一位朗读人，可以是普通的工具，而不是经过长期争取才被授予的恩惠。技术可以帮忙，如果它是唯一的计划，而唯一的许可证又放在一台坏掉的机器上，它也可能失败。老师需要时间和培训，而不仅仅是一张关于包容的海报。同学需要一种文化，在其中要求一条不同的路是正常的，帮助被提供时没有怜悯，也没有对某人病史的公开宣布。学生应当成为计划的一部分，因为他们知道一天实际在哪些点上断裂。

包容并不等于在主流房间的角落里放一张桌子，并宣布工作已经做完。一个学生可以身体上在场，却仍然被留在小组的思考之外，或被保护得如此小心，以致从来没有困难的工作被提供。公平包括高期望和正确的支持，在一起。存在真正的约束——预算，专科人员，不能在一周内重建的建筑——说出它们是诚实的。不诚实的是把那些约束当作永久什么都不做的理由，包括不做便宜或即时的事，例如说话时面向全班，提前分享幻灯片，或为一门几位学生必须参加的课选择一层的房间。

家庭和学生可以保留一份关于什么有效的记录，并可以在一次会议上要求能在一个月内被测试的改变。学校可以审查一周的课，寻找对那些没有遇到它们的人而言不可见的障碍。教育公平，如果要成为比一个短语更多的东西，就必须包括在一间从一开始就在心里装着多于一种学生、而不仅仅是在一次投诉之后才被设计的房间里学习的权利。

questions.q: 1. What simple claim does inclusive design begin with?
options: The barrier is only in the person, who must adapt endlessly
The barrier is frequently in the room, not only in the person, so a lesson only in speech, a cramped pencil test, or a building with stairs and no lift can shut someone out
Fairness in education is never a matter of disability, only of money, geography or gender
Obstacles such as stairs should be treated as personal misfortunes, not design problems
questions.exp: 文中主张障碍常常在房间里而不只在人身上，仅靠说话的课、拥挤的笔试或没有电梯的楼梯都可能把人关在外面。

questions.q: 2. Which specific practices does the writer call ordinary tools rather than favours?
options: Materials in more than one form, instructions written as well as spoken, extra time, a quiet room or a reader, plus training for teachers and a culture in which a different route is normal without pity or a public medical announcement
A poster about inclusion, with no training or time for teachers
A single licence on one broken machine as the only plan
Help that always includes a public announcement of someone’s medical history
questions.exp: 文中列举多种形式的材料、书面加口头的指示、额外时间、安静房间或朗读人，以及教师培训和不带怜悯、不公开病史的文化。

questions.q: 3. Why is placing a desk in a corner of a mainstream room not the same as inclusion?
options: Physical presence is always enough
High expectation should be withheld from disabled students
The work is done as soon as a desk is placed in a corner

A student can be physically present and still be left out of the group’s thinking, or protected so carefully that no difficult work is ever offered; fairness includes high expectation and the right support together
questions.exp: 文中指出学生可能身体在场却仍被排除在思考之外，或被保护得从不被提供困难工作；公平需要高期望与正确支持在一起。

questions.q: 4. How should real constraints such as budgets and old buildings be treated?
options: Use them as a permanent reason to do nothing cheap or immediate
Rebuild every building in a week, or else do nothing
Name them honestly, but do not use them as a permanent reason to skip cheap or immediate steps, such as facing the class when speaking, sharing slides in advance, or choosing a ground-floor room
Avoid facing the class or sharing slides, even when those steps are free
questions.exp: 文中认为应诚实说出预算和建筑等约束，但不能把它们当作永久不做便宜或即时之事的理由，例如面向全班、提前分享幻灯片或选用一层教室。

questions.q: 5. What can families and schools do so that equity is more than a phrase?
options: Wait until a complaint, and design the room only afterwards

Keep a record of what works, ask for changes that can be tested in a month, and audit a week of lessons for barriers invisible to people who do not meet them, so that rooms are designed with more than one kind of student in mind from the start
Audit nothing, because barriers are always visible to everyone
Exclude the student from planning, even though they know where the day breaks
questions.exp: 文中建议记录何有效、要求可在一个月内测试的改变，并审查一周课程中对未遇到者不可见的障碍，使房间从一开始就为多于一种学生设计。

senior.title: 🧾 Platform Work: Flexibility for Some, Precarity for Others
senior.content:
An app can now assign a meal, a ride, a delivery, or a short online task with a few taps. For some workers, this platform model is a genuine convenience: they choose hours around a class or a caring duty, start without a long hiring process, and leave a job that had felt rigid. For others, the same tools produce precarity: a thinner kind of work — pay that shifts without warning, ratings that can end access overnight, no sick leave, and an algorithm that is hard to question because no manager sits in the room. Society meets technology here in the ordinary weekday, not only in a laboratory. The design of the app is also the design of a labour market, and the rules that used to travel with a contract — a minimum wage, a rest, a way to appeal — may not automatically travel with a login.

The flexibility is real for some, and it is often advertised as if it were equally real for all. In practice, busy hours, bonuses and penalties, and the fear of being left idle can push people to stay available as if they were on a shift they cannot name. Equipment, fuel and phone data are frequently the worker’s cost. A customer’s star becomes a quiet supervisor. When a dispute arises — a late order, a damaged item, an account frozen — the path to a human decision may be a form that never answers. Some countries have begun to ask whether certain platform workers should be treated as employees for the purposes of pay and protection, or whether a third category is needed. Companies reply that a looser tie is what many users want, and that heavier rules would shrink the service. The argument is not only legal. It is about what a society is willing to call a job.

Technology can be written differently. An app can show how a fee is calculated, can offer insurance, can give a reason when access is cut, and can allow a collective voice without punishing the people who use it. Cities can require data that show waiting times and typical earnings, so that a cheerful advertisement is not the only public story. Workers can organise, even if they do not share a factory floor. Customers can tip fairly and can refuse to treat a late rider as a machine.

Students can follow one local service for a week: advertised pay, actual time, costs, and what happens if someone is ill. They can also read a single terms-of-service page and mark who holds the risk. A society that enjoys the speed of a delivery without asking who carries the insecurity is using technology as a curtain. A fairer arrangement would keep the useful flexibility and still attach responsibility to the platform that organises the work, sets the price, and profits from the tap.
senior.translation:
一个应用程序现在可以用几次轻点来分配一餐、一次乘车、一次配送，或一项简短的线上任务。对一些工作者来说，这种平台模式是一种真正的便利：他们围绕一堂课或一份照料责任选择时间，不必经过漫长的雇用过程就可以开始，并离开一份曾经显得僵硬的工作。对另一些人来说，同样的工具产生一种朝不保夕的不稳定：一种更薄的工作——没有警告就变化的报酬，可以在一夜之间结束通路的评分，没有病假，以及一种很难被质疑的算法，因为房间里没有坐着一位经理。社会在这里与科技相遇，是在普通的工作日，而不仅仅在实验室。应用程序的设计，也是一个劳动市场的设计，而曾经与一份合同一起旅行的规则——一份最低工资，一次休息，一种申诉的方式——可能不会自动与一次登录一起旅行。

对一些人来说，灵活性是真实的，而它常常被宣传得仿佛对所有人都同样真实。在实践中，繁忙的时段、奖金和惩罚，以及被留在空闲中的恐惧，可能推动人们保持待命，仿佛他们在上一班他们说不出名字的班。设备、燃料和手机流量常常是工作者的成本。顾客的一颗星变成一位安静的监督者。当争议出现时——一份迟到的订单，一件损坏的物品，一个被冻结的账户——通向一个人类决定的路，可能是一份永远不回答的表格。一些国家已经开始问，某些平台工作者是否应当在报酬和保护的意义上被当作雇员，或是否需要第三种类别。公司回答，一种更松的联系是许多用户想要的，而更重的规则会缩小这种服务。这场争论不仅仅是法律上的。它是关于一个社会愿意把什么称作一份工作。

技术可以以不同的方式被写出。一个应用程序可以显示费用如何被计算，可以提供保险，可以在通路被切断时给出理由，并可以允许一种集体的声音，而不惩罚使用它的人。城市可以要求显示等待时间和典型收入的数据，好让一则愉快的广告不是唯一的公共故事。工作者可以组织，即使他们并不共享一座工厂的地板。顾客可以公平地给小费，并可以拒绝把一位迟到的骑手当作一台机器。

学生可以跟随一项本地服务一周：被宣传的报酬，实际的时间，成本，以及如果有人生病会发生什么。他们也可以读一页服务条款，并标出谁持有风险。一个享受配送速度、却不问谁承担不安全的社会，是在把科技当作一道帘子。一种更公平的安排，会保留有用的灵活性，却仍然把责任附在那个组织工作、设定价格、并从这一次轻点中获利的平台上。

questions.q: 1. How can the same platform tools be a convenience for some and a thinner kind of work for others?
options: The rules of a contract, such as a minimum wage or a way to appeal, always travel automatically with a login
Flexibility is equally real for all, as advertisements claim
Some choose hours and start without a long hiring process, while others face shifting pay, ratings that can end access overnight, no sick leave, and an algorithm that is hard to question

options: A customer’s star never acts as a supervisor
Busy hours, bonuses and penalties, and the fear of being left idle can push people to stay available as if on an unnamed shift, while equipment, fuel and phone data are often the worker’s cost
Disputes always reach a human decision quickly
Equipment and fuel are never the worker’s cost

questions.q: 3. What legal and social question have some countries begun to ask?
options: Whether certain platform workers should be treated as employees for pay and protection, or whether a third category is needed, which is also a question of what a society is willing to call a job
Whether heavier rules would always improve a service, with no other view
Whether a looser tie is the only thing users ever want
Whether the argument is only legal and never about the name of a job

An app can show how a fee is calculated, offer insurance, give a reason when access is cut, and allow a collective voice; cities can require data on waiting times and typical earnings

questions.q: 5. What should students examine, and what would a fairer arrangement still attach to the platform?
options: The speed of a delivery only, without asking who carries the insecurity
A curtain of technology that hides the labour market

One local service for a week — advertised pay, actual time, costs, and illness — and a terms page that shows who holds the risk; responsibility should still attach to the platform that organises the work, sets the price, and profits from the tap
Flexibility with no responsibility on the platform
