senior.title: 📢 Speaking Up at Work or at School: Responsibility When Something Is Wrong
senior.content:
Most days, civic life is not a vote or a protest. It is the quieter moment when something nearby is wrong — a safety rule ignored, a classmate excluded, a number on a form that does not add up, a joke that humiliates — and a person must decide whether to speak. Speaking up is a social responsibility because silence can become a kind of permission. Harm continues, and later everyone can say they were not in charge. At the same time, speaking is not free. A student may fear being labelled a troublemaker; a worker may fear a lost shift or a lost reference. A responsible culture does not pretend that courage is costless. It tries to lower the cost and to make a clear path, so that the duty is not only a private burden on the bravest person in the room.

The skill has several parts. First, be as accurate as you can. A vague accusation is easier to dismiss and easier to regret. Notes, dates, and a calm description of what was seen are more useful than a storm of adjectives. Second, choose a channel that can actually act: a trusted teacher, a supervisor, a safety officer, a confidential line, or, when those are closed, a parent, a union or a regulator. Third, decide whether you can speak with others. A group of witnesses is harder to ignore and harder to punish, though no one should be forced to join. Fourth, look after the person who is being harmed, if there is one, rather than turning the moment only into a performance of your own virtue.

Institutions have duties of their own. A school or a workplace that has a policy on paper and a habit of punishing the messenger in practice is teaching silence. Protection against retaliation, a timely answer, and a way to appeal are part of civic infrastructure, as real as a fire exit. Not every complaint will be upheld, and a false or careless claim can itself do harm; a fair process is how a community holds both of those facts. Journalism, audits and independent offices exist because some problems cannot be solved in the room where they began.

Students can practise on a small scale: rehearsing a sentence that names a problem without insult, or agreeing in a team how a safety concern will be raised. They can also study a public case and ask who had the power to speak, who paid a price, and what rule changed afterwards. Social responsibility is sometimes described as a large feeling about society. It is also the habit of not leaving the next person alone with a fact that should have been shared. A community that practises this habit does not become noisy or harsh; it becomes harder for a quiet wrong to last simply because no one wanted to be first.
senior.translation:
在大多数日子里，公民生活并不是一次投票或一次抗议。它是当附近有什么不对时的更安静的时刻——一条被忽视的安全规则，一位被排除的同学，一张表格上对不上的数字，一个使人受辱的玩笑——而一个人必须决定是否要说出来。发声是一种社会责任，因为沉默可以变成一种许可。伤害继续，后来每个人都可以说自己并不主管。与此同时，说话并不是免费的。一个学生可能害怕被贴上惹事者的标签；一个工作者可能害怕失去一班，或失去一份推荐。一种负责任的文化并不假装勇气是没有成本的。它试图降低成本，并开辟一条清楚的路，好让这种责任不仅仅是房间里最勇敢的那个人的私人负担。

这种技能有几个部分。第一，尽可能准确。一种模糊的指责更容易被驳回，也更容易被后悔。笔记、日期，以及一段关于所看见之事的平静描述，比一阵形容词的风暴更有用。第二，选择一条实际上能够行动的渠道：一位受信任的老师，一位主管，一位安全官员，一条保密热线，或当那些被关闭时，一位家长，一个工会或一个监管者。第三，决定你是否可以与他人一起说。一群证人更难被忽视，也更难被惩罚，尽管不应当有人被强迫加入。第四，如果有正在被伤害的人，照料那个人，而不是把这一刻仅仅变成你自己美德的一场表演。

机构有它们自己的责任。一所在纸上有政策、在实践中却有惩罚报信人习惯的学校或工作场所，是在教授沉默。对报复的保护，一个及时的回答，以及一种申诉的方式，是公民基础设施的一部分，与一个消防出口一样真实。不是每一项投诉都会被支持，而一个虚假或粗心的主张本身也可能造成伤害；一个公平的过程，是一个共同体握住这两个事实的方式。新闻、审计和独立办公室的存在，是因为有些问题不能在它们开始的那个房间里被解决。

学生可以在小尺度上练习：排练一句点出问题、却不含侮辱的句子，或在一个团队里约定一项安全关切将如何被提出。他们也可以研究一个公共案例，并问谁有说话的权力，谁付出了代价，以及之后什么规则改变了。社会责任有时被描述为一种关于社会的巨大感觉。它也是一种不让下一个人独自面对一个本应被分享的事实的习惯。一个练习这种习惯的共同体并不会变得嘈杂或严厉；它只会让一种安静的错误更难仅仅因为没有人想做第一个人而持续下去。

questions.q: 1. Why does the writer call speaking up a social responsibility?
options: Because speaking is always free of cost for a student or a worker
Because civic life is mainly a vote or a protest, never a quiet nearby moment
Because a responsible culture pretends that courage is costless
Because silence can become a kind of permission, harm can continue, and later everyone can say they were not in charge
questions.exp: 文中认为发声是社会责任，因为沉默可以变成许可，伤害会继续，后来人人都可以说自己并不主管。

questions.q: 2. What should a responsible culture do about the cost of speaking?
options: Pretend that courage has no cost
Leave the duty only as a private burden on the bravest person
Admit that a student may fear a label and a worker may fear a lost shift or reference, and try to lower the cost and make a clear path so the duty is not only a private burden on the bravest person
Raise the cost, so that fewer people speak
questions.exp: 文中说负责任的文化承认勇气有成本，并努力降低成本、开辟清楚的路，而不把责任只压在最勇敢的人身上。

questions.q: 3. Which parts of the skill does the passage name?
options: Use a storm of adjectives and a vague accusation
Be accurate with notes and dates; choose a channel that can act; decide whether to speak with others; and look after the person being harmed rather than performing your own virtue
Force everyone to join a group of witnesses
Avoid teachers, supervisors, confidential lines or regulators
questions.exp: 文中列出尽可能准确、选择能行动的渠道、决定是否与他人一起说，以及照料被伤害的人而不是表演自己的美德。

questions.q: 4. What institutional duties are compared to a fire exit?
options: Protection against retaliation, a timely answer, and a way to appeal, rather than a policy on paper combined with a habit of punishing the messenger
A fair process is unnecessary, because every complaint will be upheld
False or careless claims never do harm
Journalism, audits and independent offices are useless if a problem began in a room
questions.exp: 文中把对报复的保护、及时回答和申诉途径比作消防出口一样真实的公民基础设施。

questions.q: 5. How can students practise, and what habit is social responsibility besides a large feeling?
options: Practise only insults, with no rehearsal of a calm sentence
Avoid asking who paid a price or what rule changed in a public case
Leave the next person alone with a fact that should have been shared

Rehearse a sentence that names a problem without insult, agree how a team will raise a safety concern, or study a public case; the habit is not leaving the next person alone with a fact that should have been shared
questions.exp: 文中建议排练不含侮辱的问题陈述、约定团队如何提出安全关切，或研究公共案例；这种习惯是不让下一个人独自面对本应被分享的事实。

senior.title: 🔁 Why Replication Matters: One Study Is a Beginning, Not a Verdict
senior.content:
A single study can be exciting. A result is published, a headline follows, and a classroom may treat the finding as settled. The scientific method is more cautious. Replication — repeating a study, with the same or carefully varied methods, to see whether the result appears again — is how a claim moves from interesting to reliable. One experiment can be lucky, biased, too small, or tied to a particular sample and time. If other teams, or the same team with new data, cannot obtain a similar pattern, the original result may still have been honestly reported, and yet it should not yet govern a policy or a habit. Science, at its best, is less a pile of isolated surprises than a conversation in which claims are tested until they become sturdy or until they shrink.

In recent years, researchers in several fields have found that some well-known findings are weaker, smaller, or absent when they are repeated. This “replication crisis” is not a reason to abandon science. It is a reason to practise the method more honestly. Incentives that reward only the first surprising paper, journals that prefer a clean story to a messy non-result, and statistical habits that hunt until a number looks significant can all produce a literature that is more exciting than it is solid. Better practice includes sharing data and materials, writing a plan before the results are seen, reporting negative findings, and treating a failed replication as information rather than as an insult. A result that survives these tests deserves more trust. A result that does not still teaches something about limits.

Replication is not a simple copy, and it should not be. An exact repeat can show whether the original procedure was dependable. A varied repeat — a new country, a larger sample, a slightly different measure — can show how far the claim travels. Both are part of the method. Students should learn to ask, when they meet a striking graph: Has this been repeated? By whom? With what sample? A teacher can set two short papers side by side, one original and one attempted replication, and ask the class to compare design, size and conclusion without rushing to a verdict of fraud. Most unreplicated work is not a crime. It is a first step that needed a second.

The public conversation often wants a final answer by the evening news. Responsible scientific method offers a slower gift: a claim that has been tried again, in more than one pair of hands. One study is a beginning. Replication is how a beginning becomes knowledge, or how it is returned, with thanks, to the list of ideas that did not quite hold. Students who learn to wait for that second look are not less curious; they are better prepared to live with a world in which first reports are often incomplete.
senior.translation:
一项单独的研究可以是令人兴奋的。一个结果被发表，一个标题随之而来，一间教室可能把这个发现当作已经解决。科学方法更加谨慎。重复验证——用相同或经过谨慎变化的方法重复一项研究，看结果是否再次出现——是一个主张如何从有趣走向可靠的途径。一次实验可以是幸运的、有偏差的、太小的，或与一个特定的样本和时间绑在一起的。如果其他团队，或同一个团队用新的数据，不能获得一种相似的模式，原来的结果也许仍然是被诚实报告的，却还不应当支配一项政策或一种习惯。科学在其最好的状态下，与其说是一堆孤立的惊喜，不如说是一场对话，主张在其中被测试，直到它们变得坚实，或直到它们缩小。

近年来，几个领域的研究者已经发现，一些著名的发现在被重复时更弱、更小，或不存在。这场“重复危机”并不是放弃科学的理由。它是更诚实地实践这种方法的理由。那些只奖励第一篇令人吃惊的论文的激励，那些宁愿要一个干净的故事也不要一个凌乱的无结果的期刊，以及那些一直搜寻直到一个数字看起来显著的统计习惯，都可以产生一种比它坚实的程度更令人兴奋的文献。更好的实践包括分享数据和材料，在结果被看见之前写下一份计划，报告阴性发现，并把一次失败的重复当作信息，而不是一种侮辱。一个经受住这些测试的结果，值得更多的信任。一个没有经受住的结果，仍然教给我们一些关于限度的东西。

重复验证不是一次简单的复制，它也不应当是。一次精确的重复可以显示原来的程序是否可靠。一次有变化的重复——一个新的国家，一个更大的样本，一种稍有不同的测量——可以显示这个主张走得有多远。两者都是方法的一部分。当学生遇到一幅引人注目的图时，他们应当学会问：这个被重复过吗？由谁？用什么样本？一位老师可以把两篇短论文放在一起，一篇原文，一篇试图重复的，并要求全班比较设计、规模和结论，而不急于作出欺诈的判决。大多数未被重复的工作并不是一种罪行。它是需要第二步的第一步。

公共谈话常常希望在晚间新闻之前得到一个最终答案。负责任的科学方法提供一份更慢的礼物：一个已经在多于一双手中被再次尝试的主张。一项研究是一个开始。重复验证是一个开始如何变成知识的方式，或它如何被带着感谢送回那些并不完全站得住的想法的名单。学会等待那第二次查看的学生并不是更少好奇；他们只是更好地准备好生活在一个第一批报告常常并不完整的世界里。

questions.q: 1. Why is one published study not yet a verdict, according to the passage?
options: A single experiment can be lucky, biased, too small, or tied to a particular sample, so a claim should be replicated before it governs a policy or a habit
A headline always means the finding is settled
If other teams cannot obtain a similar pattern, the original result must have been dishonest
Science is only a pile of isolated surprises, never a conversation that tests claims
questions.exp: 文中指出单次实验可能幸运、有偏差、样本太小或绑在特定样本上，因此主张在支配政策或习惯之前应当被重复验证。

questions.q: 2. What is the ‘replication crisis’ said to be a reason for, and not a reason for?
options: A reason to abandon science entirely
A reason to prefer only the first surprising paper
A reason to treat a failed replication as an insult
A reason to practise the method more honestly, not a reason to abandon science, because some well-known findings are weaker, smaller or absent when repeated
questions.exp: 文中说重复危机不是放弃科学的理由，而是更诚实地实践方法的理由。

questions.q: 3. Which habits can make a literature more exciting than it is solid, and what is better practice?
options: Hiding data and materials, and never reporting negative findings
Treating a result that fails a test as if it taught nothing about limits

Incentives that reward only the first surprise, journals that prefer a clean story to a messy non-result, and hunting until a number looks significant; better practice includes sharing data, writing a plan before results, and reporting negative findings
Writing the plan only after the results are seen
questions.exp: 文中批评只奖励首个惊喜、偏好干净故事、搜寻到显著数字的习惯；更好的做法包括分享数据、事先写计划并报告阴性发现。

questions.q: 4. How do an exact repeat and a varied repeat each help?
options: Only an exact copy is part of the method, and variation is not
An exact repeat can show whether the original procedure was dependable; a varied repeat, such as a new country or a larger sample, can show how far the claim travels
A varied repeat cannot show the range of a claim
Students should not ask whether a striking graph has been repeated, or by whom, or with what sample
questions.exp: 文中说精确重复可显示原程序是否可靠，有变化的重复可显示主张能走多远，两者都是方法的一部分。

questions.q: 5. How should a class treat an original paper and an attempted replication, and what slower gift does the method offer?
options: Compare design, size and conclusion without rushing to a verdict of fraud, since most unreplicated work is a first step, not a crime; the gift is a claim tried again in more than one pair of hands
Rush to a verdict of fraud whenever a finding was not immediately repeated
Demand a final answer by the evening news
Treat one study as knowledge, and skip the second step
questions.exp: 文中建议并排比较设计、规模和结论，不急于判为欺诈；负责任的方法提供的是在多于一双手中被再次尝试的主张。

senior.title: 🧬 Editing Genes: Promise, Line-Drawing, and Who Decides
senior.content:
For most of medical history, a harmful gene was something a family had to live with, or, at best, something doctors could work around with drugs, diet or surgery. New tools can now cut and rewrite DNA with a precision that would have sounded like fiction a generation ago. The promise is real: inherited blood disorders, some forms of blindness, and certain cancers are already the subject of careful trials. A person who is already ill may, with informed consent, accept a risk in order to treat a disease in their own body. That use raises hard questions of safety and access, and it still sits inside a familiar medical ethic: help this patient, do not pretend the tool is harmless, and do not sell a miracle ahead of the evidence.

A sharper line appears when the edit would be made in an egg, a sperm, or an early embryo, so that the change could be inherited by later generations. Supporters argue that some terrible diseases might be ended at the root, and that parents already make many genetic choices by screening. Critics answer that the long-term effects are unknown, that a mistake would travel into people who never agreed, and that the same tools could drift from treatment toward enhancement — taller, sharper, more “desirable” — in a market that would not be equally open to all. Once a society starts buying traits, equality and dignity are no longer only political words; they become questions about who may be designed, and who may be left unedited and then blamed.

Ethics in this field cannot be left only to the laboratory. It needs public argument, independent review, and laws that can say no as well as yes. Consent must be real, which is difficult when a future child cannot speak, and when a desperate family may hear only the hope in a researcher’s sentence. National borders matter too: a ban in one country is weaker if a clinic can open in another, and yet a race to the most permissive rule would be a poor way to decide the human future. International statements already exist; their force depends on whether scientists, funders and journals refuse work that crosses an agreed line.

Students can separate two questions that headlines often mix: treating a person who is already here, and changing the inheritance of people who are not. They can also ask who sits on the committees, whether patients from poorer countries are invited as partners or only as subjects, and what would count as enhancement rather than medicine. Technology will keep moving. The ethical task is to keep the line visible, to redraw it in public when the evidence changes, and to remember that a powerful tool is not yet a decision about what a human being is for.
senior.translation:
在医学史的大部分时间里，一个有害的基因是一个家庭必须与之生活的东西，或者，充其量，是医生可以用药物、饮食或手术来迂回处理的东西。新的工具现在可以以一种一代人之前听起来会像虚构的精确度，切开并改写DNA。承诺是真实的：遗传性的血液疾病，某些形式的失明，以及某些癌症，已经是谨慎试验的对象。一个已经生病的人，在知情同意下，可能为了治疗自己身体里的一种疾病而接受一种风险。那种用途提出了关于安全和可及性的困难问题，它仍然坐落在一种熟悉的医学伦理之内：帮助这位病人，不要假装这种工具是无害的，也不要在证据之前出售一个奇迹。

当编辑将在卵子、精子或早期胚胎中进行，从而使这种改变可以被后代继承时，一条更锋利的线就会出现。支持者争辩，一些可怕的疾病可能在根源上被结束，而且父母已经通过筛查做出许多遗传上的选择。批评者回答，长期效果是未知的，一个错误会进入从未同意的人身上，而且同样的工具可能从治疗滑向增强——更高，更敏锐，更“可欲”——在一个不会对所有人同样开放的市场里。一旦一个社会开始购买特质，平等和尊严就不再只是政治词语；它们变成关于谁可以被设计、谁可能被留下未经编辑然后被责备的问题。

这个领域里的伦理不能只被留给实验室。它需要公共辩论，独立审查，以及可以既说不也可以说是的法律。同意必须是真实的，当一个未来的孩子不能说话，当一个绝望的家庭可能只听到研究者句子里的希望时，这一点是困难的。国家边界也很重要：一个国家的禁令，如果一家诊所可以在另一个国家开办，就会更弱，然而一场通向最宽松规则的赛跑，会是一种决定人类未来的糟糕方式。国际声明已经存在；它们的力量取决于科学家、资助者和期刊是否拒绝越过一条约定界线的工作。

学生可以分开标题常常混合的两个问题：治疗一个已经在这里的人，以及改变还不在这里的人的遗传。他们也可以问谁坐在委员会里，来自更穷国家的病人是被当作伙伴邀请，还是只被当作对象，以及什么会被算作增强而不是医学。技术将继续移动。伦理的任务是让这条线保持可见，在证据改变时在公共中重画它，并记住，一种有力的工具还不是一个关于人类是为了什么的决定。

questions.q: 1. What familiar medical ethic still holds when a gene edit treats a person who is already ill?
options: Sell a miracle as soon as a trial begins
Help this patient, do not pretend the tool is harmless, and do not sell a miracle ahead of the evidence, even though questions of safety and access remain
Treat every use as harmless, with no need for informed consent
Ignore access, because the promise of trials is already a decision for every family

questions.q: 2. Why is a sharper ethical line drawn around edits in an egg, a sperm or an early embryo?
options: The change could be inherited by later generations who never agreed, long-term effects are unknown, and the tools could drift from treatment toward enhancement in an unequal market
Parents never make any genetic choices by screening, so no comparison exists
A mistake would stay only in one patient and could not travel
Enhancement would be equally open to all, with no risk to equality or dignity
questions.exp: 文中指出这类改变可被后代继承，长期效果未知，工具还可能从治疗滑向在不平等市场中购买特质的增强。

questions.q: 3. Why can ethics in this field not be left only to the laboratory?
options: A ban in one country is automatically strong even if a clinic opens in another
A race to the most permissive rule is a good way to decide the human future
International statements have force regardless of whether scientists, funders and journals refuse work that crosses a line
It needs public argument, independent review, and laws that can say no as well as yes, and consent is difficult when a future child cannot speak and a desperate family may hear only hope
questions.exp: 文中主张需要公共辩论、独立审查和可说不的法律；当未来孩子不能说话、绝望家庭可能只听到希望时，同意尤其困难。

questions.q: 4. What two questions should students separate when headlines mix them?
options: Who sits on a committee, and nothing else
Whether poorer patients should only be subjects, never partners
Treating a person who is already here, and changing the inheritance of people who are not
Whether enhancement and medicine are already the same thing

questions.q: 5. What remains the ethical task as the technology keeps moving?
options: Let the laboratory alone redraw the line in private
Keep the line visible, redraw it in public when the evidence changes, and remember that a powerful tool is not yet a decision about what a human being is for
Treat a powerful tool as already a decision about what a human being is for
Stop asking who is invited as a partner and what would count as enhancement
questions.exp: 文中说伦理任务是让这条线保持可见，在证据改变时公开重画，并记住有力的工具还不是关于人类是为了什么的决定。

senior.title: 😴 Sleep and Memory: Why the Night Continues the Day’s Learning
senior.content:
A student who cuts the night short in order to revise can feel virtuous and still be working against the brain. Cognitive science has shown, in many careful studies, that sleep is not a blank pause between lessons. It is a period in which the brain continues to process what was practised or read during the day. Memories are not stored once and for all at the desk. They are reactivated and reorganised during sleep, especially during stretches of deep sleep and of rapid eye movement, in ways that can make a skill more stable and a set of facts easier to retrieve later. A short night after a first encounter with material can leave the memory more fragile, even if the hours of reading looked impressive in a diary.

The laboratory picture is gradually becoming clearer, though it is not a single simple switch. In the hours after learning, the brain appears to replay recent patterns, strengthen useful connections, and, in some cases, weaken noise. Sleep also supports the kind of insight that arrives after a problem has been put down: a structure that was not obvious in the afternoon can feel available in the morning, not by magic, but because overnight work has changed the way pieces sit together. Tiredness, by contrast, harms attention the next day, so that new encoding is poorer, and the cycle of weak learning and weak sleep can feed itself. Caffeine can postpone sleepiness; it does not do the overnight work for you.

This research does not say that sleep replaces study. A night cannot invent a chapter that was never opened, and anxiety about “perfect sleep” can itself become a new obstacle. The practical lesson is more modest and more useful: protect a regular window for sleep as part of the study plan, avoid a long session that ends only when the exam begins, and, when possible, leave a first pass at new material earlier in the evening so that the night has something to work on. A brief review the next day then meets a memory that has already been rehearsed in the dark. Naps can help in some designs, and they are not a complete substitute for a full night, especially for teenagers whose clocks already run late and whose schools often start early.

Students can treat a week as a small experiment: the same kind of practice on two days, one followed by a short night and one by a fuller one, and a fair test of what remains. They can also notice how often a “I knew this yesterday” failure is a sleep story as well as a study story. Cognitive science, here, is not an excuse to romanticise rest. It is evidence that the desk and the bed are partners in the same system of learning, and that a culture which praises only the lamp at midnight may be praising a habit that throws some of the day’s work away.
senior.translation:
一个为了复习而截短夜晚的学生，可能感觉自己有美德，却仍然在与大脑作对。认知科学已经在许多谨慎的研究中显示，睡眠并不是课程之间的一段空白暂停。它是一个大脑继续处理白天被练习或被阅读的内容的时期。记忆并不是在桌边被一劳永逸地储存的。它们在睡眠中被重新激活和重新组织，尤其是在深睡眠和快速眼动的时段里，其方式可以使一项技能更稳定，使一组事实稍后更容易被提取。在与材料的第一次相遇之后一个短的夜晚，可能使记忆更脆弱，即使阅读的小时在日记里看起来令人印象深刻。

实验室的图景正在逐渐变得更清楚，尽管它不是一个单一的简单开关。在学习之后的几小时里，大脑似乎重放最近的模式，加强有用的连接，并在某些情况下减弱噪声。睡眠也支持那种在一个问题被放下之后到来的洞见：一种在下午并不明显的结构，在早晨可能感觉是可获得的，不是靠魔法，而是因为夜间的工作已经改变了各部分坐在一起的方式。相反，疲倦会损害第二天的注意，以致新的编码更差，而弱学习和弱睡眠的循环可以自我喂养。咖啡因可以推迟困倦；它并不会为你做夜间的工作。

这项研究并不是说睡眠可以代替学习。一个夜晚不能发明一章从未被打开的内容，而对“完美睡眠”的焦虑本身也可能变成一个新的障碍。实际的教训更谦逊，也更有用：把一个规律的睡眠窗口当作学习计划的一部分来保护，避免一场只在考试开始时才结束的长时段，并且在可能时，把对新材料的第一次通过留在傍晚更早的时候，好让夜晚有东西可以处理。第二天一次简短的复习，然后会遇到一份已经在黑暗中被排练过的记忆。小睡在某些设计里可以帮忙，它们并不是对完整一夜的完全替代，尤其是对那些生物钟已经偏晚、而学校又常常很早开始的青少年而言。

学生可以把一周当作一个小实验：在两天里进行同一种练习，一天之后是一个短夜，一天之后是一个更完整的夜，再公平地测试留下了什么。他们也可以注意到，一次“我昨天还知道这个”的失败，常常既是一个睡眠故事，也是一个学习故事。认知科学在这里，并不是一个把休息浪漫化的借口。它是一种证据：桌子和床是同一套学习系统中的伙伴，而一种只赞美午夜灯火的文化，可能正在赞美一种把白天的一部分工作扔掉的习惯。

questions.q: 1. Why is sleep not a blank pause between lessons, according to cognitive science in this passage?
options: Memories are stored once and for all at the desk, and the night adds nothing
A short night after a first encounter always makes a memory more stable

The brain continues to process what was practised or read, reactivating and reorganising memories, especially in deep sleep and rapid eye movement, so that a skill can become more stable and facts easier to retrieve
Hours of reading in a diary already prove that the memory is not fragile
questions.exp: 文中指出睡眠期间大脑继续处理白天所学，记忆被重新激活和重组，尤其在深睡眠和快速眼动阶段，技能可更稳定，事实更易提取。

questions.q: 2. What appears to happen in the hours after learning, and how can insight arrive in the morning?
options: Insight arrives only by magic, with no overnight change

The brain appears to replay recent patterns, strengthen useful connections and sometimes weaken noise, so a structure that was not obvious in the afternoon can feel available after overnight work has changed how pieces sit together
Tiredness improves attention the next day and makes new encoding stronger
Caffeine does the overnight work of replay and strengthening
questions.exp: 文中说学习后几小时大脑似乎重放近期模式、加强有用连接，有时减弱噪声；早晨的洞见是因为夜间工作改变了各部分的组合方式。

questions.q: 3. Why can a cycle of weak learning and weak sleep feed itself?
options: Tiredness harms attention the next day, so that new encoding is poorer
A short night always improves the next day’s encoding
Caffeine completes the overnight work and breaks the cycle automatically
Attention is never harmed by tiredness
questions.exp: 文中指出疲倦会损害第二天的注意，使新的编码更差，弱学习与弱睡眠可以循环加强。

questions.q: 4. What modest practical lesson does the research support, without saying that sleep replaces study?
options: Replace all study with sleep, and invent unopened chapters overnight
Treat anxiety about perfect sleep as harmless
Treat naps as a complete substitute for a full night, especially for teenagers

Protect a regular sleep window as part of the plan, avoid a session that ends only when the exam begins, leave a first pass earlier in the evening when possible, and use a brief review the next day; a night cannot invent a chapter that was never opened
questions.exp: 文中说睡眠不能代替未打开的章节，实际教训是保护规律睡眠窗口，避免熬到开考，尽量把初读留在傍晚更早，次日再做简短复习。

questions.q: 5. What small experiment can students run, and what does the writer say a culture that praises only the midnight lamp may be doing?
options: Romanticise rest as an excuse to abandon the desk
Treat the desk and the bed as enemies, never as partners in the same system

Compare the same practice after a short night and a fuller one, and notice that a ‘I knew this yesterday’ failure can be a sleep story as well as a study story; such a culture may be praising a habit that throws some of the day’s work away
Ignore sleep stories and count only the lamp at midnight as virtue
questions.exp: 文中建议比较短夜与更完整的夜之后留下的记忆，并指出只赞美午夜灯火的文化可能在赞美一种把白天部分工作扔掉的习惯。
